concepts.formula: annual retention = (1 - monthly churn)^12

concepts.name: Net revenue retention
concepts.def: Recurring revenue from a cohort of customers a year later, including upsells and minus downgrades and churn, divided by its starting revenue. Gross revenue retention excludes expansion and caps at one hundred percent.
concepts.formula: NRR = (start ARR + expansion - contraction - churn) / start ARR

concepts.name: Average revenue per user
concepts.def: Revenue in a period divided by average users or subscribers. Changes come from pricing, mix and upsell; widely used in telecom, media and consumer internet.
concepts.formula: ARPU = revenue / average users

concepts.name: Annual recurring revenue
concepts.def: The annualized value of recurring subscription contracts at a point in time, a non-GAAP metric whose definitions vary. Monthly recurring revenue (MRR) times twelve for monthly plans.
concepts.formula: ARR = MRR x 12

concepts.name: SaaS magic number
concepts.def: New annualized recurring revenue from a quarter divided by the prior quarter's sales and marketing spend. A sales efficiency gauge; above about one suggests spending should rise.
concepts.formula: magic number = (quarterly revenue change x 4) / prior quarter S&M

concepts.name: Burn multiple
concepts.def: Net cash burned divided by net new ARR in the same period, popularized by David Sacks. Lower means growth is bought more efficiently.
concepts.formula: burn multiple = net burn / net new ARR

concepts.name: Land and expand
concepts.def: A go-to-market approach that wins a small initial deployment, then grows revenue within the account through more seats, products or usage. Its success shows up in net revenue retention.

concepts.name: Usage-based pricing
concepts.def: Charging by consumption, such as compute, transactions or data, rather than by seat. Aligns price with value and speeds expansion, but makes revenue more cyclical and harder to forecast.
concepts.aliases: consumption pricing,pay as you go,usage pricing,seat based pricing

concepts.name: Customer concentration
concepts.def: Dependence on a few large customers for a big share of revenue, disclosed in filings when any one exceeds ten percent. Raises buyer power and the risk of sudden revenue loss.
concepts.aliases: key customer risk,10 percent customers,top customer concentration

concepts.name: Gross merchandise value
concepts.def: Total value of transactions on a marketplace before fees, returns or cancellations. Not revenue; the company earns only its take of GMV.
concepts.formula: revenue = GMV x take rate

concepts.name: Take rate
concepts.def: Marketplace revenue as a percentage of GMV. Rises with marketplace power and ancillary services like ads and payments, but too high a rate pushes participants to transact elsewhere.
concepts.formula: take rate = net revenue / GMV

concepts.name: Disintermediation
concepts.def: Buyers and sellers who meet through a marketplace or intermediary transacting directly to avoid its fees. Most acute where matches repeat, such as services; platforms counter with payments, insurance and reviews.

concepts.name: Two-sided market
concepts.def: A platform serving two user groups whose value to each other rises with the size of the other side, such as buyers and sellers. Pricing often subsidizes one side to attract the other.
concepts.aliases: two sided platform,multi sided market,marketplace,platform business

concepts.name: Marketplace liquidity
concepts.def: The probability that a listing sells or a search finds a match within a reasonable time. Once local liquidity is reached, network effects take over; it is often achieved city by city or category by category.
concepts.aliases: match rate,sell through rate,fill rate marketplace

concepts.name: Fabless model
concepts.def: Semiconductor companies that design chips but outsource manufacturing to foundries. Asset-light with high gross margins, but dependent on foundry capacity and pricing.

concepts.name: Foundry
concepts.def: A contract chip manufacturer that produces wafers for other companies' designs. Leading-edge foundry capacity is concentrated and enormously capital intensive.

concepts.name: Integrated device manufacturer
concepts.def: A semiconductor firm that both designs and fabricates its chips. Controls its process but carries fab utilization risk and very high capital needs.

concepts.name: Process node
concepts.def: A semiconductor manufacturing generation, named in nanometers that no longer map to physical feature size. Newer nodes give more transistors per area and better power efficiency at much higher wafer cost.

concepts.name: Moore's law
concepts.def: Gordon Moore's (1965, revised 1975) observation that transistors per chip double about every two years. Its slowing has shifted gains toward packaging, specialized chips and architecture.

concepts.name: Wafer fab equipment
concepts.def: Tools used to make chips, such as lithography, deposition, etch and inspection. Spending on it tracks chipmakers' capex and is among the most cyclical parts of the semiconductor industry.

concepts.name: Design win
concepts.def: A chip supplier's component being selected for a customer's product design. Revenue follows with a lag of a year or more and lasts for the product's life, so wins are a leading indicator.

concepts.name: Content per unit
concepts.def: Dollar value of a supplier's products in each end unit, such as semiconductor content per car or phone. Growth in content can drive revenue even when end-unit volumes are flat.
concepts.formula: revenue = units x content per unit x share

concepts.name: Average selling price
concepts.def: Revenue divided by units sold. Watched in semiconductors, memory, devices and housing, where pricing swings drive margins more than volume.
concepts.formula: ASP = revenue / units

concepts.name: Net interest margin
concepts.def: Net interest income, interest earned less interest paid, divided by average earning assets. The core profitability gauge for lenders; driven by rates, curve shape, deposit costs and asset mix.
concepts.formula: NIM = net interest income / average earning assets

concepts.name: Deposit beta
concepts.def: The share of a policy rate change that a bank passes through to deposit rates. Low betas widen margins as rates rise; betas tend to climb the longer rates stay high.
concepts.formula: deposit beta = change in deposit rate / change in policy rate

concepts.name: Efficiency ratio
concepts.def: A bank's non-interest expenses divided by revenue, net interest income plus fees. Lower is better; it measures the cost of generating each unit of revenue.
concepts.formula: efficiency ratio = noninterest expense / (NII + noninterest income)
concepts.aliases: cost income ratio,efficiency ratio,cost to income

concepts.name: Pre-provision net revenue
concepts.def: A bank's revenue minus operating expenses before credit loss provisions and taxes. Shows earnings power available to absorb loan losses through a cycle.
concepts.formula: PPNR = NII + fee income - noninterest expense

concepts.name: Provision for credit losses
concepts.def: The income statement charge that builds a lender's loss allowance. Under CECL it reflects expected lifetime losses, so provisions jump early when the outlook worsens.
concepts.formula: ending allowance = beginning allowance + provision - net charge-offs

concepts.name: CECL
concepts.def: Current expected credit loss model, the US standard requiring lenders to reserve for expected lifetime losses at origination. IFRS 9 uses a staged expected loss model instead.
concepts.aliases: cecl,current expected credit loss,ifrs 9 ecl,expected credit loss

concepts.name: Net charge-offs
concepts.def: Loans written off as uncollectible minus recoveries, usually expressed as an annualized percentage of average loans. The realized credit loss that reserves are meant to cover.
concepts.formula: NCO ratio = (charge-offs - recoveries) / average loans

concepts.name: Risk-weighted assets
concepts.def: A bank's assets scaled by regulatory risk weights, so safer assets like government bonds count less than corporate loans. The denominator of capital ratios.

concepts.name: CET1 ratio
concepts.def: Common equity tier 1 capital divided by risk-weighted assets, the main measure of bank solvency under the Basel III rules. Capital above regulatory minimums and buffers is available for buybacks and growth.
concepts.formula: CET1 ratio = CET1 capital / RWA

concepts.name: Return on tangible common equity
concepts.def: Net income to common shareholders divided by average tangible common equity. The bank profitability measure most tied to price to tangible book.
concepts.formula: ROTCE = net income to common / average TCE

concepts.name: Uninsured deposits
concepts.def: Bank deposits above the deposit insurance limit. They are the most flight-prone funding, so a high share raises run risk when confidence falls.

concepts.name: Combined ratio
concepts.def: A property and casualty insurer's losses plus expenses divided by earned premium. Below one hundred percent means an underwriting profit before investment income.
concepts.formula: combined ratio = loss ratio + expense ratio

concepts.name: Loss ratio
concepts.def: Claims and claim adjustment expenses divided by earned premium. Reported on a calendar year basis, which mixes current claims with changes to prior-year reserves.
concepts.formula: loss ratio = incurred losses / earned premium

concepts.name: Insurance float
concepts.def: Premiums collected but not yet paid out as claims, which an insurer invests meanwhile. If underwriting is profitable, float is funding with a negative cost, a core point in Buffett's approach.
concepts.formula: cost of float = underwriting loss / average float

concepts.name: Loss reserves
concepts.def: An insurer's estimate of claims owed but not yet paid, including incurred but not reported claims. The largest liability and the largest source of judgment in insurer earnings.
concepts.aliases: claims reserves,loss and lae reserves,technical provisions

concepts.name: IBNR
concepts.def: Incurred but not reported: reserves for claims that have happened but have not yet been reported. Estimated actuarially, often with chain-ladder methods, and especially uncertain in long-tail lines.

concepts.name: Reserve development
concepts.def: Changes to prior-year loss reserve estimates. Favorable development releases profit, adverse development hurts it; a long run of adverse development signals underreserving.

concepts.name: Embedded value
concepts.def: A life insurer's adjusted net assets plus the present value of future profits on existing policies, less the cost of required capital. Excludes value from future new business.
concepts.formula: EV = adjusted net assets + value of in-force business
concepts.aliases: mcev,market consistent embedded value,life insurer embedded value

concepts.name: REIT
concepts.def: A real estate investment trust: a company owning or financing property that avoids corporate tax by distributing most taxable income, at least ninety percent in the US. Valued on FFO, AFFO and NAV.

concepts.name: Funds from operations
concepts.def: The standard REIT earnings measure defined by Nareit: net income plus real estate depreciation, excluding gains or losses on property sales and impairments.
concepts.formula: FFO = net income + real estate D&A - gains on property sales

concepts.name: Adjusted funds from operations
concepts.def: FFO less recurring capital expenditures, leasing costs and straight-line rent adjustments. Closer to distributable cash flow but defined differently by each REIT.
concepts.formula: AFFO = FFO - recurring capex - straight-line rent adjustment

concepts.name: Net operating income
concepts.def: Property rental revenue minus property-level operating expenses, before interest, depreciation and corporate overhead. Divided by the cap rate it gives a direct estimate of property value.
concepts.formula: NOI = rental income - property operating expenses

concepts.name: Capitalization rate
concepts.def: A property's net operating income divided by its value or price, the real estate analogue of an earnings yield. Cap rates rise with interest rates and perceived risk.
concepts.formula: cap rate = NOI / property value

concepts.name: Same-store NOI
concepts.def: NOI growth from properties owned in both periods, excluding acquisitions and developments. The organic growth measure for REITs, driven by rent and occupancy changes.
concepts.aliases: same property noi,ss noi,like for like noi

concepts.name: Triple net lease
concepts.def: A lease in which the tenant pays property taxes, insurance and maintenance on top of rent. Gives landlords bond-like cash flows tied to tenant credit and lease length.

concepts.name: Upstream, midstream and downstream
concepts.def: The oil and gas value chain: exploration and production, then transport, storage and processing, then refining and marketing. Each segment has different commodity exposure and valuation methods.

concepts.name: Proved reserves
concepts.def: Oil and gas quantities that are reasonably certain to be recoverable under existing economic and operating conditions, disclosed under SEC rules. Probable and possible reserves add less certain volumes.

concepts.name: PV-10
concepts.def: The present value of future pre-tax net cash flows from proved reserves, discounted at ten percent using SEC prices. A standardized but rough benchmark for producer asset value.

concepts.name: Barrel of oil equivalent
concepts.def: A unit combining oil and gas volumes by energy content, usually six thousand cubic feet of gas per barrel. Price differences between oil and gas mean a boe of gas is usually worth far less.
concepts.formula: 1 boe ~ 6 mcf natural gas

concepts.name: Reserve replacement ratio
concepts.def: Reserves added in a year divided by production. Below one hundred percent for long means the producer is liquidating itself.
concepts.formula: RRR = reserve additions / production

concepts.name: Finding and development cost
concepts.def: Capital spent on exploration and development divided by reserves added, per boe. Compared with the margin per boe, it shows whether reinvestment creates value.
concepts.formula: F&D = exploration and development capex / reserve additions

concepts.name: Breakeven oil price
concepts.def: The oil price at which a well, producer or budget covers its costs. Definitions vary from wellhead breakeven to the price that funds capex and dividends from cash flow.
concepts.aliases: breakeven,full cycle breakeven,fiscal breakeven,free cash flow breakeven

concepts.name: Producer hedging
concepts.def: Producers selling forward or buying puts and collars on future output to lock in prices and protect cash flow and debt service. Hedge books shape how much a price move reaches earnings.

concepts.name: Patent cliff
concepts.def: The sharp drop in a drug's sales when its patent protection expires and generics or biosimilars enter. Pharmaceutical valuations depend on the timing of exclusivity loss and pipeline replacement.

concepts.name: Aftermarket revenue
concepts.def: Recurring sales of parts, service and upgrades to an installed base of equipment, usually at higher margins and with steadier demand than original equipment sales.

concepts.name: Derivative
concepts.def: A contract whose value depends on the price of an underlying asset, rate, index or event. Main families are forwards, futures, options and swaps, used to hedge, speculate or arbitrage.

concepts.name: Underlying asset
concepts.def: The security, index, rate or commodity whose price determines a derivative's payoff. Its price, volatility and carry drive the derivative's value.

concepts.name: Notional value
concepts.def: The face amount on which a derivative's payments are calculated. For swaps it is rarely exchanged; for futures and options it equals contract size times price and measures economic exposure, not money at risk.
concepts.formula: Notional = contract size x multiplier x underlying price

concepts.name: Delta
concepts.def: Sensitivity of an option's price to a one unit change in the underlying price. Ranges 0 to 1 for calls and -1 to 0 for puts; also read loosely as a hedge ratio and rough probability of finishing in the money.
concepts.formula: Delta = dV/dS; Black-Scholes call delta = N(d1)

concepts.name: Gamma
concepts.def: Rate of change of delta for a one unit move in the underlying. Highest for at-the-money options near expiry; long options are long gamma and gain from large moves in either direction.
concepts.formula: Gamma = d2V/dS2 = N'(d1) / (S x sigma x sqrt(T))

concepts.name: Vega
concepts.def: Change in an option's value for a one volatility point change in implied volatility. Largest for at-the-money, longer dated options; long options are long vega.
concepts.formula: Vega = dV/dsigma = S x N'(d1) x sqrt(T)

concepts.name: Theta
concepts.def: Change in an option's value as one day passes, holding other inputs fixed. Long options usually have negative theta, the cost of holding gamma; time decay accelerates near expiry for at-the-money options.

concepts.name: Rho
concepts.def: Sensitivity of an option's value to a change in the risk-free interest rate. Calls gain and puts lose as rates rise; rho matters most for long dated options.

concepts.name: Vanna
concepts.def: Second order greek measuring how delta changes with implied volatility, equivalently how vega changes with spot. Important for dealer hedging flows when volatility moves with the market.
concepts.formula: Vanna = d2V / dS dsigma

concepts.name: Volga
concepts.def: Second order greek measuring how vega changes with implied volatility, the convexity of option value in volatility. Out-of-the-money wings carry high volga, which is why they are priced with a smile.
concepts.formula: Volga = d2V / dsigma2

concepts.name: Charm
concepts.def: Rate at which an option's delta changes as time passes, holding spot fixed. Explains why delta hedges drift overnight and why dealer hedging flows build into expiry.
concepts.formula: Charm = d2V / dS dt

concepts.name: Speed
concepts.def: Third order greek measuring how gamma changes with the underlying price. Used by desks to see how gamma exposure will shift after a large spot move.
concepts.formula: Speed = d3V / dS3

concepts.name: Dollar delta
concepts.def: Delta expressed as the equivalent dollar position in the underlying, so exposures across strikes and assets can be added. A dollar delta of 1 million gains about 10,000 on a 1 percent rally.
concepts.formula: Dollar delta = delta x contracts x multiplier x S

concepts.name: Dollar gamma
concepts.def: Gamma expressed as the change in dollar delta for a 1 percent move in the underlying. Lets traders compare convexity across underlyings of different prices.
concepts.formula: Dollar gamma (per 1%) = gamma x S^2 x 0.01 x multiplier

concepts.name: Delta hedging
concepts.def: Trading the underlying to offset an option position's delta so the combined book is insensitive to small price moves. Re-hedging as delta changes turns option P&L into a bet on realized versus implied volatility.

concepts.name: Delta neutral
concepts.def: A position whose net delta is zero, so small moves in the underlying leave its value roughly unchanged. Remaining exposure is to gamma, vega and theta.

concepts.name: Gamma scalping
concepts.def: Running a long option position and repeatedly delta hedging, selling into rallies and buying dips. It earns money if realized volatility exceeds the implied volatility paid, offset by theta.

concepts.name: Gamma P&L
concepts.def: Profit of a delta hedged option over a short period, driven by the gap between realized and implied variance scaled by dollar gamma. It is the core identity of volatility trading.
concepts.formula: P&L per step = 0.5 x gamma x S^2 x (realized variance - implied variance) x dt

concepts.name: Gamma-theta tradeoff
concepts.def: Under Black-Scholes, a delta hedged option's theta and gamma offset, so being long convexity costs time decay. Breakeven daily move equals implied volatility divided by roughly 16.
concepts.formula: Theta approx = -0.5 x gamma x S^2 x sigma^2 (ignoring rates)

concepts.name: Long gamma
concepts.def: Positions with positive convexity, such as owned options, whose delta moves in the trader's favor as price moves. They profit from large moves and pay theta.

concepts.name: Short gamma
concepts.def: Positions with negative convexity, such as sold options, that lose from large moves and earn theta in calm markets. Hedging requires buying high and selling low, which can amplify moves.

concepts.name: Moneyness
concepts.def: Where an option's strike sits relative to the underlying or forward price. Expressed as in, at or out of the money, as strike over spot, log moneyness, or as delta.
concepts.formula: Log moneyness = ln(K / F)

concepts.name: At the money
concepts.def: An option whose strike equals or is close to the current underlying or forward price. It has the most time value, highest gamma near expiry and a delta near 0.5 in absolute value.

concepts.name: In the money
concepts.def: A call with strike below spot or a put with strike above spot, so it has positive intrinsic value. Deep in-the-money options behave much like the underlying.

concepts.name: Out of the money
concepts.def: A call with strike above spot or a put with strike below spot, so intrinsic value is zero and the premium is all time value. Cheap in dollars but expire worthless most of the time.

concepts.name: Option intrinsic value
concepts.def: The value an option would have if exercised now: spot minus strike for a call and strike minus spot for a put, floored at zero.
concepts.formula: Call intrinsic = max(S - K, 0); put intrinsic = max(K - S, 0)

concepts.name: Option time value
concepts.def: The part of an option's premium above intrinsic value, reflecting the chance of a favorable move before expiry. It decays to zero at expiration.
concepts.formula: Time value = premium - intrinsic value

concepts.name: Option premium
concepts.def: The price paid by the buyer to the writer of an option, equal to intrinsic plus time value. It is the buyer's maximum loss and the writer's maximum gain.

concepts.name: Strike price
concepts.def: The fixed price at which an option holder may buy (call) or sell (put) the underlying. Listed strikes follow exchange-set intervals.

concepts.name: Option expiration
concepts.def: The date after which an option can no longer be exercised. Listed equity options generally expire on Fridays, with daily and weekly expiries on major indices and ETFs.

concepts.name: American option
concepts.def: An option that can be exercised any time up to expiry. Most single stock listed options are American; early exercise can be optimal for deep in-the-money calls before dividends and deep in-the-money puts.

concepts.name: European option
concepts.def: An option exercisable only at expiry. Most index options such as SPX are European and cash settled, and Black-Scholes prices them in closed form.

concepts.name: Bermudan option
concepts.def: An option exercisable on a set of discrete dates before expiry, between European and American. Bermudan swaptions embedded in callable bonds are the main example.

concepts.name: Early exercise
concepts.def: Exercising an American option before expiry. Rarely optimal for calls except just before a dividend that exceeds remaining time value, and sometimes optimal for deep in-the-money puts when rates are positive.

concepts.name: Assignment
concepts.def: The obligation placed on an option writer when a holder exercises, delivering or receiving the underlying at the strike. The clearing house allocates exercises to short positions, often randomly.

concepts.name: Pin risk
concepts.def: Uncertainty for an option writer when the underlying closes near the strike at expiry, so it is unclear whether short options will be assigned. The trader may wake up with an unwanted stock position.

concepts.name: Open interest
concepts.def: The number of futures or options contracts outstanding that have not been closed, exercised or delivered. Rising open interest with price signals new positions; it differs from daily volume.

concepts.name: Option chain
concepts.def: A table of all listed calls and puts on an underlying, by expiry and strike, showing bid, ask, volume, open interest, implied volatility and greeks.

concepts.name: Contract multiplier
concepts.def: The number of units of the underlying controlled by one derivative contract. US equity options use 100 shares; futures multipliers are set per contract.

concepts.name: Cash settlement
concepts.def: Settling a derivative by paying the difference between the final reference price and the contract price, with no delivery of the underlying. Used for index options, VIX products and many futures.

concepts.name: Physical delivery
concepts.def: Settling a derivative by delivering the actual underlying, such as shares, bonds or barrels, against payment. Creates delivery logistics and squeezes that cash settled contracts avoid.

concepts.name: Option pricing model
concepts.def: Any framework that values options from assumptions about the underlying's dynamics and no-arbitrage. Ranges from closed form models like Black-Scholes to trees, PDE solvers and Monte Carlo.

concepts.name: d1 and d2
concepts.def: The two standardized terms in the Black-Scholes formula. N(d1) is the call's delta; N(d2) is the risk-neutral probability the call finishes in the money.
concepts.formula: d1 = [ln(S/K) + (r - q + 0.5 sigma^2) T] / (sigma sqrt T); d2 = d1 - sigma sqrt T

concepts.name: Probability in the money
concepts.def: The risk-neutral probability that an option expires in the money, N(d2) for a call under Black-Scholes. It differs from real-world probability by the risk premium.
concepts.formula: Call P(ITM) = N(d2); put P(ITM) = N(-d2)

concepts.name: Binomial tree
concepts.def: A lattice model that splits each time step into an up or down move with risk-neutral probabilities and values options by backward induction. Cox, Ross and Rubinstein (1979); handles American exercise naturally.
concepts.formula: p = (e^(r dt) - d) / (u - d), u = e^(sigma sqrt dt), d = 1/u

concepts.name: Finite difference method
concepts.def: Numerical solution of an option pricing PDE on a grid of price and time. Explicit, implicit and Crank-Nicolson schemes trade off stability and accuracy; well suited to American and barrier options.

concepts.name: Least squares Monte Carlo
concepts.def: Longstaff and Schwartz (2001) method for pricing American and Bermudan options by simulation, regressing continuation values on state variables to decide exercise at each date.

concepts.name: Risk-neutral pricing
concepts.def: Valuing a derivative as the expected payoff under a probability measure where all assets earn the risk-free rate, discounted at that rate. Valid because the payoff can be hedged, so risk preferences drop out.
concepts.formula: V0 = e^(-rT) x E_Q[payoff]

concepts.name: Risk-neutral measure
concepts.def: The probability measure Q under which discounted asset prices are martingales. Implied from option prices, it overweights bad states relative to real-world probabilities because investors pay to insure them.

concepts.name: No-arbitrage pricing
concepts.def: Setting a derivative's price so that no combination of it with traded assets yields a riskless profit. Foundation of forwards, put-call parity and option models; the fundamental theorem links it to a risk-neutral measure.

concepts.name: Replicating portfolio
concepts.def: A portfolio of the underlying and cash, rebalanced over time, that reproduces a derivative's payoff. Its cost is the derivative's arbitrage-free price.

concepts.name: Dynamic replication
concepts.def: Continuously rebalancing a hedge to reproduce an option's payoff, as in Black-Scholes. In practice discrete rebalancing, costs and jumps leave hedging error.

concepts.name: Static replication
concepts.def: Reproducing a payoff with a fixed portfolio of vanilla options set up once, with no ongoing trading. Used for variance swaps, barriers via put-call symmetry and other exotics.

concepts.name: Geometric Brownian motion
concepts.def: Continuous-time process in which log returns are normally distributed with constant drift and volatility, so prices are lognormal and stay positive. The price assumption behind Black-Scholes.
concepts.formula: dS = mu S dt + sigma S dW

concepts.name: Local volatility
concepts.def: Model in which volatility is a deterministic function of spot and time, calibrated to match every vanilla price on the surface. Dupire (1994) gave the formula; it tends to misprice forward skew.
concepts.formula: Dupire: sigma_loc^2 = (dC/dT) / (0.5 K^2 d2C/dK2), zero rates

concepts.name: Stochastic volatility
concepts.def: Class of models in which volatility follows its own random process, usually correlated with the underlying. Generates smiles and realistic forward skew dynamics.

concepts.name: Heston model
concepts.def: Heston (1993) stochastic volatility model where variance mean reverts with a square-root process correlated with spot. Has a semi-closed form for European options, making calibration fast.
concepts.formula: dv = kappa (theta - v) dt + xi sqrt(v) dW2, corr(dW1, dW2) = rho

concepts.name: Jump diffusion
concepts.def: Model adding random jumps to a diffusion, as in Merton (1976). Jumps fatten tails and steepen short-dated skew, which pure diffusions cannot reproduce.

concepts.name: Garman-Kohlhagen model
concepts.def: Garman and Kohlhagen (1983) extension of Black-Scholes to FX options, treating the foreign interest rate as a continuous dividend yield.

concepts.name: FX option
concepts.def: An option to exchange one currency for another at a set rate. Traded mostly OTC and quoted in volatility by delta, through ATM, risk reversals and butterflies.

concepts.name: Volatility surface
concepts.def: Implied volatility plotted across strike (or delta) and expiry. Its shape, the smile or skew per expiry and the term structure across expiries, encodes the market's risk-neutral distribution.
concepts.formula: sigma_implied = f(K, T)

concepts.name: Volatility smile
concepts.def: Pattern where implied volatility rises for strikes away from the money, typical of FX and single stocks around events. It shows the market prices fatter tails than the lognormal model.

concepts.name: Volatility term structure
concepts.def: Implied volatility across expiries at a fixed moneyness. Usually upward sloping in calm markets and inverted in stress, when near-term vol spikes above longer-dated vol.
concepts.aliases: vol term structure,term structure of volatility,iv term structure

concepts.name: ATM volatility
concepts.def: Implied volatility of the at-the-money option for a given expiry. It is the headline level of the surface and the anchor for skew and term structure quotes.
concepts.aliases: atm vol,at the money vol,atmf vol

concepts.name: Forward volatility
concepts.def: Implied volatility for a future period between two expiries, backed out from the term structure. Used to judge whether a later window is cheap or rich.
concepts.formula: Forward variance = (sigma2^2 T2 - sigma1^2 T1) / (T2 - T1)

concepts.name: Forward variance
concepts.def: Expected variance over a future window implied by today's variance swap or option prices. Tradable via forward-starting variance swaps or VIX futures.

concepts.name: Sticky strike
concepts.def: Assumption that the implied volatility at each strike stays fixed when spot moves. Under it, the ATM vol changes as spot slides along the skew.

concepts.name: Sticky delta
concepts.def: Assumption that implied volatility at each delta or moneyness level stays fixed as spot moves, so the whole smile shifts with spot. Common in FX.

concepts.name: Skew slope
concepts.def: Steepness of the volatility skew, often quoted as the vol difference between 25 delta puts and calls or between 90 and 110 percent strikes. Steeper skew means downside protection is relatively expensive.

concepts.name: SVI parameterization
concepts.def: Stochastic volatility inspired formula from Gatheral (2004) that fits each expiry's total implied variance as a function of log moneyness with five parameters, with conditions to avoid arbitrage.
concepts.formula: w(k) = a + b [rho (k - m) + sqrt((k - m)^2 + s^2)]

concepts.name: Static arbitrage
concepts.def: Riskless profit available from a fixed set of option positions when a surface is mispriced, such as negative butterflies across strikes or falling total variance across expiries.

concepts.name: Risk-neutral density
concepts.def: The probability distribution of the underlying at expiry implied by option prices. Its skew and fat tails reveal how the market prices crashes and rallies.
concepts.aliases: implied distribution,option implied density,rnd,state price density

concepts.name: Breeden-Litzenberger formula
concepts.def: Breeden and Litzenberger (1978) result that the second derivative of call prices with respect to strike gives the discounted risk-neutral density. Butterflies therefore price state contingent claims.
concepts.formula: q(K) = e^(rT) x d2C/dK2

concepts.name: Implied correlation
concepts.def: Average correlation among index members implied by index option volatility relative to member option volatilities. High readings mean index options price stocks moving together.
concepts.formula: rho_impl approx = (sigma_index^2 - sum w_i^2 sigma_i^2) / (sum over i<>j of w_i w_j sigma_i sigma_j)

concepts.name: Expected move
concepts.def: The price range the options market implies for a period, often read from the at-the-money straddle price for an earnings date. The straddle approximates the expected absolute move, about 0.8 standard deviations, so one standard deviation is roughly 1.25 times the straddle.
concepts.formula: Expected move (1 sd) approx = S x sigma x sqrt(T); ATM straddle approx 0.8 x S x sigma x sqrt(T), so 1 sd approx 1.25 x straddle

concepts.name: Event volatility
concepts.def: The extra variance options price for a known event such as earnings or an FDA decision, extracted by comparing expiries just before and after the date.
concepts.formula: Event var = sigma_post^2 T_post - sigma_pre^2 T_pre

concepts.name: Volatility crush
concepts.def: Sharp fall in implied volatility once an anticipated event passes and uncertainty resolves. Option buyers can be right on direction and still lose because premium collapses.

concepts.name: IV rank
concepts.def: Where current implied volatility sits within its range over a lookback, usually a year. IV percentile instead counts the share of days with lower vol. Both are crude gauges of rich or cheap volatility.
concepts.formula: IV rank = (IV - min IV) / (max IV - min IV)

concepts.name: Volatility cone
concepts.def: Chart of the historical range of realized volatility by measurement horizon, used to judge whether current implied vol at each tenor is high or low versus history.

concepts.name: Implied-realized spread
concepts.def: Gap between implied volatility and the volatility later realized over the option's life. Persistently positive on equity indices, it is the payoff to systematic option selling.
concepts.aliases: iv rv spread,vol premium,implied minus realized

concepts.name: Leverage effect
concepts.def: Tendency of equity volatility to rise when prices fall, observed by Black (1976). It produces negative spot-vol correlation and downside skew.

concepts.name: Spot-vol correlation
concepts.def: Correlation between changes in the underlying and changes in implied volatility. Strongly negative for equity indices, it drives vanna exposure and how skew prices.

concepts.name: Volatility clustering
concepts.def: Large price changes tend to follow large changes and calm follows calm, so volatility is persistent and forecastable. Modeled with GARCH.

concepts.name: Range-based volatility
concepts.def: Volatility estimators using high, low, open and close prices, such as Parkinson, Garman-Klass and Yang-Zhang. They extract more information per day than close-to-close estimates.
concepts.formula: Parkinson: sigma^2 = (1 / (4 ln 2)) x mean[ln(H/L)^2]
concepts.aliases: parkinson volatility,garman klass,yang zhang,high low volatility

concepts.name: Square root of time rule
concepts.def: Scaling volatility across horizons by the square root of time, valid when returns are independent. Annual vol = daily vol x sqrt(252); breaks down with autocorrelation or fat tails.
concepts.formula: sigma_T = sigma_1 x sqrt(T)

concepts.name: Rule of 16
concepts.def: Trader shorthand that daily standard deviation is annualized volatility divided by 16, since sqrt(256) = 16 is close to sqrt(252). A 16 vol implies roughly 1 percent daily moves.
concepts.formula: Daily move approx = annual vol / 16

concepts.name: Option leverage
concepts.def: Percentage change in an option's price per percentage change in the underlying. Out-of-the-money options have the highest leverage and fastest decay.
concepts.formula: Lambda = delta x S / V

concepts.name: Synthetic position
concepts.def: Combining options, or options and the underlying, to replicate another exposure via put-call parity. Long call plus short put at one strike equals a long forward.

concepts.name: Conversion and reversal
concepts.def: Arbitrage trades enforcing put-call parity. A conversion is long stock, long put, short call; a reversal is the opposite. Their pricing reveals implied financing and borrow costs.

concepts.name: Box spread
concepts.def: A long call spread plus a long put spread at the same two strikes, paying the strike difference at expiry with no market risk. Its price implies a financing rate, so it works as a synthetic loan.
concepts.formula: Box value = (K2 - K1) x e^(-rT)

concepts.name: Jelly roll
concepts.def: Long a synthetic forward at one expiry and short it at another, same strike. It isolates the carry between two dates, financing and dividends, and is used for rolling positions.

concepts.name: Implied borrow rate
concepts.def: Cost to borrow stock implied by put-call parity. When shares are hard to borrow, puts trade rich and calls cheap versus parity, revealing the lending fee.
concepts.aliases: implied borrow cost,option implied borrow,implied stock loan

concepts.name: Implied dividend
concepts.def: Dividends the market expects, backed out from put-call parity or dividend futures. Divergence from analyst forecasts can signal cuts or trading opportunities.

concepts.name: Weekly options
concepts.def: Listed options with roughly one week to expiry, now offered on major indices and many stocks, with daily expiries on some indices. They concentrate gamma close to expiry.

concepts.name: LEAPS
concepts.def: Long-term equity anticipation securities: listed options with more than a year to expiry. High vega and low theta per day; often used as stock replacement.

concepts.name: FLEX options
concepts.def: Exchange listed options with customizable strike, expiry and exercise style, cleared like standard listed options. Used by institutions and by buffer ETFs.

concepts.name: OTC options
concepts.def: Bilateral option contracts negotiated directly between counterparties, often under an ISDA agreement. Fully customizable but carry counterparty and liquidity risk.

concepts.name: Options Clearing Corporation
concepts.def: The central clearing house for US listed options, which becomes buyer to every seller and seller to every buyer, guaranteeing performance and allocating assignments.

concepts.name: Index options
concepts.def: Options on equity indices such as SPX or NDX, typically European and cash settled. They carry steep put skew because investors buy them to insure portfolios.

concepts.name: Options spread
concepts.def: A position combining two or more options on the same underlying, differing in strike, expiry or type. Spreads cap risk and cost and isolate a view on direction, volatility or time.

concepts.name: Vertical spread
concepts.def: Buying and selling options of the same type and expiry at different strikes. Defines maximum gain and loss and lowers net premium versus an outright option.

concepts.name: Call spread
concepts.def: Long a call at one strike and short a call at a higher strike, same expiry. A bull call spread profits from a moderate rally with capped upside and lower cost.
concepts.formula: Max gain = K2 - K1 - net debit
concepts.aliases: bull call spread,call vertical,long call spread

concepts.name: Debit spread
concepts.def: An options spread that costs net premium to open, such as a long call spread. Max loss is the debit paid; it profits if the underlying moves toward the short strike.

concepts.name: Credit spread (options)
concepts.def: An options spread that collects net premium, such as selling a put and buying a lower strike put. Max gain is the credit; max loss is strike width minus credit.
concepts.aliases: credit vertical,bull put spread,bear call spread,put credit spread

concepts.name: Strangle
concepts.def: Long an out-of-the-money call and an out-of-the-money put on the same expiry. Cheaper than a straddle but needs a larger move to pay off.

concepts.name: Short strangle
concepts.def: Selling an out-of-the-money put and call, collecting premium if the underlying stays in a range. Profits from time decay and falling vol but has open-ended tail risk.

concepts.name: Short straddle
concepts.def: Selling a call and put at the same at-the-money strike. Maximum theta and premium income, with losses growing in either direction as the underlying moves away.

concepts.name: Butterfly spread
concepts.def: Long one option at a low strike, short two at a middle strike and long one at a high strike, equal spacing. Pays most if the underlying expires at the middle strike; prices the risk-neutral density.
concepts.formula: Payoff peak = K2 - K1 at K2

concepts.name: Iron butterfly
concepts.def: A short at-the-money straddle plus a long out-of-the-money strangle as wings. Earns premium if the underlying pins near the center, with capped losses.

concepts.name: Iron condor
concepts.def: A short put spread plus a short call spread with the same expiry, collecting premium for a range bound view. Defined risk but negative gamma and vega.

concepts.name: Calendar spread
concepts.def: Selling a near-dated option and buying a longer-dated one at the same strike. Profits from faster decay of the short leg and from a rise in back-month vol; a bet on the term structure.

concepts.name: Diagonal spread
concepts.def: A calendar spread with different strikes, such as selling a near-dated out-of-the-money call against a longer-dated call. Mixes directional, time decay and term structure views.

concepts.name: Ratio spread
concepts.def: Buying a number of options and selling a different number at another strike, such as long one call and short two higher calls. Cheap or credit entry, but uncovered beyond the short strike.

concepts.name: Backspread
concepts.def: Selling fewer near-the-money options and buying more further out-of-the-money options. Long convexity, it profits from a large move in the direction of the extra options.

concepts.name: Risk reversal
concepts.def: Long an out-of-the-money call and short an out-of-the-money put, or the reverse. As a trade it is a cheap directional bet; as an FX quote it measures skew between 25 delta calls and puts.
concepts.formula: 25d RR = vol(25d call) - vol(25d put)

concepts.name: Seagull
concepts.def: A three leg structure, typically a call spread financed by selling an out-of-the-money put, or the mirror. Popular in FX and commodity hedging for near zero cost protection.

concepts.name: Protective put
concepts.def: Owning the underlying plus a put, which sets a floor on losses for the put's life. Costs premium; the payoff matches a long call by put-call parity.
concepts.aliases: married put,portfolio insurance put,long put hedge

concepts.name: Cash-secured put
concepts.def: Selling a put while holding cash equal to the strike value, so assignment can be paid for. Earns premium and may buy stock below today's price; equivalent to a covered call by parity.

concepts.name: Short put
concepts.def: Selling a put option, collecting premium in return for the obligation to buy the underlying at the strike. Gains if the price stays above the strike; large losses in a crash.

concepts.name: Naked call
concepts.def: Selling a call without owning the underlying. Losses are theoretically unlimited if the price rises, so brokers require high margin.

concepts.name: Wheel strategy
concepts.def: Retail income strategy of selling cash-secured puts until assigned, then selling covered calls on the shares until called away, and repeating. Its return profile is short volatility.

concepts.name: Buy-write
concepts.def: Buying stock and writing a call against it in one trade. The CBOE BXM index tracks a systematic monthly at-the-money buy-write on the S&P 500.

concepts.name: Put-write strategy
concepts.def: Systematic sale of index puts collateralized by cash, as tracked by the CBOE PUT index. It harvests the variance risk premium but suffers sharp drawdowns in crashes.

concepts.name: Stock replacement
concepts.def: Swapping a stock holding for deep in-the-money calls or LEAPS to keep upside while freeing capital and capping downside to the premium.

concepts.name: Long volatility
concepts.def: Positions that gain when volatility rises or large moves occur, such as owned straddles, VIX calls or variance swaps. They tend to bleed in calm markets and pay in crises.

concepts.name: Short volatility
concepts.def: Positions that earn premium when volatility stays below implied, such as sold options or short VIX futures. Steady small gains with rare large losses, a classic negatively skewed payoff.

concepts.name: Volatility arbitrage
concepts.def: Trading the difference between implied volatility and a forecast of realized volatility, holding delta hedged options. Not riskless: profit depends on the realized path.

concepts.name: Skew trading
concepts.def: Positions that profit from changes in the steepness of the volatility skew, such as risk reversals or put ratio spreads, usually vega and delta hedged.

concepts.name: Payoff diagram
concepts.def: Chart of a derivative position's value at expiry against the underlying price. Used to read breakevens, maximum gain and loss of option strategies.

concepts.name: Exotic option
concepts.def: Any option whose payoff or exercise rule differs from a plain vanilla call or put, such as barriers, digitals, Asians or multi-asset options. Mostly traded OTC and in structured products.

concepts.name: Vanilla option
concepts.def: A standard European or American call or put with a single underlying and fixed strike and expiry. The building block for spreads and for calibrating exotic models.

concepts.name: Path dependence
concepts.def: Property of a payoff that depends on the underlying's price history, not just the final price. Barriers, Asians, lookbacks and autocallables are path dependent.

concepts.name: Barrier option
concepts.def: An option that comes into existence (knock-in) or ceases to exist (knock-out) if the underlying touches a barrier level. Cheaper than vanillas; hedging is hard near the barrier.

concepts.name: Knock-out option
concepts.def: A barrier option that expires worthless if the underlying touches the barrier during its life, sometimes paying a rebate. Up-and-out and down-and-out are the common types.

concepts.name: Knock-in option
concepts.def: A barrier option that only becomes a live vanilla option if the underlying touches the barrier. A knock-in plus the matching knock-out equals the vanilla.
concepts.formula: Knock-in + knock-out = vanilla

concepts.name: Barrier hedging
concepts.def: Dealer risk management of barrier books, where delta and gamma jump as spot nears the barrier. Defending or breaching large barriers can cause visible flows in FX and index markets.

concepts.name: Digital option
concepts.def: An option paying a fixed amount if the underlying finishes beyond the strike, and nothing otherwise. Its price is close to the risk-neutral probability and is very sensitive to skew near the strike.
concepts.formula: Cash-or-nothing call = DF x N(d2) x payout
concepts.aliases: binary option,cash or nothing,all or nothing,digital

concepts.name: One-touch option
concepts.def: Pays a fixed amount if the underlying touches a level at any time before expiry. A no-touch pays if it never does; double variants use two levels. Common in FX.
concepts.aliases: one touch,no touch,double no touch,dnt,american digital

concepts.name: Asian option
concepts.def: An option whose payoff depends on the average price over a period rather than the final price. Averaging lowers volatility and cost; common in commodities and FX hedging.

concepts.name: Lookback option
concepts.def: An option whose payoff uses the maximum or minimum price reached over its life, letting the holder buy at the low or sell at the high. Expensive because it removes timing risk.

concepts.name: Compound option
concepts.def: An option on an option, such as a call on a call. Used to hedge contingent exposures like bids on projects.

concepts.name: Chooser option
concepts.def: An option where the holder decides at a future date whether it becomes a call or a put. Suited to binary events with uncertain direction.

concepts.name: Cliquet option
concepts.def: A series of forward-starting options whose strikes reset periodically, with gains locked in each period and often local and global caps and floors. Highly sensitive to forward skew.

concepts.name: Forward-start option
concepts.def: An option whose strike is set at a future date as a percentage of the spot then prevailing. Its value depends on forward volatility and forward skew.

concepts.name: Quanto option
concepts.def: An option on a foreign asset whose payoff is converted at a fixed exchange rate, removing currency risk. Its pricing depends on the correlation between the asset and the FX rate.

concepts.name: Basket option
concepts.def: An option on a weighted basket of assets. Cheaper than options on each component because diversification lowers basket volatility; a long correlation position.

concepts.name: Rainbow option
concepts.def: A multi-asset option paying on the best or worst performer among several underlyings. Worst-of options are cheap and short correlation; best-of are expensive and long it.

concepts.name: Worst-of option
concepts.def: Option or note payoff based on the weakest of several underlyings. Investors who sell worst-of puts in structured notes are short correlation and short volatility.

concepts.name: Exchange option
concepts.def: Option to swap one asset for another. Margrabe (1978) priced it in closed form using the volatility of the price ratio.
concepts.formula: Margrabe: sigma = sqrt(sigma1^2 + sigma2^2 - 2 rho sigma1 sigma2)

concepts.name: Spread option
concepts.def: An option on the difference between two prices, such as crack, spark or calendar spreads. Its value depends heavily on the correlation between the legs.

concepts.name: Autocallable
concepts.def: Structured note that pays a coupon and redeems early if the underlying is above a trigger on an observation date, but exposes the investor to losses through a knock-in put if it falls far.

concepts.name: Reverse convertible
concepts.def: Short-dated note paying a high coupon in exchange for the investor selling a put on a stock; at maturity it repays principal or delivers shares if the stock has fallen.

concepts.name: Structured note
concepts.def: A bank-issued debt security whose return is linked to a derivative payoff on equities, rates or other assets. Investors take issuer credit risk and usually pay embedded fees.

concepts.name: Principal-protected note
concepts.def: A structured note combining a zero-coupon bond with a call option, returning principal at maturity plus some upside participation. Protection depends on the issuer's credit.

concepts.name: Accumulator
concepts.def: OTC contract obliging the holder to buy an asset periodically at a discount strike, knocking out above a barrier, often buying double below the strike. Losses can grow fast in a decline.

concepts.name: Target redemption forward
concepts.def: FX structure delivering a series of forwards at an enhanced rate that terminates once accumulated gains reach a target, while losses are often leveraged and uncapped.

concepts.name: Warrant
concepts.def: A long-dated call option issued by a company on its own shares; exercise creates new shares and dilutes holders. Also used for exchange-traded bank-issued options in Europe and Asia.

concepts.name: Embedded option
concepts.def: An option built into another security, such as a call feature in a callable bond, a conversion right or a prepayment option in a mortgage. It must be valued separately to price the security.

concepts.name: Cross gamma
concepts.def: Sensitivity of one asset's delta to moves in another, arising in multi-asset options. Its sign shows whether a book is long or short correlation.

concepts.name: Correlation risk
concepts.def: Exposure of a derivatives book to changes in correlation among underlyings. Exotics desks selling worst-of notes accumulate long correlation risk that is hard to hedge.

concepts.name: Dealer hedging flows
concepts.def: Trading by option market makers to hedge the greeks of their book. When dealers are short gamma their hedges add to moves; when long gamma they dampen them.

concepts.name: Gamma flip
concepts.def: Estimated price level where aggregate dealer gamma changes sign. Above it dealers are thought long gamma and dampen moves; below, short gamma and amplify them. Estimates rely on positioning assumptions.
concepts.aliases: zero gamma level,gamma flip point,zero gamma

concepts.name: Vanna flows
concepts.def: Dealer delta hedging triggered by changes in implied volatility rather than price. Falling vol after a selloff can force dealers to buy back hedges, supporting a rally.

concepts.name: Charm flows
concepts.def: Dealer delta hedging caused by the passage of time as option deltas decay, concentrated into expiries. Often cited as a driver of drift into monthly options expiration.

concepts.name: Strike pinning
concepts.def: Tendency of a stock to close near a large open interest strike at expiry, linked to delta hedging by long gamma holders who sell rallies and buy dips around the strike.

concepts.name: Max pain
concepts.def: Strike at which the total value of outstanding options would be lowest at expiry. Some traders treat it as a magnet for price; evidence is weak.

concepts.name: Monthly options expiration
concepts.def: The standard monthly expiry for listed US equity options, the third Friday of the month. Large open interest rolls off, freeing dealer hedges and often changing market dynamics.

concepts.name: Quad witching
concepts.def: Quarterly third Friday when stock index futures, index options, stock options and single stock futures expire together, bringing heavy volume and closing auction imbalances.

concepts.name: Portfolio insurance
concepts.def: Dynamic hedging strategy that replicates a protective put by selling index futures as prices fall. Its mechanical selling is widely blamed for amplifying the 1987 crash.
concepts.aliases: cppi,constant proportion portfolio insurance,dynamic hedging insurance

concepts.name: Variance swap
concepts.def: Forward contract that pays the difference between realized variance over a period and a fixed variance strike, times variance notional. Gives pure exposure to volatility without delta hedging.
concepts.formula: Payoff = variance notional x (realized var - K_var); var notional = vega notional / (2 x K_vol)

concepts.name: Variance strike
concepts.def: The fixed level of a variance swap, quoted in volatility terms. Set by replicating with a strip of out-of-the-money options weighted by 1/K^2, so it sits above ATM vol when skew is steep.
concepts.formula: K_var = (2 e^(rT) / T) x integral of OTM option price / K^2 dK

concepts.name: Vega notional
concepts.def: Size of a variance or volatility swap expressed as P&L per one vol point change in realized volatility near the strike. Market convention for quoting variance swap size.
concepts.formula: Vega notional = variance notional x 2 x K_vol

concepts.name: Variance notional
concepts.def: Multiplier on a variance swap's payoff per unit of variance difference. Because payoff is linear in variance, P&L is convex in volatility.
concepts.formula: Variance notional = vega notional / (2 x K_vol)

concepts.name: Volatility swap
concepts.def: Forward contract paying realized volatility minus a strike. Because volatility is the square root of variance, a vol swap strike sits below the variance strike by a convexity adjustment.

concepts.name: Volatility convexity adjustment
concepts.def: Gap between the variance swap strike and the fair volatility swap strike, caused by Jensen's inequality. It widens with the volatility of volatility.
concepts.formula: K_vol approx = sqrt(K_var) - Var(var) / (8 x K_var^1.5)

concepts.name: Log contract
concepts.def: Neuberger (1994) claim paying the log of the terminal price. A delta hedged log contract earns realized variance, which is why variance swaps can be replicated with options.

concepts.name: Carr-Madan spanning formula
concepts.def: Carr and Madan (1998) result that any smooth payoff of the terminal price can be replicated by a bond, a forward and a continuum of out-of-the-money options weighted by the payoff's second derivative.
concepts.formula: f(S_T) = f(F) + f'(F)(S_T - F) + integral f''(K) x OTM option(K) dK

concepts.name: Corridor variance swap
concepts.def: Variance swap that accrues realized variance only while the underlying is inside a price range. Lets traders target downside or upside volatility.

concepts.name: Gamma swap
concepts.def: Variance swap variant where each day's squared return is weighted by the price relative to its initial level. Exposure shrinks after declines, so it is less exposed to crash variance than a standard var swap.

concepts.name: Volatility of volatility
concepts.def: How much implied or realized volatility itself fluctuates. Drives the price of VIX options, the convexity of variance swaps and the curvature of the smile.

concepts.name: VVIX
concepts.def: CBOE index of the 30-day implied volatility of VIX options, computed with the VIX methodology. A gauge of demand for convexity on volatility itself.

concepts.name: VIX methodology
concepts.def: VIX is 100 times the square root of 30-day risk-neutral expected variance on the S&P 500, computed from a strip of out-of-the-money SPX options interpolated between two expiries. It is model-free, not an average of implied vols.
concepts.formula: sigma^2 = (2/T) sum (dK/K^2) e^(RT) Q(K) - (1/T)(F/K0 - 1)^2
concepts.aliases: vix calculation,vix formula,model free implied variance

concepts.name: VIX futures
concepts.def: Cash settled futures on the VIX index at a future date. They price expected future 30-day volatility, not spot VIX, and usually trade above spot in calm markets.

concepts.name: VIX options
concepts.def: European, cash settled options on VIX futures for the matching expiry. Calls are popular tail hedges; their skew is usually upward sloping, unlike equity options.

concepts.name: VIX term structure
concepts.def: Curve of VIX futures prices across expiries. Usually in contango, so long volatility products lose value as futures roll down; inverts into backwardation during selloffs.
concepts.aliases: vix curve,vix futures curve,vix contango,vix backwardation

concepts.name: VIX roll yield
concepts.def: Return from VIX futures converging toward spot VIX as expiry approaches. Negative for long holders in contango, which explains long run losses in long VIX ETPs.

concepts.name: VIX settlement
concepts.def: VIX futures and options settle to a special opening quotation calculated from actual opening trades in SPX options on expiration morning, not to the prior close.

concepts.name: Volatility ETP
concepts.def: Exchange-traded products tracking rolling VIX futures indices, long, leveraged or inverse. Long versions decay in contango; inverse versions can be wiped out by a vol spike.

concepts.name: Leveraged ETF
concepts.def: ETF that targets a daily multiple of an index return, rebalancing each day. Over longer horizons returns diverge from the multiple due to volatility drag, and end-of-day rebalancing adds flows.
concepts.aliases: letf,inverse etf,2x etf,3x etf,daily leveraged etf

concepts.name: Volatility drag
concepts.def: Reduction in compound growth caused by volatility: geometric return is roughly arithmetic return minus half the variance. Severe for leveraged and inverse daily-reset products.
concepts.formula: Geometric return approx = arithmetic return - 0.5 x sigma^2

concepts.name: CBOE SKEW index
concepts.def: Index derived from the third moment of the S&P 500 risk-neutral distribution implied by out-of-the-money options. Higher values mean more priced tail risk.

concepts.name: Dispersion trade
concepts.def: Selling index volatility and buying volatility on index members, usually delta hedged. Profits when realized correlation is below the implied correlation priced in index options.

concepts.name: Correlation swap
concepts.def: Swap paying the difference between realized average pairwise correlation of a basket and a fixed strike. A direct way to trade correlation without the vega of a dispersion trade.
concepts.formula: Payoff = notional x (realized average correlation - strike)

concepts.name: Realized correlation
concepts.def: Correlation actually observed among assets' returns over a window. Compared with implied correlation, it determines the payoff of dispersion and correlation trades.

concepts.name: Correlation risk premium
concepts.def: Tendency of index implied correlation to exceed later realized correlation, because investors pay for protection against diversification failing in crashes. Sellers earn it through dispersion.

concepts.name: Volatility carry
concepts.def: Expected return from holding a volatility position if nothing changes, from roll-down along the term structure and the implied-realized spread. Short vol books earn it but carry tail risk.

concepts.name: VSTOXX
concepts.def: Implied volatility index on the Euro Stoxx 50, calculated with a model-free method like VIX. The main European volatility benchmark with listed futures and options.

concepts.name: Volatility index
concepts.def: An index measuring the market's expected volatility of an underlying, usually from option prices. Examples include VIX for the S&P 500, VSTOXX, MOVE for Treasuries and OVX for crude oil.

concepts.name: Volatility targeting
concepts.def: Scaling portfolio exposure inversely to recent or forecast volatility to hold risk near a target. Vol control funds and risk parity deleverage after vol spikes, which can add selling pressure.
concepts.formula: Exposure = target vol / forecast vol

concepts.name: Contract specifications
concepts.def: The exchange rules defining a futures or options contract: underlying, size, multiplier, tick, months, last trading day, settlement method and deliverable grades.

concepts.name: Tick size
concepts.def: Minimum price increment at which an instrument can be quoted or traded. Tick value is tick size times the multiplier; wide ticks relative to price make the spread constrained and queues long.
concepts.formula: Tick value = tick size x contract multiplier

concepts.name: Futures month codes
concepts.def: Single letters identifying contract months: F Jan, G Feb, H Mar, J Apr, K May, M Jun, N Jul, Q Aug, U Sep, V Oct, X Nov, Z Dec. ESZ is a December S&P 500 e-mini.

concepts.name: Front month
concepts.def: The nearest-to-expiry futures contract, usually the most liquid. Traders roll from the front to the next month before expiry or delivery.

concepts.name: Futures curve
concepts.def: Futures prices plotted by expiry. Its slope, contango or backwardation, reflects carry, storage costs, convenience yield and expectations, and determines roll returns.

concepts.name: Futures roll
concepts.def: Closing an expiring futures position and opening the same exposure in a later contract. The calendar spread paid or received sets the roll cost; roll periods bring heavy spread volume.

concepts.name: Futures calendar spread
concepts.def: Long one futures expiry and short another on the same underlying. Exchanges list it as a single instrument; it trades the shape of the curve with lower margin than outrights.

concepts.name: Continuous futures contract
concepts.def: A long price history built by splicing successive futures contracts, back-adjusted or ratio-adjusted at roll dates. Unadjusted splices create false price gaps in backtests.

concepts.name: Initial margin
concepts.def: Collateral required to open a futures or derivatives position, sized by the clearing house to cover likely losses over a short close-out period. It is a performance bond, not a down payment.

concepts.name: Maintenance margin
concepts.def: Minimum margin balance a position must keep. If losses take the account below it, a margin call requires topping back up to initial margin.

concepts.name: Variation margin
concepts.def: Daily cash transfer of gains and losses on futures and cleared swaps, based on the settlement price. Large moves create sudden liquidity needs even for hedged positions.

concepts.name: Mark-to-market
concepts.def: Revaluing positions at current market prices, daily for futures. Gains and losses are realized in cash each day, which removes credit build-up but creates funding needs.

concepts.name: Settlement price
concepts.def: Official daily price set by an exchange, often a volume weighted price near the close, used for margining and marking. Final settlement price determines payoff at expiry.

concepts.name: Trade at settlement
concepts.def: Order type letting futures traders buy or sell at the day's settlement price, or a few ticks away, before it is known. Used by funds benchmarked to settlement.

concepts.name: Clearing house
concepts.def: Central counterparty that interposes itself between buyer and seller, guaranteeing trades and collecting margin. It concentrates counterparty risk into one well capitalized, margined entity.

concepts.name: Novation
concepts.def: Replacing one contract with new ones, as when a clearing house becomes the counterparty to both sides of a trade, or when a bilateral swap is transferred to a new party.

concepts.name: Default waterfall
concepts.def: Order in which a clearing house absorbs a member default: the defaulter's margin and fund contribution, CCP capital, other members' default fund, then further assessments.

concepts.name: Futures commission merchant
concepts.def: Firm that accepts customer orders and margin for futures and cleared swaps and is a member of clearing houses. Must segregate customer funds.

concepts.name: SPAN margin
concepts.def: Standard Portfolio Analysis of Risk, a margin system developed by CME that sets requirements from the worst loss across a grid of price and volatility scenarios, with offsets for spreads.

concepts.name: Portfolio margin
concepts.def: Risk-based margining that sets requirements from stressed losses on a whole portfolio, recognizing hedges. Usually allows far more leverage than position-based rules like Reg T.

concepts.name: Regulation T margin
concepts.def: Federal Reserve rule setting initial margin on US securities purchases, generally 50 percent, with exchange and broker maintenance requirements on top.

concepts.name: Futures price limits
concepts.def: Exchange-set maximum daily price moves for some futures contracts. Trading halts or is restricted at the limit, which can trap traders in locked limit markets.

concepts.name: Position limits
concepts.def: Caps set by exchanges or regulators on the number of contracts one trader can hold, mainly in physical commodities, to limit manipulation and squeezes.

concepts.name: First notice day
concepts.def: First day a seller of a physically delivered futures contract can notify intent to deliver. Speculators usually roll or close before it to avoid delivery.

concepts.name: Last trading day
concepts.def: Final day a futures or options contract can be traded before expiry and settlement or delivery.

concepts.name: Forward price
concepts.def: Price agreed today for delivery at a future date that makes the contract worth zero at inception. Set by cost of carry: spot plus financing and storage minus income.
concepts.formula: F = S x e^((r - q) T)

concepts.name: Futures versus forwards
concepts.def: Futures are standardized, exchange traded, cleared and marked daily; forwards are bilateral, customized and settle at maturity. With random rates, daily settlement makes their prices differ slightly.

concepts.name: Cash-and-carry arbitrage
concepts.def: Buying the spot asset with borrowed money and selling futures when futures trade above fair value, delivering at expiry. The reverse trade applies when futures are cheap.

concepts.name: Reverse cash-and-carry
concepts.def: Shorting the spot asset and buying futures when futures trade below fair value. Requires borrowing the asset, so lending costs limit the trade.
concepts.aliases: reverse carry,reverse cash and carry arbitrage

concepts.name: Equity index futures
concepts.def: Futures on stock indices such as the S&P 500, Nasdaq 100 or Euro Stoxx 50, cash settled to a special opening or closing price. The cheapest way to add or hedge market beta.

concepts.name: Futures fair value
concepts.def: Theoretical price of an index future from spot plus financing minus expected dividends to expiry. Pre-market quotes compare futures to fair value to gauge the likely open.
concepts.formula: FV = S x (1 + r x t) - dividends to expiry

concepts.name: E-mini futures
concepts.def: Electronically traded, smaller-size CME equity index futures, such as the e-mini S&P 500 at 50 times the index. Micro contracts are one tenth the e-mini size.

concepts.name: Implied financing rate
concepts.def: Interest rate implied by the gap between index futures and spot after dividends. When dealers' balance sheets are tight it rises above benchmark rates, signaling the cost of synthetic leverage.

concepts.name: Dividend futures
concepts.def: Futures paying the dividends declared by an index or stock over a calendar period. They let investors trade or hedge dividend risk separately from price.

concepts.name: Single stock futures
concepts.def: Futures on individual shares. Widely traded in Europe and Asia; they offer leverage and synthetic shorting without borrowing shares.

concepts.name: Basis risk
concepts.def: Risk that a hedge and the exposure it covers do not move together, so the basis changes. Arises from different grades, locations, maturities or instruments.

concepts.name: Cross hedge
concepts.def: Hedging an exposure with a related but different instrument, such as jet fuel with heating oil futures. Effective only as long as the correlation holds.

concepts.name: Stack-and-roll hedge
concepts.def: Hedging long-dated obligations with a stack of short-dated futures rolled forward. Exposed to curve shifts and margin calls, as Metallgesellschaft found in 1993.

concepts.name: Exchange for physical
concepts.def: Privately negotiated swap of a futures position for the matching physical or cash position, reported to the exchange. Used to adjust hedges without trading on screen.
concepts.aliases: efp,exchange of futures for physical,exchange for related position

concepts.name: Forward points
concepts.def: Difference between the FX forward rate and spot, quoted in pips. Points reflect the interest rate differential between the two currencies.
concepts.formula: Forward points = forward rate - spot rate

concepts.name: Cross-currency swap
concepts.def: Swap exchanging principal and interest payments in two currencies, with principal exchanged at start and maturity. Used to hedge foreign currency debt.

concepts.name: Futures convexity adjustment
concepts.def: Difference between interest rate futures and forward rates caused by daily margining: shorts gain when rates rise and reinvest at higher rates, so futures rates exceed forward rates.

concepts.name: Gross basis
concepts.def: Cash bond price minus futures price times conversion factor. It includes carry to delivery plus the value of the short's delivery options.
concepts.formula: Gross basis = bond price - futures price x CF

concepts.name: Net basis
concepts.def: Gross basis minus carry to delivery. It measures the value of the short's delivery options and is near zero for the cheapest to deliver bond close to delivery.
concepts.formula: Net basis = gross basis - carry

concepts.name: Delivery options
concepts.def: Choices granted to the short in Treasury futures: which bond to deliver (quality), when in the month (timing) and late afternoon delivery notice (wildcard). They make futures trade cheap to forward.

concepts.name: Swap
concepts.def: A derivative in which two parties exchange streams of cash flows, such as fixed for floating interest, one currency for another or an asset's total return for a funding rate.

concepts.name: Fixed leg
concepts.def: Side of an interest rate swap that pays a constant rate on the notional. Its value moves like a fixed coupon bond as rates change.

concepts.name: Floating leg
concepts.def: Side of a swap whose payments reset to a reference rate such as SOFR each period. Worth close to par at each reset, so it carries little duration.

concepts.name: Swap rate
concepts.def: Fixed rate that makes a new interest rate swap worth zero. It is a weighted average of forward rates and a key benchmark for corporate borrowing and hedging.
concepts.formula: Par swap rate = (1 - DF_n) / sum(tau_i x DF_i)

concepts.name: Overnight index swap
concepts.def: Swap exchanging a fixed rate for the compounded overnight rate, such as SOFR or ESTR. OIS rates are the market's best read of the expected policy path and the standard discount curve.

concepts.name: Multi-curve framework
concepts.def: Pricing approach using one curve for discounting and separate curves for projecting each floating index tenor, needed once basis between tenors became material after 2008.

concepts.name: Discount factor
concepts.def: Present value of one unit paid at a future date, the building block of all fixed income pricing.

concepts.name: Zero-coupon rate
concepts.def: Yield on a single cash flow at a given maturity, with no intermediate coupons. Zero curves are used to discount each cash flow at its own rate.
concepts.formula: z(t) = -ln(DF(t)) / t

concepts.name: Swap DV01
concepts.def: Change in a swap's value for a one basis point parallel shift in rates, used to size swap hedges against bonds or other swaps.
concepts.formula: DV01 = modified duration x notional x 0.0001
concepts.aliases: pv01,bpv,dollar value of a basis point

concepts.name: Swap annuity
concepts.def: Present value of one basis point paid on the fixed leg each period to maturity. Converts swap rate moves into dollar P&L and drives swaption pricing.
concepts.formula: Annuity = sum(tau_i x DF_i)

concepts.name: Forward-starting swap
concepts.def: Interest rate swap whose payments begin at a future date, used to lock in rates for planned borrowing or to trade forward parts of the curve.

concepts.name: Amortizing swap
concepts.def: Interest rate swap whose notional declines on a schedule, matching an amortizing loan or mortgage pool.

concepts.name: Asset swap
concepts.def: Combining a fixed rate bond with a pay-fixed swap so the investor receives a floating rate plus a spread. The asset swap spread compares bond yields with swap rates.

concepts.name: Equity swap
concepts.def: Swap exchanging the return on a stock or index for a fixed or floating rate. Used for synthetic exposure, tax or access reasons and in prime brokerage.

concepts.name: Contract for difference
concepts.def: OTC contract paying the change in an asset's price between opening and closing, with financing charged on the notional. Popular with retail traders outside the US and banned for US retail.

concepts.name: Payer swaption
concepts.def: Right to enter a swap paying fixed at the strike rate, gaining value as rates rise. Used to hedge against higher borrowing costs.

concepts.name: Receiver swaption
concepts.def: Right to enter a swap receiving fixed at the strike rate, gaining value as rates fall. Mortgage investors buy them to hedge negative convexity.

concepts.name: Bermudan swaption
concepts.def: Swaption exercisable on several dates into a swap ending at a fixed maturity. Callable bond issuers are effectively long them, and dealers hedge the resulting books.

concepts.name: Swaption volatility cube
concepts.def: Implied volatilities of swaptions by option expiry, underlying swap tenor and strike. The rates equivalent of an equity vol surface, often fitted with SABR.

concepts.name: Caps and floors
concepts.def: A cap is a strip of call options on a floating rate (caplets) that pays when the rate exceeds a strike; a floor is a strip of puts. Borrowers buy caps to limit rising interest costs.

concepts.name: Caplet
concepts.def: Single-period call option on a floating rate, paying notional times period times the excess of the rate over the strike. Caps are sums of caplets.
concepts.formula: Payoff = N x tau x max(L - K, 0), paid at period end

concepts.name: Constant maturity swap
concepts.def: Swap whose floating leg resets to a swap rate of fixed tenor, such as the 10-year rate, rather than a short rate. Requires a convexity adjustment; CMS spread options trade the curve slope.

concepts.name: Mortgage prepayment risk
concepts.def: Risk that homeowners repay mortgages early when rates fall, returning principal to MBS investors when reinvestment yields are lower. Gives agency MBS their negative convexity.

concepts.name: Convexity hedging
concepts.def: Trading by MBS holders and servicers to rebalance duration as rates move, receiving fixed as rates fall and paying as they rise. In size it can amplify rate moves.

concepts.name: CIR model
concepts.def: Cox, Ingersoll and Ross (1985) short-rate model with square-root volatility that keeps rates non-negative under typical parameters.
concepts.formula: dr = a (b - r) dt + sigma sqrt(r) dW

concepts.name: HJM framework
concepts.def: Heath, Jarrow and Morton (1992) approach modeling the whole forward curve, showing that under no-arbitrage the drift of forward rates is set by their volatilities.

concepts.name: LIBOR market model
concepts.def: Model of discrete forward rates that each follow lognormal or shifted dynamics, consistent with Black pricing of caplets. Used for path-dependent rates exotics.
concepts.aliases: lmm,bgm model,brace gatarek musiela,forward market model

concepts.name: ISDA Master Agreement
concepts.def: Standard contract published by the International Swaps and Derivatives Association governing OTC derivatives between two parties, covering netting, events of default and close-out.

concepts.name: OTC derivatives
concepts.def: Derivatives negotiated bilaterally rather than on an exchange, including most swaps, FX forwards and exotic options. Post-2008 reforms pushed standardized ones into central clearing.

concepts.name: Swap execution facility
concepts.def: Regulated US trading platform for swaps created under Dodd-Frank, offering order books or request for quote for swaps subject to the trade execution mandate.

concepts.name: Uncleared margin rules
