concepts.formula: F = [(RSS_r - RSS_u)/q] / [RSS_u/(n - k)]

concepts.name: Akaike information criterion
concepts.def: A model selection score that rewards fit and penalizes parameters, estimating relative out-of-sample prediction error. Lower is better; it tends to pick larger models than BIC.
concepts.formula: AIC = 2k - 2 lnL

concepts.name: Bayesian information criterion
concepts.def: Schwarz's model selection score with a heavier parameter penalty that grows with sample size, so it favors more parsimonious models and is consistent for the true model when it is among the candidates.
concepts.formula: BIC = k ln(n) - 2 lnL

concepts.name: Maximum likelihood estimation
concepts.def: Choosing parameter values that make the observed data most probable under the model. Efficient when the model is correct; misspecified distributions can still give consistent estimates via quasi-likelihood.
concepts.formula: theta_hat = argmax sum ln f(x_i | theta)
concepts.aliases: mle, ml estimation, quasi-maximum likelihood, qmle

concepts.name: Generalized method of moments
concepts.def: Hansen's (1982) estimation method that chooses parameters to make sample moment conditions, such as pricing errors, as close to zero as possible. Standard for testing asset pricing models with a stochastic discount factor.
concepts.formula: min g(theta)' W g(theta), with g the sample moments
concepts.aliases: gmm, hansen gmm, method of moments

concepts.name: Difference-in-differences
concepts.def: Estimating a causal effect by comparing the change in outcomes for a treated group before and after an event with the change for an untreated group. Relies on parallel trends without treatment.
concepts.formula: DiD = (Y_treat,after - Y_treat,before) - (Y_control,after - Y_control,before)
concepts.aliases: did, diff in diff, parallel trends

concepts.name: Regression discontinuity
concepts.def: Estimating a causal effect by comparing units just above and just below a threshold that determines treatment, such as index inclusion cutoffs, where units near the line are otherwise similar.
concepts.aliases: rdd, rd design, regression discontinuity design

concepts.name: Synthetic control
concepts.def: Abadie's method of building a weighted combination of untreated units that tracks the treated unit before an event, then using it as the counterfactual afterward. Suited to single treated units such as a country.

concepts.name: Propensity score matching
concepts.def: Matching or weighting treated and untreated units by their estimated probability of treatment given observed characteristics, to mimic a randomized comparison. It cannot fix bias from unobserved confounders.

concepts.name: Natural experiment
concepts.def: An event or rule that assigns treatment as if at random, such as a regulatory change or index reconstitution, letting researchers estimate causal effects without a designed experiment.

concepts.name: Causal graph
concepts.def: A directed acyclic graph whose arrows encode assumed causal links among variables. It shows which variables to control for and which to leave alone to estimate a causal effect.
concepts.aliases: dag, directed acyclic graph, causal diagram, pearl

concepts.name: Backdoor criterion
concepts.def: Pearl's rule for choosing control variables: adjust for a set that blocks every non-causal path from treatment to outcome that enters the treatment through an arrow, without including descendants of the treatment.

concepts.name: Collider bias
concepts.def: Spurious association created by conditioning on a variable caused by both the treatment and the outcome, such as studying only funds that survived. Controlling for more variables can make bias worse.
concepts.aliases: berkson's paradox, conditioning on a collider

concepts.name: Placebo test
concepts.def: Rerunning a causal or event analysis on fake event dates, untreated groups or outcomes that should not respond. Finding effects there suggests the main result is spurious.

concepts.name: Simpson's paradox
concepts.def: A relationship that holds within every subgroup reversing or vanishing when the groups are combined, because group sizes differ. Common in aggregated performance and attribution data.

concepts.name: Regression to the mean
concepts.def: Extreme observations tend to be followed by less extreme ones because part of any extreme result is luck. Explains why top-ranked funds and estimated betas tend to drift toward average.
concepts.aliases: reversion to the mean, galton regression

concepts.name: Normal distribution
concepts.def: The symmetric bell-shaped distribution fully described by mean and variance. Convenient for risk models, but daily asset returns show far more extreme moves than it implies.
concepts.formula: f(x) = exp(-(x - mu)^2 / (2 sigma^2)) / (sigma sqrt(2 pi))

concepts.name: Lognormal distribution
concepts.def: The distribution of a variable whose logarithm is normal. Black-Scholes assumes prices are lognormal, which keeps them positive and makes compounded returns normal.
concepts.formula: E(X) = exp(mu + sigma^2 / 2)

concepts.name: Student's t distribution
concepts.def: A symmetric distribution with heavier tails than the normal, controlled by degrees of freedom. Often used in VaR and GARCH models to capture fat-tailed returns.
concepts.formula: excess kurtosis = 6 / (v - 4) for v > 4
concepts.aliases: t distribution, student t, fat-tailed t

concepts.name: Central limit theorem
concepts.def: Sums or averages of many independent finite-variance variables approach a normal distribution. Convergence is slow with fat tails and fails with infinite variance, which matters for aggregated returns.

concepts.name: Law of large numbers
concepts.def: Sample averages converge to the expected value as the sample grows. It applies across many independent bets, not necessarily to one investor's path through time, which is where ergodicity matters.

concepts.name: Effective sample size
concepts.def: The number of independent observations a dependent dataset is worth. Autocorrelation, overlapping returns and few independent regimes make long histories far less informative than their length suggests.
concepts.formula: AR(1) case: n_eff approx n x (1 - rho) / (1 + rho)

concepts.name: Supervised learning
concepts.def: Learning a mapping from inputs to known targets using labeled examples, then predicting targets for new inputs. Return forecasting and default prediction are supervised problems.

concepts.name: Unsupervised learning
concepts.def: Finding structure in unlabeled data, such as clusters, latent factors or anomalies, without a target variable. Used in finance for regime detection, stock clustering and statistical factor extraction.

concepts.name: Self-supervised learning
concepts.def: Learning representations by predicting parts of the data from other parts, such as the next token or a masked value, so the labels come from the data itself. The basis of language model pretraining.

concepts.name: Training set
concepts.def: The portion of data a model's parameters are fitted on. In time series it must precede the validation and test periods to avoid leakage.

concepts.name: Validation set
concepts.def: Data held out from training and used to tune hyperparameters and choose among models. Repeated use makes it partly in-sample.

concepts.name: Test set
concepts.def: Data kept untouched until final evaluation. It gives an unbiased estimate of performance only if it is used once, after all modeling choices are fixed.

concepts.name: Train, validation and test split
concepts.def: Partitioning data into training, validation and test sets. For market data the split should be chronological, with gaps between segments so overlapping labels do not leak.

concepts.name: Hyperparameter
concepts.def: A setting chosen before training rather than learned from the data, such as tree depth, learning rate or penalty strength.

concepts.name: Hyperparameter tuning
concepts.def: Searching over hyperparameter values to maximize validation performance. Extensive tuning on financial data is a form of multiple testing and inflates backtest results.

concepts.name: Grid search
concepts.def: Evaluating every combination from a predefined grid of hyperparameter values. Simple but expensive, and wasteful when only a few hyperparameters matter.

concepts.name: Random search
concepts.def: Sampling hyperparameter combinations at random from specified ranges. Bergstra and Bengio (2012) showed it usually finds good settings faster than grid search.

concepts.name: Bayesian optimization
concepts.def: Hyperparameter search that fits a surrogate model, often a Gaussian process, to past trials and picks the next trial with an acquisition function that balances exploration and exploitation.

concepts.name: Loss function
concepts.def: A function scoring how far predictions are from targets; training minimizes it. The choice encodes what errors cost, for example squared versus absolute error.

concepts.name: Objective function
concepts.def: The quantity an optimizer minimizes or maximizes, typically the loss plus regularization penalties. In trading research it may be a utility or risk-adjusted return target.

concepts.name: Mean squared error
concepts.def: Average of squared prediction errors. Penalizes large misses heavily, and its minimizer is the conditional mean.
concepts.formula: MSE = (1/n) x sum of (y - yhat)^2

concepts.name: Root mean squared error
concepts.def: Square root of mean squared error, expressed in the units of the target, so it reads as a typical error size.
concepts.formula: RMSE = sqrt(MSE)

concepts.name: Mean absolute error
concepts.def: Average absolute prediction error. Less sensitive to outliers than squared error, and its minimizer is the conditional median.
concepts.formula: MAE = (1/n) x sum of abs(y - yhat)

concepts.name: Cross-entropy loss
concepts.def: Classification loss equal to the negative log probability assigned to the true class. Rewards confident correct probabilities and punishes confident mistakes severely.
concepts.formula: L = -sum of y x ln(p)
concepts.aliases: log loss,logloss,negative log likelihood,nll,binary cross entropy

concepts.name: Huber loss
concepts.def: Loss that is quadratic for small errors and linear for large ones, combining squared-error efficiency near zero with absolute-error robustness to outliers such as bad ticks.

concepts.name: Quantile loss
concepts.def: Asymmetric absolute loss whose minimizer is a chosen quantile of the target distribution. Used to forecast value at risk and prediction intervals.
concepts.formula: L = max(q x e, (q - 1) x e), where e = y - yhat

concepts.name: Hinge loss
concepts.def: Classification loss used by support vector machines that is zero once a point is classified correctly with enough margin and grows linearly otherwise.
concepts.formula: L = max(0, 1 - y x f(x))

concepts.name: Gradient descent
concepts.def: Iterative optimization that moves parameters against the gradient of the loss, scaled by a learning rate, until the loss stops falling.
concepts.formula: theta_new = theta - learning rate x gradient of loss

concepts.name: Stochastic gradient descent
concepts.def: Gradient descent using gradients from small random batches instead of the full dataset. Each step is cheap, and the noise can help escape poor regions of the loss surface.

concepts.name: Learning rate
concepts.def: Step size for each gradient update. Too high and training diverges; too low and it crawls or stalls. Usually decayed during training.

concepts.name: Adam optimizer
concepts.def: Adaptive optimizer of Kingma and Ba (2014) that scales each parameter's step using running averages of its gradients and squared gradients. The default for most neural networks.

concepts.name: Mini-batch
concepts.def: The subset of training examples used for one gradient update. Batch size trades gradient noise against hardware efficiency.

concepts.name: Early stopping
concepts.def: Halting training when validation performance stops improving, a cheap regularizer that limits the effective complexity of the model.

concepts.name: Underfitting
concepts.def: When a model is too simple or constrained to capture real structure, giving high error on both training and test data. The high-bias side of the bias-variance trade-off.

concepts.name: Generalization error
concepts.def: Expected prediction error on new data from the same distribution. Training error underestimates it; out-of-sample tests estimate it.

concepts.name: Generalization gap
concepts.def: Difference between training performance and out-of-sample performance. A large gap is the signature of overfitting.

concepts.name: Inductive bias
concepts.def: Assumptions built into a model that let it generalize beyond its data, such as linearity, smoothness, locality in convolutional networks or sequence order in recurrent networks.

concepts.name: No free lunch theorem
concepts.def: Wolpert's result that, averaged over all possible problems, no learning algorithm outperforms any other. Gains come from matching a model's inductive bias to the problem at hand.

concepts.name: Curse of dimensionality
concepts.def: As features multiply, data become sparse in feature space, distances lose meaning and the sample size needed explodes. Severe in finance, where many candidate features face short histories.

concepts.name: Double descent
concepts.def: Pattern where test error falls, rises near the point where a model can fit the training data exactly, then falls again as model size keeps growing.

concepts.name: Learning curve
concepts.def: Plot of training and validation performance against sample size or training time, used to diagnose whether more data or more capacity would help.

concepts.name: Model capacity
concepts.def: The range of functions a model can represent. Higher capacity fits more patterns, including noise.

concepts.name: Logistic regression
concepts.def: Linear model for binary outcomes that maps a weighted sum of features to a probability through the logistic function. A strong, interpretable baseline for default or direction prediction.

concepts.name: Generalized linear model
concepts.def: Regression family linking a linear predictor to the mean of a response from an exponential-family distribution, covering linear, logistic and Poisson regression.

concepts.name: Generalized additive model
concepts.def: Regression in which the response is a sum of smooth nonlinear functions of individual features, keeping per-feature interpretability while allowing curvature.

concepts.name: Lasso regression
concepts.def: Linear regression with an L1 penalty on coefficients that shrinks many exactly to zero and so selects features (Tibshirani 1996).
concepts.formula: minimize sum of squared residuals + lambda x sum of abs(b)

concepts.name: Elastic net
concepts.def: Penalized regression combining L1 and L2 penalties (Zou and Hastie 2005). Selects features like lasso while handling groups of correlated predictors like ridge.
concepts.formula: minimize RSS + lambda1 x sum of abs(b) + lambda2 x sum of b^2

concepts.name: Principal component regression
concepts.def: Regressing the target on the first few principal components of the features rather than the raw features, which reduces dimension and multicollinearity.

concepts.name: Partial least squares
concepts.def: Dimension reduction that builds components to maximize covariance with the target, unlike PCA, which ignores the target. Used in return prediction with many correlated predictors.

concepts.name: Support vector machine
concepts.def: Classifier that finds the boundary with the widest margin between classes and handles nonlinear boundaries through kernels. Support vector regression applies the idea to continuous targets.

concepts.name: Kernel trick
concepts.def: Computing inner products in a high-dimensional feature space through a kernel function without building that space explicitly, letting linear methods fit nonlinear patterns.

concepts.name: Gaussian process
concepts.def: Bayesian nonparametric model placing a prior over functions defined by a covariance kernel, giving predictions with uncertainty bands. Cost grows with the cube of sample size.

concepts.name: Decision tree (machine learning)
concepts.def: Model that splits data recursively on feature thresholds into leaves with simple predictions. Captures nonlinearity and interactions, but a single tree overfits and is unstable.

concepts.name: Bagging
concepts.def: Bootstrap aggregating (Breiman 1996): training models on bootstrap resamples and averaging them, which cuts the variance of unstable learners such as deep trees.

concepts.name: Boosting
concepts.def: Ensemble method that fits weak learners in sequence, each focusing on the errors left by the ones before, mainly to reduce bias.

concepts.name: XGBoost
concepts.def: Widely used gradient boosting library (Chen and Guestrin 2016) with regularized tree objectives, second-order gradients and efficient split finding. A default for tabular financial data.

concepts.name: LightGBM
concepts.def: Gradient boosting library from Microsoft that uses histogram-based splits and leaf-wise tree growth for speed on large tabular datasets.

concepts.name: CatBoost
concepts.def: Gradient boosting library from Yandex with ordered boosting and native handling of categorical features, designed to reduce target leakage from category encoding.

concepts.name: Isolation forest
concepts.def: Anomaly detector that isolates points with random splits; anomalies need fewer splits to isolate than normal points. Used for bad-tick and fraud detection.

concepts.name: K-means clustering
concepts.def: Partitions observations into k clusters by minimizing squared distance to cluster centroids. Requires choosing k and favors round clusters of similar size.

concepts.name: Hierarchical clustering
concepts.def: Builds a tree of nested clusters by merging or splitting groups according to a linkage rule. Underpins hierarchical risk parity.

concepts.name: Gaussian mixture model
concepts.def: Models data as a weighted mix of Gaussian distributions fitted by expectation-maximization, giving soft cluster probabilities. Used to describe return regimes.

concepts.name: Expectation-maximization
concepts.def: Iterative maximum likelihood method for models with hidden variables: estimate the hidden assignments, then refit the parameters, and repeat until convergence.

concepts.name: Hidden Markov model
concepts.def: Model in which an unobserved state follows a Markov chain and each state emits observations from its own distribution. Applied to inferring bull, bear and crisis regimes.

concepts.name: Autoencoder
concepts.def: Neural network trained to reconstruct its input through a narrow bottleneck, learning a compressed representation. Used for denoising, anomaly detection and latent factor models.

concepts.name: Variational autoencoder
concepts.def: Autoencoder that learns a probabilistic latent space (Kingma and Welling 2013), so new samples, such as synthetic return paths, can be generated.

concepts.name: Genetic algorithm
concepts.def: Optimization inspired by evolution that mutates and recombines candidate solutions and keeps the fittest. Applied to trading rule discovery, where it overfits backtests easily.

concepts.name: Instrumented PCA
concepts.def: Model of Kelly, Pruitt and Su (2019) with latent factors whose loadings vary with observable stock characteristics, tying statistical factors to traits such as value and momentum.

concepts.name: Empirical asset pricing via machine learning
concepts.def: Gu, Kelly and Xiu (2020) compared machine learning methods for predicting US stock returns from many characteristics. Trees and neural networks beat linear models, mainly by capturing nonlinear interactions, with momentum, liquidity and volatility signals dominant.

concepts.name: Harvey-Liu-Zhu hurdle
concepts.def: Harvey, Liu and Zhu (2016) argued that, given extensive factor mining, a new factor should clear a t-statistic of about 3 rather than the conventional 2.

concepts.name: Weight decay
concepts.def: Penalty that shrinks neural network weights toward zero at each update; equivalent to an L2 penalty under plain stochastic gradient descent.

concepts.name: Dropout
concepts.def: Regularization that randomly zeroes a fraction of neural network units during training (Srivastava et al. 2014), preventing co-adaptation and acting like an implicit ensemble.

concepts.name: Data augmentation
concepts.def: Expanding training data with transformed copies, such as noise-added or resampled return paths, to make models more robust. Augmentation that breaks time order can leak information.

concepts.name: Tree pruning
concepts.def: Limiting decision tree complexity by cutting branches with little validation benefit, or by capping depth and minimum leaf size.

concepts.name: MAP estimation
concepts.def: Maximum a posteriori estimation: choosing the parameters that maximize likelihood times prior. A Gaussian prior gives ridge regression and a Laplace prior gives lasso.

concepts.name: Sparsity
concepts.def: Model property in which most coefficients or weights are zero, improving interpretability and often robustness. Encouraged by L1 penalties.

concepts.name: K-fold cross-validation
concepts.def: Splitting data into k folds and training on k-1 while testing on the remaining one, in turn. Standard k-fold assumes independent observations and leaks badly in financial time series.

concepts.name: Time-series split
concepts.def: Validation in which each test fold comes after its training data in time, with expanding or rolling training windows, so the model never trains on the future.

concepts.name: Expanding window
concepts.def: Training window anchored at the start of the sample that grows with each step, using all available history.

concepts.name: Nested cross-validation
concepts.def: An inner loop tunes hyperparameters and an outer loop scores performance on folds the tuning never saw, avoiding the optimistic bias of selecting and scoring on the same data.

concepts.name: Backtesting
concepts.def: Simulating a strategy on historical data to estimate how it would have performed, including signals, costs and constraints. A backtest is a hypothesis test with many hidden trials, not proof.

concepts.name: Minimum backtest length
concepts.def: Bailey, Borwein, Lopez de Prado and Zhu (2014): the more strategy variants tried, the longer the backtest must be before a high Sharpe ratio is unlikely to have arisen by chance.

concepts.name: Paper trading
concepts.def: Running a strategy live on real-time data without capital, testing pipelines, latency and signal stability out of sample before money is at risk.

concepts.name: Baseline model
concepts.def: A simple reference model, such as the historical mean, a random walk or a linear regression, that a complex model must beat to justify its cost.

concepts.name: Naive forecast
concepts.def: Forecast equal to the last observed value or a long-run average. For returns, the historical mean is the standard benchmark behind out-of-sample R squared.

concepts.name: Confusion matrix
concepts.def: Table of predicted versus actual classes counting true positives, false positives, true negatives and false negatives; the basis of most classification metrics.

concepts.name: Precision
concepts.def: Share of predicted positives that are truly positive. Matters when acting on a false signal is costly.
concepts.formula: Precision = TP / (TP + FP)

concepts.name: Recall
concepts.def: Share of actual positives the model catches, also called sensitivity or true positive rate. Matters when missing an event, such as a default, is costly.
concepts.formula: Recall = TP / (TP + FN)

concepts.name: F1 score
concepts.def: Harmonic mean of precision and recall, a single number balancing the two.
concepts.formula: F1 = 2 x precision x recall / (precision + recall)

concepts.name: Accuracy
concepts.def: Share of predictions that are correct. Misleading with imbalanced classes and for return direction, where a few large moves matter more than many small ones.
concepts.formula: Accuracy = (TP + TN) / N

concepts.name: ROC curve
concepts.def: Plot of true positive rate against false positive rate across decision thresholds; the area under it is AUC.

concepts.name: Precision-recall curve
concepts.def: Plot of precision against recall across thresholds. More informative than the ROC curve for rare events such as defaults or crashes.

concepts.name: Class imbalance
concepts.def: When one class is rare, such as defaults or fraud, so naive models predict the majority and accuracy misleads. Addressed by reweighting, resampling or threshold choice.

concepts.name: SMOTE
concepts.def: Synthetic minority oversampling technique (Chawla et al. 2002), which creates synthetic minority examples by interpolating between neighbors. Must be applied only inside training folds.

concepts.name: Decision threshold
concepts.def: The probability cutoff that turns a classifier's score into an action. It should be set from the costs and payoffs of each error, not left at 0.5.

concepts.name: IC information ratio
concepts.def: Mean information coefficient divided by its standard deviation over time, measuring how consistent a signal's skill is.
concepts.formula: ICIR = mean(IC) / std(IC)

concepts.name: Reliability diagram
concepts.def: Plot of predicted probabilities against observed frequencies by bin. A calibrated model lies on the diagonal.

concepts.name: Platt scaling
concepts.def: Recalibrating classifier scores by fitting a logistic regression on held-out data (Platt 1999).

concepts.name: Target leakage
concepts.def: Including a feature that carries information about the target that was not available at prediction time, such as a field updated after the event. Produces spectacular backtests that fail live.

concepts.name: Preprocessing leakage
concepts.def: Fitting scalers, imputers, PCA or feature selection on the full dataset before splitting, so test-period statistics shape the training data.

concepts.name: Overlapping labels
concepts.def: When label horizons overlap, such as 20-day forward returns sampled daily, adjacent observations share outcomes. This inflates the apparent sample size and leaks across train and test splits.

concepts.name: Test set reuse
concepts.def: Evaluating many models on the same holdout until one looks good, which turns the test set into training data through selection.

concepts.name: Restatement bias
concepts.def: Using revised fundamentals in a backtest when only the originally reported figures were known at the time.

concepts.name: Reporting lag
concepts.def: Delay between a period's end and the public release of its data, such as weeks for quarterly filings or macro statistics. Features must be lagged to match.

concepts.name: Concept drift
concepts.def: Change over time in the relationship between features and target, so a once-valid model degrades. Common in markets as participants adapt to known patterns.

concepts.name: Label shift
concepts.def: Change in the distribution of the target, such as the default rate, while the feature distribution within each class stays fixed.

concepts.name: Model decay
concepts.def: Loss of predictive performance after deployment from drift, crowding or regime change; requires monitoring and a retraining policy.

concepts.name: Alpha decay
concepts.def: Erosion of a signal's predictive power, either over the holding horizon after the signal forms or over calendar time as others discover and trade it.

concepts.name: Signal half-life
concepts.def: Time for a signal's predictive power or expected return contribution to fall by half, guiding rebalance frequency and acceptable turnover.

concepts.name: Spurious correlation
concepts.def: Correlation arising from chance, common trends or confounders rather than a real link. Abundant whenever many series are searched.

concepts.name: Garden of forking paths
concepts.def: Gelman and Loken's term for analysis choices made after seeing the data, which create many implicit tests even without conscious fishing.

concepts.name: Benchmark overfitting
concepts.def: Tuning methods to a shared public benchmark until reported gains reflect the test set's quirks rather than general skill.

concepts.name: Fixed-horizon labeling
concepts.def: Labeling each observation by the sign or size of its return over a fixed future window. Simple, but ignores the path taken and changing volatility.

concepts.name: Trend-scanning labels
concepts.def: Labeling method that fits trend regressions over several forward windows and takes the sign of the most significant t-statistic as the label (Lopez de Prado).

concepts.name: Sample uniqueness
concepts.def: The degree to which an observation's label horizon does not overlap those of other observations; used to down-weight redundant samples (Lopez de Prado 2018).

concepts.name: Sequential bootstrap
concepts.def: Bootstrap that draws observations with probability tied to their uniqueness, reducing redundancy among overlapping labels.

concepts.name: Fractional differentiation
concepts.def: Differencing a series by a non-integer order to make it stationary while keeping more memory of price levels than ordinary returns do.

concepts.name: CUSUM filter
concepts.def: Event sampler that triggers when cumulative deviations from a reference level exceed a threshold, so sampling concentrates around large moves.

concepts.name: Information-driven bars
concepts.def: Sampling market data by activity, such as trades, volume or dollar value, instead of clock time. Returns become closer to normal and better synchronized with information arrival.

concepts.name: Tick bars
concepts.def: Bars formed after a fixed number of trades rather than a fixed time interval.

concepts.name: Volume bars
concepts.def: Bars formed each time a fixed number of shares or contracts trades.

concepts.name: Dollar bars
concepts.def: Bars formed each time a fixed notional value trades, which stays robust to price level changes and share count changes.

concepts.name: Time bars
concepts.def: Bars sampled at fixed clock intervals, such as one minute or one day. They oversample quiet periods and undersample busy ones.

concepts.name: Imbalance bars
concepts.def: Bars formed when signed order flow imbalance exceeds its expected level, aiming to sample when informed trading appears.

concepts.name: SHAP values
concepts.def: Shapley additive explanations (Lundberg and Lee 2017): attribute each prediction to features using Shapley values from cooperative game theory, giving consistent local and global importance.

concepts.name: Shapley value
concepts.def: Shapley (1953): a fair split of a coalition's payoff that averages each player's marginal contribution over all orders in which players could join.

concepts.name: Mean decrease impurity
concepts.def: Tree-based importance that sums the impurity reduction from splits on each feature. Fast, but computed in-sample and biased toward features with many distinct values.

concepts.name: Clustered feature importance
concepts.def: Computing importance for clusters of correlated features together, avoiding the dilution that occurs when substitute features split the credit.

concepts.name: Partial dependence plot
concepts.def: Plot of a model's average prediction as one feature varies, averaging over the observed values of the others. Hides effects that differ across observations.

concepts.name: Interpretability
concepts.def: The degree to which people can understand why a model makes a prediction. Matters for risk sign-off, regulation and spotting nonsense relationships.

concepts.name: Feature interaction
concepts.def: When one feature's effect depends on another's value, such as momentum behaving differently in high-volatility regimes. Trees capture interactions automatically; linear models need explicit terms.

concepts.name: Covariance denoising
concepts.def: Cleaning a sample correlation matrix by replacing eigenvalues consistent with pure noise, as judged by random matrix theory, to stabilize portfolio optimization.

concepts.name: Marchenko-Pastur distribution
concepts.def: Distribution of eigenvalues of a purely random correlation matrix given the ratio of variables to observations. Eigenvalues inside its bounds cannot be told apart from noise.

concepts.name: Champion-challenger testing
concepts.def: Running a candidate model beside the production model and promoting it only after it beats the incumbent on live data.

concepts.name: Reproducibility
concepts.def: The ability to rerun a research result and get the same outputs, which requires fixed data versions, code, random seeds and environment.

concepts.name: Random seed
concepts.def: Initial value for a pseudorandom number generator. Fixing it makes runs reproducible; varying it shows how much a result depends on luck.

concepts.name: Cross-sectional prediction
concepts.def: Forecasting which assets will beat others at a point in time, rather than whether the market will rise. Offers more breadth and observations than time-series prediction.

concepts.name: Time-series prediction
concepts.def: Forecasting one asset's or market's future values from its own history and other variables. Few independent observations make it harder than cross-sectional prediction.

concepts.name: Forecast horizon
concepts.def: The length of time a prediction targets. Shorter horizons give more observations but higher cost drag; longer ones give fewer independent samples.

concepts.name: Probabilistic forecast
concepts.def: Forecast giving a full distribution or event probabilities rather than a single point, scored by proper scoring rules such as log loss or CRPS.

concepts.name: Proper scoring rule
concepts.def: Scoring rule whose expected score is optimized by reporting one's true probabilities, such as the log score or the Brier score.

concepts.name: Prediction interval
concepts.def: Range expected to contain a future observation with a stated probability. It is wider than a confidence interval for the mean because it includes the noise of the outcome itself.

concepts.name: Feature selection
concepts.def: Choosing a subset of candidate features to cut noise, cost and overfitting, using filters, wrapper searches or embedded methods such as lasso. Must be done inside training folds.

concepts.name: Out-of-distribution inputs
concepts.def: Inputs unlike anything in the training data, where model outputs are unreliable. Markets produce these in crises.

concepts.name: Adversarial validation
concepts.def: Training a classifier to tell training rows from test rows. If it succeeds, the distributions differ and validation results may not carry over.

concepts.name: Tabular data
concepts.def: Data organized as rows and feature columns, such as stock-month panels. Gradient-boosted trees often match or beat deep learning on it.

concepts.name: Panel data
concepts.def: Data observing many entities over many periods, such as stocks by month. Inference needs care with cross-sectional and time dependence, for example clustered standard errors.

concepts.name: Neural network
concepts.def: Model of layered units, each taking a weighted sum of inputs passed through a nonlinear activation, with weights learned by backpropagation. A flexible function approximator that needs much data.

concepts.name: Multilayer perceptron
concepts.def: Feedforward neural network with one or more hidden layers of fully connected units; the standard deep model for tabular inputs.

concepts.name: Activation function
concepts.def: Nonlinear function applied to a unit's weighted input, such as ReLU, sigmoid or tanh, which lets networks represent nonlinear relationships.

concepts.name: ReLU
concepts.def: Rectified linear unit, the default hidden-layer activation: cheap to compute and resistant to vanishing gradients.
concepts.formula: ReLU(x) = max(0, x)

concepts.name: Softmax
concepts.def: Function turning a vector of scores into probabilities that sum to one; used for multi-class outputs and attention weights.
concepts.formula: softmax(z_i) = exp(z_i) / sum of exp(z_j)

concepts.name: Backpropagation
concepts.def: Algorithm computing the gradient of the loss with respect to every network weight by applying the chain rule backward through the layers (Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams 1986).

concepts.name: Vanishing gradient
concepts.def: Gradients shrinking exponentially as they pass backward through many layers or time steps, stalling learning in early layers. Addressed by ReLU, gated recurrent units and residual connections.

concepts.name: Residual connection
concepts.def: Shortcut that adds a layer's input to its output (He et al. 2015), easing gradient flow and making very deep networks trainable.

concepts.name: Deep learning
concepts.def: Machine learning with many-layered neural networks that learn hierarchical representations from raw data; dominant for images, audio and language.

concepts.name: Representation learning
concepts.def: Learning useful features automatically from raw data instead of engineering them by hand.

concepts.name: Embedding
concepts.def: Dense vector representing an item such as a word, document, company or asset, learned so that similar items sit close together. Used for peer identification and semantic search.

concepts.name: Universal approximation theorem
concepts.def: Result (Cybenko 1989; Hornik 1991) that a network with one hidden layer and enough units can approximate any continuous function on a bounded domain. It says nothing about learning that function from finite data.

concepts.name: Convolutional neural network
concepts.def: Network applying learned filters across local windows with shared weights; efficient for images and also applied to price charts and limit order book snapshots.

concepts.name: Recurrent neural network
concepts.def: Network that processes sequences step by step with a hidden state carrying memory of past inputs. Plain versions struggle with long-range dependencies.

concepts.name: LSTM
concepts.def: Long short-term memory (Hochreiter and Schmidhuber 1997): recurrent unit with gates controlling what to store, forget and output, which eases vanishing gradients over long sequences.

concepts.name: DeepLOB
concepts.def: Deep model of Zhang, Zohren and Roberts (2019) combining convolutions and an LSTM to predict short-term mid-price moves from limit order book data.

concepts.name: Deep hedging
concepts.def: Framework of Buehler, Gonon, Teichmann and Wood (2019) that trains neural networks to hedge derivatives under transaction costs and frictions by directly optimizing a risk measure over simulated paths.

concepts.name: Temporal fusion transformer
concepts.def: Attention-based multi-horizon forecasting model (Lim et al. 2021) combining recurrent layers, variable selection and interpretable attention over time.

concepts.name: Time-series foundation model
concepts.def: Large model pretrained on many time series to forecast unseen series without task-specific training. Its value for financial returns is unproven given their low signal to noise.

concepts.name: Graph neural network
concepts.def: Network that passes messages along graph edges, learning from relationships such as supply chains, ownership links or co-movement networks.

concepts.name: Transfer learning
concepts.def: Reusing a model trained on one task or dataset as the starting point for another, saving data and compute.

concepts.name: Fine-tuning
concepts.def: Continuing the training of a pretrained model on a smaller task-specific dataset to adapt it.

concepts.name: Pretraining
concepts.def: Initial large-scale training of a model on broad data, usually self-supervised, to learn general representations before adapting it to tasks.

concepts.name: Foundation model
concepts.def: Large model pretrained on broad data that can be adapted to many downstream tasks, such as a large language model. Term from Bommasani et al. (2021).

concepts.name: Large language model
concepts.def: Transformer trained on vast amounts of text to predict the next token, which yields broad abilities in writing, reasoning, coding and information extraction.

concepts.name: Next-token prediction
concepts.def: Training objective of predicting each token from the ones before it; the core pretraining task for GPT-style language models.

concepts.name: Transformer
concepts.def: Architecture of Vaswani et al. (2017), "Attention Is All You Need", built on self-attention instead of recurrence, which allows parallel training on long sequences. The basis of modern language models.

concepts.name: Attention mechanism
concepts.def: Method that lets a model weight parts of its input by relevance when producing each output, computed from query, key and value vectors.

concepts.name: Self-attention
concepts.def: Attention in which every position in a sequence attends to every other position, with cost growing with the square of sequence length.
concepts.formula: Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(Q x K^T / sqrt(d)) x V

concepts.name: Positional encoding
concepts.def: Information added to token representations to convey order, since attention alone ignores position; includes sinusoidal and rotary schemes.

concepts.name: Encoder-decoder
concepts.def: Architecture in which an encoder maps the input to representations and a decoder generates output from them; the original transformer design for translation.

concepts.name: Decoder-only model
concepts.def: Transformer that generates text left to right using causal self-attention, the design of GPT-style language models.

concepts.name: BERT
concepts.def: Encoder-only transformer (Devlin et al. 2018) pretrained by predicting masked words, widely fine-tuned for classification and extraction, including financial sentiment.

concepts.name: FinBERT
concepts.def: BERT variant further trained on financial text for tasks such as sentiment classification of news, filings and analyst reports.

concepts.name: Tokenizer
concepts.def: Component that splits text into tokens from a fixed vocabulary, often subword pieces built by byte-pair encoding. Token counts drive model cost and context limits.

concepts.name: Context window
concepts.def: Maximum number of tokens a model can process in one call, covering prompt and output. Longer windows raise memory and compute cost per request.

concepts.name: KV cache
concepts.def: Stored key and value vectors for past tokens so a transformer need not recompute them for each new token. It grows with context length and batch size and often binds inference memory.

concepts.name: Scaling laws
concepts.def: Empirical power-law relationships between model loss and parameters, data and compute (Kaplan et al. 2020), used to plan the size of training runs.

concepts.name: Chinchilla scaling
concepts.def: Hoffmann et al. (2022) found that compute-optimal training grows parameters and training tokens in roughly equal proportion, implying many earlier models were undertrained.

concepts.name: In-context learning
concepts.def: A model performing a new task from instructions or examples in its prompt, without any change to its weights.

concepts.name: Few-shot prompting
concepts.def: Including a few worked examples in a prompt to show the desired task and format; zero-shot prompting gives instructions only.

concepts.name: Prompt engineering
concepts.def: Designing instructions, context and examples so that a model produces reliable output.

concepts.name: Chain of thought
concepts.def: Prompting or training a model to write intermediate reasoning steps before its answer, which improves multi-step problem solving (Wei et al. 2022).

concepts.name: Reasoning model
concepts.def: Language model trained, often with reinforcement learning, to generate extended reasoning before answering, trading more inference tokens for accuracy on hard problems.

concepts.name: Test-time compute
concepts.def: Spending more computation at inference, through longer reasoning, repeated sampling or search, to improve answers. Shifts compute demand from training toward inference.

concepts.name: Post-training
concepts.def: Everything after pretraining that shapes a model's behavior: supervised fine-tuning, preference optimization and reinforcement learning.

concepts.name: Supervised fine-tuning
concepts.def: Post-training a pretrained model on curated prompt and response pairs to teach it to follow instructions.

concepts.name: RLHF
concepts.def: Reinforcement learning from human feedback: train a reward model on human preference comparisons, then optimize the language model against that reward.

concepts.name: Reward model
concepts.def: Model trained to score outputs by predicted human or rule-based preference, used as the optimization target in RLHF.

concepts.name: RL with verifiable rewards
concepts.def: Training models with reinforcement learning on tasks whose answers can be checked automatically, such as math or code tests, avoiding a learned reward model.

concepts.name: LoRA
concepts.def: Low-rank adaptation (Hu et al. 2021): fine-tuning by learning small low-rank update matrices while freezing the original weights, cutting memory and storage needs.

concepts.name: Quantization
concepts.def: Representing weights and activations with fewer bits, such as 8 or 4, to cut memory use and speed up inference at some cost in accuracy.

concepts.name: Knowledge distillation
concepts.def: Training a smaller student model to imitate a larger teacher's outputs, keeping much of the capability at lower inference cost (Hinton et al. 2015).

concepts.name: Mixture of experts
concepts.def: Architecture that routes each token to a few of many expert subnetworks, so total parameters grow without a matching rise in compute per token.

concepts.name: FlashAttention
concepts.def: Attention algorithm (Dao et al. 2022) that reorders the computation to minimize reads and writes to slow memory, speeding training and inference with exact results.

concepts.name: Hallucination
concepts.def: A language model stating false or fabricated information fluently, such as invented figures or citations. A core risk when using models for investment research.

concepts.name: Retrieval-augmented generation
concepts.def: Supplying a model with documents retrieved from a search index at query time so its answers are grounded in specific sources.

concepts.name: Vector database
concepts.def: Store that indexes embeddings for fast nearest-neighbor similarity search; underlies retrieval-augmented generation.

concepts.name: Sampling temperature
concepts.def: Parameter scaling a model's output probabilities before sampling. Low values make output near-deterministic; high values make it more varied.

concepts.name: Perplexity
concepts.def: Exponential of the average negative log likelihood per token; lower values mean the model predicts the text better.
concepts.formula: PPL = exp(average negative log likelihood per token)

concepts.name: AI benchmarks
concepts.def: Standardized test sets for comparing models on a capability such as coding or math. Contamination of training data and saturation limit what scores mean.

concepts.name: Benchmark saturation
concepts.def: When top models score near the ceiling of a benchmark, so it no longer separates them and new tests are needed.

concepts.name: Multimodal model
concepts.def: Model that takes in or produces several data types, such as text, images, audio and charts.

concepts.name: Diffusion model
concepts.def: Generative model that learns to reverse a gradual noising process, producing images, audio or video by iterative denoising.

concepts.name: Text as data
concepts.def: Treating documents such as filings, transcripts and news as quantitative inputs through word counts, dictionaries, embeddings or language models; surveyed by Gentzkow, Kelly and Taddy (2019).

concepts.name: Bag of words
concepts.def: Representing a document by its word counts, ignoring order. Simple and transparent; the basis of dictionary sentiment methods.

concepts.name: TF-IDF
concepts.def: Term frequency times inverse document frequency: weights words that are frequent in a document but rare across the collection.
concepts.formula: tfidf = tf x ln(N / df)

concepts.name: Loughran-McDonald dictionary
concepts.def: Finance-specific sentiment word lists of Loughran and McDonald (2011), built because general dictionaries misclassify words such as liability, tax or cost as negative in financial text.

concepts.name: Financial sentiment analysis
concepts.def: Scoring the tone of financial text, such as news, filings or calls, with dictionaries, classifiers or language models to predict returns, volatility or flows.

concepts.name: Word2vec
concepts.def: Method of Mikolov et al. (2013) that learns word embeddings by predicting words from their neighbors, so related words get nearby vectors.

concepts.name: Topic model
concepts.def: Unsupervised method, classically latent Dirichlet allocation (Blei, Ng and Jordan 2003), describing each document as a mixture of topics.

concepts.name: Named entity recognition
concepts.def: Extracting and classifying names of companies, people, places and amounts from text; a first step in mapping news to tickers.

concepts.name: Lazy prices
concepts.def: Cohen, Malloy and Nguyen (2020): firms whose annual report text changes notably from the prior year subsequently underperform, as investors underreact to the changes.

concepts.name: Markov decision process
concepts.def: Framework of states, actions, transition probabilities, rewards and a discount factor that formalizes sequential decisions; the foundation of reinforcement learning.

concepts.name: Bellman equation
concepts.def: Recursive condition that a state's value equals the best immediate reward plus the discounted expected value of the next state; the basis of dynamic programming.
concepts.formula: V(s) = max over a of [r(s, a) + gamma x E V(s')]

concepts.name: Policy (reinforcement learning)
concepts.def: A rule mapping states to actions, deterministic or random, that a reinforcement learning agent learns in order to maximize expected cumulative reward.

concepts.name: Value function
concepts.def: Expected cumulative discounted reward from a state, or from a state-action pair, when following a given policy.

concepts.name: Q-learning
concepts.def: Off-policy algorithm (Watkins 1989) that learns the value of each state-action pair from experience through repeated Bellman updates.

concepts.name: Deep Q-network
concepts.def: Q-learning with a neural network approximating action values, stabilized by experience replay and target networks (Mnih et al. 2015).

concepts.name: Policy gradient
concepts.def: Reinforcement learning methods that adjust policy parameters directly in the direction that raises expected reward.

concepts.name: Actor-critic
concepts.def: Architecture in which an actor chooses actions and a critic estimates value, reducing the variance of policy updates.

concepts.name: Proximal policy optimization
concepts.def: Policy gradient method of Schulman et al. (2017) that limits the size of each update with a clipped objective; widely used, including in RLHF.

concepts.name: Exploration-exploitation trade-off
concepts.def: Balancing trying actions to learn their value against choosing the best-known action; central to bandits and reinforcement learning.

concepts.name: Multi-armed bandit
concepts.def: Problem of repeatedly choosing among options with unknown payoffs to maximize total reward; the simplest exploration-exploitation setting.

concepts.name: Thompson sampling
concepts.def: Bandit strategy that draws from each option's posterior payoff distribution and picks the option with the best draw (Thompson 1933).

concepts.name: Reward hacking
concepts.def: An agent maximizing the measured reward in unintended ways, such as a trading agent exploiting simulator flaws or a model gaming its reward model.

concepts.name: Reward shaping
concepts.def: Designing intermediate rewards to guide learning. For trading agents, choices such as risk penalties and cost charges largely determine behavior.

concepts.name: Discount factor (reinforcement learning)
concepts.def: Weight between 0 and 1 applied to future rewards; lower values make an agent short-sighted.

concepts.name: Offline reinforcement learning
concepts.def: Learning a policy from a fixed log of past data without interacting with the environment, the realistic setting for trading. Fails when the policy favors actions rarely seen in the data.

concepts.name: Market simulator
concepts.def: Synthetic environment, such as an order book model or agent-based model, used to train and test trading agents. Agents readily exploit unrealistic features such as missing market impact.

concepts.name: Agent-based model
concepts.def: Simulation of many interacting agents following rules, used to study emergent market behavior such as bubbles, herding and crashes.

concepts.name: Sim-to-real gap
concepts.def: Performance lost when a policy trained in simulation meets the real market, because of unmodeled impact, latency and other traders' reactions.

concepts.name: Reinforcement learning for execution
concepts.def: Applying reinforcement learning to slice large orders over time to minimize implementation shortfall, an approach studied by Nevmyvaka, Feng and Kearns (2006).

concepts.name: Feature engineering
concepts.def: Transforming raw data into predictive inputs, such as ratios, changes, ranks and interactions. In finance, domain-driven features usually matter more than the choice of model.

concepts.name: Log returns
concepts.def: Natural log of the price relative. Log returns add up over time and roughly equal simple returns for small moves, but do not add across assets in a portfolio.
concepts.formula: r = ln(P_t / P_t-1)

concepts.name: Cross-sectional ranking
concepts.def: Converting a feature to its rank or percentile among assets each period, which removes scale, outliers and market-wide shifts.

concepts.name: Standardization (z-score)
concepts.def: Rescaling a feature to mean zero and unit variance using only statistics available at the time of each observation.
concepts.formula: z = (x - mean) / standard deviation

concepts.name: Lagged features
concepts.def: Past values of a variable used as predictors, lagged far enough that they were truly available at decision time.

concepts.name: Rolling-window features
concepts.def: Statistics computed over trailing windows, such as 20-day volatility or 12-month momentum. Each window must end before the prediction time.

concepts.name: Volatility-scaled returns
concepts.def: Returns divided by a recent volatility estimate, making signals and targets comparable across assets and regimes.

concepts.name: Sector neutralization
concepts.def: Removing sector averages from a feature or signal so predictions reflect differences within sectors rather than sector bets.

concepts.name: Factor neutralization
concepts.def: Regressing a signal on known factor exposures and keeping the residual, isolating information not already captured by common factors.

concepts.name: Residual returns
concepts.def: Returns left after removing exposure to the market and other factors; a common prediction target for stock selection models.

concepts.name: Forward return target
concepts.def: The future return over a chosen horizon used as the training label. Choices of horizon, price adjustment and benchmark shape what the model learns.

concepts.name: Calendar features
concepts.def: Inputs derived from dates, such as day of week, month-end, option expiry or holiday proximity.

concepts.name: Target encoding
concepts.def: Replacing a category with the average target value observed for that category. It leaks unless computed out-of-fold.

concepts.name: Missing data imputation
concepts.def: Filling gaps in data by forward fill, medians or models. It must use only past information and should flag that a value was missing.

concepts.name: Trade signing
concepts.def: Classifying trades as buyer- or seller-initiated, using exchange aggressor flags or rules such as Lee and Ready (1991) when flags are missing.

concepts.name: Realized variance
concepts.def: Sum of squared intraday returns over a period, a model-free estimate of variance. Microstructure noise biases it at very high sampling frequencies.
concepts.formula: RV = sum of r_i^2

concepts.name: Firm characteristics panel
concepts.def: Panel of stock-level characteristics such as size, value, momentum, profitability and accruals, standardized each month; the standard input for cross-sectional return models.

concepts.name: Signal turnover
concepts.def: How much a signal's implied portfolio changes each rebalance. High turnover needs a larger predictive edge to overcome trading costs.

concepts.name: Alpha signal
concepts.def: A quantitative forecast of relative or absolute returns used to set positions.

concepts.name: Regime features
concepts.def: Inputs describing the market state, such as volatility level, trend or credit spreads, which let models condition on the environment.

concepts.name: Feature store
concepts.def: System that stores computed features with timestamps for reuse in training and live serving, keeping definitions identical and point-in-time correct in both.

concepts.name: Satellite imagery
concepts.def: Images from satellites used to count cars in parking lots, gauge crop health, read oil tank levels or track construction before official data appear.

concepts.name: Geolocation data
concepts.def: Anonymized mobile device location data used to estimate foot traffic at stores, factories or venues.

concepts.name: Card transaction data
concepts.def: Aggregated credit card, debit card or bank transaction data used to estimate company sales ahead of reported results.
concepts.aliases: credit card data,card spend data,consumer transaction data

concepts.name: Email receipt data
concepts.def: Purchase data parsed from consumer email receipts by opted-in panels, giving item-level detail on online spending.

concepts.name: Web scraping
concepts.def: Automated collection of public web data, such as prices, product listings, job postings or reviews. Raises terms-of-service and legal questions.

concepts.name: Web traffic data
concepts.def: Panel or clickstream estimates of site visits, downloads and active users, used as proxies for engagement and demand at internet companies.

concepts.name: Job postings data
concepts.def: Scraped or aggregated hiring listings that show where companies are expanding, cutting or shifting strategy.

concepts.name: Social media sentiment
concepts.def: Measures of attention and tone from social platforms and forums, linked to retail flows, meme stocks and short-term volatility.

concepts.name: News analytics
concepts.def: Machine-readable news feeds tagged with entities, topics, novelty and sentiment, timestamped for trading use.

concepts.name: Ship tracking data
concepts.def: Automatic identification system (AIS) transponder data on vessel positions, used to track oil exports, commodity flows and port congestion.

concepts.name: Online pricing data
concepts.def: Scraped online prices of goods across retailers, used to measure inflation in real time and to judge company pricing power.

concepts.name: Search trends
concepts.def: Volume of internet search queries for chosen terms, a proxy for consumer interest, investor attention and labor market stress.

concepts.name: Supply chain data
concepts.def: Data mapping customers, suppliers and shipments between firms. Cohen and Frazzini (2008) showed news propagates along customer-supplier links with a lag.

concepts.name: ESG data
concepts.def: Environmental, social and governance scores and inputs from data vendors. Ratings for the same company often disagree widely across providers.

concepts.name: Weather data
concepts.def: Observations and forecasts of temperature, precipitation and storms, which drive energy demand, crop yields and retail traffic.

concepts.name: Patent data
concepts.def: Patent filings and citations used to measure innovation output and technology positioning.

concepts.name: Securities lending data
concepts.def: Data on shares on loan, borrow fees and lendable supply utilization, signaling short-seller demand and squeeze risk.

concepts.name: KPI prediction
concepts.def: Using alternative data to forecast company-reported operating metrics, such as revenue, subscribers or same-store sales, and trading the expected surprise versus consensus.

concepts.name: Panel bias
concepts.def: Distortion when an alternative data panel, such as card users or app installs, does not represent the target population or changes composition over time.

concepts.name: Material nonpublic information
concepts.def: Information a reasonable investor would consider important that has not been publicly disclosed. Trading on it is illegal insider trading, so data vendors must show their data contain none.

concepts.name: Alternative data due diligence
concepts.def: Vetting a dataset's sourcing, consent, licensing, MNPI risk, history length, coverage and point-in-time integrity before buying or using it.

concepts.name: Data provenance
concepts.def: Record of where data came from and how they were collected and transformed; needed for legal compliance and for trusting a signal.

concepts.name: Data licensing
concepts.def: Contract terms governing who may use data, for which purposes, and whether redistribution, derived works or exclusivity are allowed.

concepts.name: Data privacy
concepts.def: Protection of personal information in datasets through consent, anonymization and aggregation, governed by laws such as GDPR and CCPA.

concepts.name: Data exclusivity
concepts.def: Licensing a dataset to one or a few buyers to preserve its edge. Widely sold data decay faster as their signal is traded away.

concepts.name: Alternative data decay
concepts.def: Loss of a dataset's predictive value as more buyers adopt it, its panel changes, or companies learn to manage the measured metric.

concepts.name: Training compute
concepts.def: Total floating point operations used to train a model. For a dense transformer it is roughly six times parameters times training tokens.
concepts.formula: C = 6 x N x D (N parameters, D tokens)

concepts.name: FLOPs and FLOP/s
concepts.def: Floating point operations, the unit of compute work, and FLOP/s, the rate a chip performs them. A job's total FLOPs differs from a chip's peak FLOP/s, which real workloads rarely reach.

concepts.name: Model FLOPs utilization
concepts.def: Share of a cluster's peak compute actually spent on useful model math. Communication, memory stalls and failures keep it well below 100 percent in large training runs.
concepts.formula: MFU = achieved model FLOP/s / peak FLOP/s

concepts.name: Compute-optimal training
concepts.def: Choosing model size and number of training tokens to minimize loss for a fixed compute budget.

concepts.name: Overtraining (inference-optimal)
concepts.def: Training a smaller model on more tokens than compute-optimal, spending more on training to cut the lifetime cost of serving it.

concepts.name: Data parallelism
concepts.def: Splitting each batch across many devices that each hold a full model copy, then averaging their gradients. Gradient exchange makes network bandwidth critical.

concepts.name: Model parallelism
concepts.def: Splitting one model across devices, by dividing layer matrices (tensor parallelism) or assigning layers to stages (pipeline parallelism). Tensor parallelism needs the fastest interconnects.

concepts.name: Synthetic data
concepts.def: Artificially generated data from simulations or models, used to augment scarce real data or to train language models. Risks include mismatch with reality and degraded models when trained on their own output.

concepts.name: Data wall
concepts.def: The concern that the stock of high-quality human text for pretraining is finite and being used up, shifting effort toward synthetic data, other modalities and reinforcement learning.

concepts.name: Frontier model
concepts.def: The most capable models at a given time, trained at the largest compute scale by a few labs.
concepts.aliases: frontier ai,state of the art model

concepts.name: Open-weight model
concepts.def: Model whose trained parameters are published for anyone to run and modify, though training data and code may stay private. Puts pressure on the pricing of closed models.

concepts.name: Closed model
concepts.def: Model available only through its provider's API or apps, with weights kept private.

concepts.name: Small language model
concepts.def: Compact model, often distilled from a larger one, cheap enough to run on modest hardware or devices for narrower tasks.

concepts.name: On-device AI
concepts.def: Running models locally on phones, PCs or vehicles instead of in data centers, cutting latency and serving cost but limited by device memory and power.

concepts.name: Neural processing unit
concepts.def: Accelerator block for AI workloads built into phones and PCs, used for on-device inference.

concepts.name: Inference cost
concepts.def: Cost of serving model outputs, driven by model size, tokens processed, hardware price, utilization and batching. The main variable cost of AI products.

concepts.name: Prefill
concepts.def: Inference phase that processes the whole prompt in parallel to build the KV cache; it is limited mainly by compute.

concepts.name: Decode
concepts.def: Inference phase that generates output tokens one at a time, each step reading the full weights and KV cache; it is limited mainly by memory bandwidth.

concepts.name: Time to first token
concepts.def: Latency from sending a request to receiving the first output token, dominated by queueing and prefill.

concepts.name: Tokens per second
concepts.def: Throughput of generated tokens, per user or per system. Larger batches raise system throughput but slow each user.

concepts.name: Continuous batching
concepts.def: Serving technique that adds and removes requests from a running batch at every decoding step, raising accelerator utilization.

concepts.name: Speculative decoding
concepts.def: Using a small draft model to propose several tokens that the large model checks in one pass, speeding generation without changing the output distribution.

concepts.name: GPU utilization
concepts.def: Share of time or capacity that accelerators spend on useful work. Low utilization inflates the effective cost of each unit of compute.

concepts.name: CUDA ecosystem
concepts.def: Nvidia's CUDA programming platform, libraries and developer base, which raise switching costs for customers considering rival accelerators.

concepts.name: Tensor processing unit
concepts.def: Google's custom AI accelerator built around large matrix multiply units, used internally and rented through its cloud.

concepts.name: ASIC
concepts.def: Application-specific integrated circuit: a chip designed for one workload, trading flexibility for efficiency. Custom AI accelerators are ASICs.

concepts.name: FPGA
concepts.def: Field-programmable gate array: chip whose logic can be reconfigured after manufacture; used for ultra-low-latency trading, networking and prototyping.

concepts.name: Tensor core
concepts.def: Specialized GPU circuitry for fast matrix multiply-accumulate at reduced precision; the source of most AI throughput on modern GPUs.

concepts.name: Numerical precision
concepts.def: Bit width used to represent numbers, such as FP32, BF16, FP8 or FP4. Lower precision raises throughput and cuts memory at some risk to accuracy.

concepts.name: Memory wall
concepts.def: The widening gap between processor compute speed and memory bandwidth, which leaves many AI workloads waiting for data rather than doing math.

concepts.name: Memory bandwidth
concepts.def: Rate at which data move between memory and processor, in bytes per second. It sets the ceiling on token generation speed for large models.

concepts.name: Arithmetic intensity
concepts.def: Operations performed per byte moved from memory. Low-intensity workloads are memory bound and high-intensity ones compute bound, as shown by the roofline model.
concepts.formula: intensity = FLOPs / bytes moved

concepts.name: Rack-scale system
concepts.def: Servers designed as a whole rack, with many GPUs joined by a high-speed fabric into one large scale-up domain; requires liquid cooling and very high power per rack.

concepts.name: Scale-up versus scale-out
concepts.def: Scale-up links accelerators into one tightly coupled domain with very high bandwidth; scale-out joins many such domains over a network fabric with lower bandwidth per chip.
concepts.aliases: scale up,scale out,front end versus back end network

concepts.name: NVLink
concepts.def: Nvidia's high-bandwidth GPU-to-GPU interconnect for scale-up domains, much faster than standard PCIe links.

concepts.name: AI networking
concepts.def: Networks linking accelerators in AI clusters. Collective exchange of gradients and activations makes network bandwidth and latency a key determinant of cluster efficiency.

concepts.name: InfiniBand
concepts.def: Low-latency, high-bandwidth network standard with native remote direct memory access, long dominant in AI training clusters.

concepts.name: Ethernet for AI
concepts.def: Ethernet enhanced with congestion control and remote direct memory access for AI clusters, competing with InfiniBand for scale-out fabrics.

concepts.name: Optical transceiver
concepts.def: Module converting electrical signals to light and back for fiber links between switches and servers. Volumes scale with cluster size and link speed.

concepts.name: Co-packaged optics
concepts.def: Placing optical engines in the same package as a switch or processor chip, cutting the power used to drive signals compared with pluggable transceivers.

concepts.name: GPU rental pricing
concepts.def: Hourly price of renting accelerator capacity, on demand or under reserved contracts. Falling rates signal easing scarcity and pressure the value of GPU fleets.
concepts.aliases: gpu hour,gpu rental rates,price per gpu hour

concepts.name: GPU depreciation
concepts.def: The accounting useful life assigned to AI servers. Longer lives lift reported earnings, while rapid generational gains may shorten real economic life.

concepts.name: GPU-backed lending
concepts.def: Debt secured by GPU fleets and their rental contracts, used by neoclouds. Credit risk depends on residual values and the quality of the customer contracts.

concepts.name: Compute contract
concepts.def: Multi-year agreement to buy cloud or GPU capacity, often take-or-pay, creating backlog for the provider and fixed commitments for the buyer.

concepts.name: Take-or-pay contract
concepts.def: Contract obliging the buyer to pay for a committed quantity whether or not it uses it; common in compute, power and energy deals.

concepts.name: AI chip export controls
concepts.def: Government restrictions on exporting advanced AI chips, chipmaking tools and related technology to certain countries, reshaping demand, supply chains and product design.

concepts.name: DRAM
concepts.def: Dynamic random-access memory: the main working memory in computers, storing bits as charge that must be refreshed. A cyclical commodity market with few producers.

concepts.name: NAND flash
concepts.def: Non-volatile memory that keeps data without power, used in solid-state drives; more commoditized and cyclical than DRAM.

concepts.name: Memory pricing cycle
concepts.def: Boom-bust swings in DRAM and NAND prices as capacity additions lag demand shifts, moving producers' margins sharply.

concepts.name: HBM stacking
concepts.def: Stacking DRAM dies vertically, linked by through-silicon vias, and placing the stack beside the processor on an interposer for very wide bandwidth. HBM uses more wafer area per bit than standard DRAM.

concepts.name: Fabless chip company
concepts.def: Chip company that designs chips but outsources manufacturing to foundries, unlike an integrated device manufacturer, which designs and makes its own.

concepts.name: EUV lithography
concepts.def: Extreme ultraviolet lithography, which uses very short wavelength light to print the finest chip features. The tools come from a single supplier, ASML.

concepts.name: Chip yield
concepts.def: Share of dies on a wafer that work. It falls with larger die size and immature processes, raising the cost per good chip.

concepts.name: Reticle limit
concepts.def: Maximum die area a lithography tool can print in one exposure, which caps the size of a single chip and motivates chiplets and advanced packaging.

concepts.name: Chiplet
concepts.def: Small die combined with others in one package to form a larger processor, improving yield and allowing parts made on different nodes to be mixed.

concepts.name: Advanced packaging
concepts.def: Techniques that connect multiple dies densely within one package, such as 2.5D interposers and 3D stacking; a recurring bottleneck for AI accelerator supply.

concepts.name: CoWoS
concepts.def: Chip-on-wafer-on-substrate: TSMC's 2.5D packaging that places logic dies and HBM stacks side by side on a silicon interposer. Its capacity has constrained AI accelerator output.

concepts.name: 3D chip stacking
concepts.def: Stacking dies on top of each other with vertical connections, increasingly made by hybrid copper bonding, to shorten wires and raise bandwidth.

concepts.name: EDA software
concepts.def: Electronic design automation tools used to design and verify chips; a concentrated market with high switching costs.

concepts.name: Foundry concentration risk
concepts.def: Concentration of leading-edge chip fabrication in one company and one geography, a supply and geopolitical risk for the whole AI industry.

concepts.name: Colocation
concepts.def: Data center model in which a provider leases space, power and cooling to tenants who install their own equipment, priced per kilowatt per month.

concepts.name: Critical IT load
concepts.def: Power available to IT equipment, the standard measure of data center capacity in megawatts, excluding cooling and other overhead.

concepts.name: Power usage effectiveness
concepts.def: Total facility power divided by IT equipment power; a value of 1.0 would mean zero overhead for cooling and power conversion.
concepts.formula: PUE = total facility energy / IT equipment energy

concepts.name: Rack power density
concepts.def: Power drawn per server rack in kilowatts. AI racks draw many times more than conventional racks, forcing liquid cooling and heavier electrical design.

concepts.name: Liquid cooling
concepts.def: Removing server heat with liquid instead of air, needed for dense AI racks. Direct-to-chip cold plates are the main form; immersion in fluid is an alternative.

concepts.name: Grid interconnection
concepts.def: Process and queue for connecting new loads or generators to the power grid. Long waits make power access the main constraint on data center timing.

concepts.name: Behind-the-meter power
concepts.def: Electricity generated on site, often by gas turbines or engines, and used directly without passing through the utility grid, letting data centers bypass interconnection delays.

concepts.name: Power purchase agreement
concepts.def: Long-term contract to buy electricity from a specific generator at agreed prices, used by hyperscalers to secure clean or firm power.

concepts.name: Small modular reactor
concepts.def: Factory-built nuclear reactor of smaller size, proposed as firm carbon-free power for data centers; commercial deployment is still at an early stage.

concepts.name: Electrical equipment shortage
concepts.def: Long lead times for transformers, switchgear and turbines as data center and grid demand outruns manufacturing capacity.

concepts.name: Flexible data center load
concepts.def: Data centers agreeing to cut consumption during grid stress in exchange for faster connection or lower costs; training jobs tolerate this better than live inference.

concepts.name: Powered land
concepts.def: Sites with secured power capacity and zoning for data centers, valued for how quickly they can be energized.

concepts.name: Stranded asset risk
concepts.def: Risk that data centers or GPU fleets lose value before paying back their cost because demand falls short or technology moves on.

concepts.name: Depreciation drag
concepts.def: Future depreciation expense created by heavy current capex, which weighs on margins over the useful life of the assets.

concepts.name: AI overbuild risk
concepts.def: Risk that total AI infrastructure investment exceeds sustainable demand, as in past railway and telecom build-outs, leading to overcapacity, price collapse and write-downs.

concepts.name: Data center JV financing
concepts.def: Off-balance-sheet structures, such as joint ventures and special purpose vehicles funded by private capital, that build data centers leased back to a hyperscaler.
concepts.aliases: spv financing,build to suit,data center joint venture

concepts.name: Jevons paradox
concepts.def: Jevons (1865): efficiency gains that cut the cost of using a resource can increase its total consumption. Applied to AI, cheaper tokens may raise total compute demand.

concepts.name: AI stack
concepts.def: Layers of the AI industry: chips and equipment, infrastructure and cloud, models, and applications, each with different margins and sources of advantage.

concepts.name: Wrapper company
concepts.def: Business whose product is a thin layer over a third-party model, exposed to its supplier's pricing and to rivals with the same access.

concepts.name: Picks and shovels
concepts.def: Investing in suppliers to a boom, such as chips, equipment and power, rather than betting on which end users will win.

concepts.name: API pricing
concepts.def: Charging developers per token processed by a model, with separate rates for input and output and discounts for caching and batch jobs.

concepts.name: Cost per token
concepts.def: Price or cost for each unit of model input or output, usually quoted per million tokens.

concepts.name: Input versus output token pricing
concepts.def: Output tokens cost more than input tokens because generation is sequential and memory bound, while prompt tokens are processed in parallel.

concepts.name: Prompt caching
concepts.def: Reusing the processed form of repeated prompt prefixes across requests at a discount, cutting cost and latency for long shared context.

concepts.name: Reasoning tokens
concepts.def: Tokens a reasoning model generates while thinking before its answer, billed as output and raising the cost per task.

concepts.name: Token price deflation
concepts.def: Rapid fall in the price per token for a given level of capability, driven by better hardware, software efficiency and competition.

concepts.name: Model commoditization
concepts.def: Erosion of pricing power as many models reach similar capability, shifting value toward distribution, proprietary data and cost.

concepts.name: Seat-based pricing
concepts.def: Charging per user per month, the traditional software model, which AI agents threaten if they reduce the number of human users needed.

concepts.name: Seat compression
concepts.def: Fall in the number of software licenses customers need when AI automates work, pressuring seat-based software revenue.

concepts.name: AI gross margin
concepts.def: Gross margin of AI products after inference compute costs; typically below classic software margins because every use consumes compute.

concepts.name: Annualized run-rate revenue
