concepts.def: Recent monthly or weekly revenue scaled to a yearly figure; common for fast-growing AI firms but flattering when usage is volatile or one-off.
concepts.formula: run-rate = monthly revenue x 12

concepts.name: Model routing
concepts.def: Directing each request to the cheapest model able to handle it, lowering cost and reducing dependence on any one provider.

concepts.name: Cloud-lab partnership
concepts.def: Arrangement in which a model lab receives compute and investment from a cloud provider, which resells the lab's models and captures its compute spending.

concepts.name: AI agent
concepts.def: System in which a language model plans, calls tools and takes multi-step actions toward a goal with limited human direction.

concepts.name: Tool use
concepts.def: A model emitting structured calls to external functions, such as search, code execution or databases, and using the results in its answer.

concepts.name: Model Context Protocol
concepts.def: Open protocol introduced by Anthropic in 2024 that standardizes how AI applications connect models to tools and data sources.

concepts.name: Computer-use agent
concepts.def: Agent that operates a computer through screenshots, clicks and typing, letting it use software that has no API.

concepts.name: Coding agent
concepts.def: Agent that reads, writes, runs and tests code in a repository; one of the first agent categories with heavy real usage.

concepts.name: Human in the loop
concepts.def: Design requiring human review or approval at key steps, trading speed for control over errors and risk.

concepts.name: Prompt injection
concepts.def: Attack in which instructions hidden in content an AI reads, such as a web page or document, hijack its behavior.

concepts.name: Task horizon
concepts.def: Length of task, measured in the time a person would need, that an agent can complete reliably. Longer horizons multiply the chances of compounding errors.

concepts.name: Compounding error
concepts.def: When each step of a multi-step task has some chance of failure, overall success falls geometrically with the number of steps.
concepts.formula: P(success) = p^n for n independent steps each succeeding with probability p

concepts.name: Market data feed
concepts.def: Stream of quotes, trades and status messages from a venue or vendor. Feeds differ in depth, latency, normalization and cost.

concepts.name: Direct exchange feed
concepts.def: Proprietary data feed from an exchange, faster and deeper than the consolidated feed, used by latency-sensitive traders.

concepts.name: Market by price (Level 2)
concepts.def: Feed showing aggregate resting size at each price level on each side, without individual orders.

concepts.name: Market by order (Level 3)
concepts.def: Full order-level feed of every add, modify, cancel and execution, allowing exact rebuilding of the book and queue positions.

concepts.name: Tick data
concepts.def: Record of every individual trade and quote update, the most granular historical market data. Trade and quote (TAQ) datasets are the standard source for US equities research.

concepts.name: OHLCV bars
concepts.def: Open, high, low, close and volume aggregated over intervals. Compact, but discards the sequence of prices within each bar, so stop and limit fills inside a bar are ambiguous.

concepts.name: Feed handler
concepts.def: Software that receives raw venue messages, decodes the protocol, rebuilds the order book and passes normalized data to applications.

concepts.name: Exchange binary protocol
concepts.def: Compact binary message formats used by exchange feeds, such as Nasdaq ITCH, which feed handlers decode for speed.

concepts.name: Multicast distribution
concepts.def: Network method sending one stream to many subscribers at once. Exchanges broadcast feeds this way, so dropped packets must be recovered separately.

concepts.name: Gap detection and recovery
concepts.def: Detecting missing messages through sequence numbers and recovering them from retransmission or snapshot channels before the book is trusted again.

concepts.name: Snapshot and incremental updates
concepts.def: Feeds combine periodic full-book snapshots with incremental updates; a consumer starts from a snapshot and applies the changes in sequence.

concepts.name: Conflation
concepts.def: Combining rapid updates into fewer messages that carry only the latest state per interval; saves bandwidth but hides intermediate prices.

concepts.name: Normalized market data
concepts.def: Data from many venues converted into one common schema and symbology, easier to use at some cost in latency and venue-specific detail.

concepts.name: Market data fees
concepts.def: Charges by exchanges and vendors for real-time and historical data, with separate fees for display, non-display algorithmic use and redistribution.

concepts.name: Official closing price
concepts.def: Closing price set by a venue's closing auction, used for index levels, fund valuation and benchmarks; it can differ from the last trade.

concepts.name: Options chain data
concepts.def: All listed strikes and expiries for an underlying, with quotes, volume, open interest and implied volatilities.

concepts.name: Roll adjustment
concepts.def: Adjusting a continuous futures series at each roll by adding the price gap (back-adjusted) or multiplying by a ratio, removing artificial jumps between contracts. Roll timing follows calendar, volume or open interest rules.

concepts.name: Security master
concepts.def: Central database of each instrument's identifiers, attributes and history; the backbone that joins data across sources.

concepts.name: Symbology
concepts.def: System of instrument identifiers, such as tickers, CUSIP, ISIN, SEDOL, FIGI and vendor codes, and the mapping among them over time.

concepts.name: Ticker change
concepts.def: Change in a security's trading symbol from a rename, merger or relisting. Tickers are reused over time, so they are unsafe as permanent keys.

concepts.name: Permanent identifier
concepts.def: Identifier that stays fixed for a security across name and ticker changes, such as CRSP's PERMNO, used to link price histories correctly.

concepts.name: Entity resolution
concepts.def: Matching records that refer to the same company or instrument across datasets with differing names and identifiers.

concepts.name: Corporate actions
concepts.def: Company events that change share count, price or security identity, such as splits, dividends, spin-offs, mergers, rights issues and name changes. Price histories must be adjusted for them.

concepts.name: Adjustment factor
concepts.def: Cumulative multiplier applied to historical prices and volumes to account for splits and distributions, making returns continuous.
concepts.formula: adjusted price = raw price x cumulative adjustment factor

concepts.name: Adjusted prices
concepts.def: Historical prices rescaled for splits and often dividends. Adjusted levels change whenever new actions occur, so raw prices and factors should be stored separately.

concepts.name: Total return index
concepts.def: Price series that assumes dividends and distributions are reinvested; the correct basis for comparing long-horizon performance.

concepts.name: Delisting return
concepts.def: Return on a stock's final delisting event. Shumway (1997) showed that omitting these returns biases backtests upward, especially for small stocks delisted for poor performance.

concepts.name: Survivorship-free data
concepts.def: Dataset that includes securities that later delisted, merged or failed, so backtests see the universe as it actually was.

concepts.name: Index constituent history
concepts.def: Dated record of which securities belonged to an index and when. Using today's members for past periods builds survivorship into the universe.

concepts.name: Universe selection
concepts.def: Choosing which assets a strategy may trade on each date using only information known then, such as past liquidity, price and size filters.

concepts.name: Point-in-time data
concepts.def: Data stored as they were known at each past moment, keeping original values before revisions and the time each became available. Essential for avoiding look-ahead bias.

concepts.name: Bitemporal data
concepts.def: Records carrying two timestamps: when a fact was true and when it was recorded or known, which allows queries of what was known as of any date.

concepts.name: As-of join
concepts.def: Joining each record to the latest record from another table at or before its timestamp; the standard way to align asynchronous data without look-ahead.

concepts.name: Data vintages
concepts.def: Successive published versions of a statistic, such as each estimate of a quarter's GDP, kept so backtests use the value known at the time (as in the ALFRED database).

concepts.name: CRSP
concepts.def: Center for Research in Security Prices: academic database of US stock prices, returns and delistings with permanent identifiers; the standard for survivorship-free equity research.

concepts.name: Compustat
concepts.def: Database of standardized company fundamentals widely used in academic and quantitative research, with point-in-time versions available.

concepts.name: I/B/E/S
concepts.def: Institutional Brokers' Estimate System: database of analyst earnings forecasts and recommendations with their history.

concepts.name: Event timestamp
concepts.def: Time an event happened at its source, such as the exchange matching engine.

concepts.name: Receive timestamp
concepts.def: Time a message reached the consumer's system. Its gap from the event timestamp measures feed latency, and realistic simulations should act on it.

concepts.name: Timestamp alignment
concepts.def: Making sure data from different sources share a clock and time zone and reflect when each value was actually knowable.

concepts.name: Clock synchronization
concepts.def: Keeping system clocks aligned to a reference time using protocols such as NTP or PTP, often with hardware timestamping on network cards; regulators require tight sync for audit trails.

concepts.name: Time zone handling
concepts.def: Storing times in UTC and converting carefully, since daylight saving shifts and differing exchange local times cause silent misalignment.

concepts.name: Trading calendar
concepts.def: Schedule of each venue's trading days, holidays, early closes and session times, needed to compute returns and align markets.

concepts.name: Release calendar
concepts.def: Schedule of data releases and earnings dates with exact times, needed to timestamp when information became public.

concepts.name: Data pipeline
concepts.def: Automated sequence that ingests, validates, transforms and stores data on a schedule to feed research and trading.

concepts.name: Data orchestration
concepts.def: Scheduling and coordinating pipeline tasks as a dependency graph with retries and alerts, using tools such as Airflow or cron.

concepts.name: Idempotency
concepts.def: Property that rerunning a job gives the same result without duplicating data; essential for safe retries and backfills.

concepts.name: Columnar storage
concepts.def: Storing data by column instead of by row, which allows heavy compression and fast scans of a few fields across many rows; Parquet is the common open format.

concepts.name: Time-series database
concepts.def: Database optimized for timestamped data, with fast range queries, as-of joins and compression; kdb+ is the classic one in trading.

concepts.name: Data lake
concepts.def: Low-cost storage of raw data in native formats for later processing, in contrast to a warehouse of cleaned, modeled tables; a lakehouse adds table features on top of the lake.

concepts.name: Data quality checks
concepts.def: Automated tests for completeness, valid ranges, duplicates, staleness and cross-source consistency, run before data reach models.

concepts.name: Bad tick filter
concepts.def: Rules removing erroneous prints, such as trades far from the prevailing quote or later-cancelled trades, from price data.

concepts.name: Data gaps
concepts.def: Missing intervals caused by outages, holidays or vendor problems, which must be told apart from genuine periods of no activity.

concepts.name: Schema drift
concepts.def: Unannounced change in a data source's fields, types or meanings that silently breaks downstream pipelines; data contracts guard against it.

concepts.name: Data lineage
concepts.def: Tracking how each dataset was derived from its sources through each transformation, for debugging and audit.

concepts.name: Data versioning
concepts.def: Keeping immutable snapshots of datasets so any result can be reproduced on the exact data used.

concepts.name: Research-production parity
concepts.def: Ensuring the code and data path used in backtests matches live trading, so that differences in timing, fills or features do not create phantom performance.

concepts.name: Event-driven backtester
concepts.def: Backtest engine that processes market events in time order through the same logic as live trading; more realistic than vectorized backtests for execution-sensitive strategies.

concepts.name: Fill simulation
concepts.def: Modeling which orders would have executed in a backtest and at what price, accounting for queue position, spread and market impact.

concepts.name: Vendor data discrepancy
concepts.def: Differences between vendors' values for the same field, arising from timing, adjustments or methodology; cross-checking sources catches errors.

concepts.name: Crude oil benchmark
concepts.def: A reference crude grade whose assessed or traded price anchors pricing of physical cargoes and derivatives, with other grades priced at a differential to it.

concepts.name: Dubai and Oman crude
concepts.def: Medium sour crude benchmarks used to price Middle East exports to Asia, assessed from Dubai, Oman and related grades.

concepts.name: Dated Brent
concepts.def: Price assessment of physical North Sea cargoes loading in a near forward window, drawn from a basket of North Sea grades plus WTI Midland; the base for pricing most of the world's physical crude.

concepts.name: API gravity
concepts.def: American Petroleum Institute measure of liquid density relative to water; higher API means lighter crude that usually yields more gasoline and diesel per barrel.
concepts.formula: API = 141.5 / specific gravity - 131.5

concepts.name: Sweet and sour crude
concepts.def: Classification of crude by sulfur content: sweet crude is low in sulfur, sour crude is high and costs more to refine, so it usually trades at a discount.

concepts.name: Crude quality differential
concepts.def: Premium or discount of a crude grade versus a benchmark, reflecting density, sulfur, acidity, location, freight and how many refineries can run it.

concepts.name: Light-heavy crude spread
concepts.def: Price gap between light sweet and heavy sour crudes; it widens when heavy supply is plentiful or complex refining capacity is scarce, and narrows when heavy barrels are cut.
concepts.aliases: light heavy spread,sweet sour spread,heavy differential

concepts.name: Western Canadian Select
concepts.def: Heavy sour Canadian crude blend priced at a differential to WTI; the discount tracks pipeline and rail takeaway capacity out of Alberta and heavy refining demand on the US Gulf Coast.

concepts.name: Cushing hub
concepts.def: Pipeline and storage hub in Cushing, Oklahoma that is the delivery point for NYMEX WTI futures; tank levels there strongly influence WTI time spreads.

concepts.name: Commodity calendar spread
concepts.def: Price difference between two delivery months of the same commodity futures; a positive near-minus-far spread signals backwardation and a negative one signals contango.
concepts.formula: spread = near-month price - later-month price

concepts.name: Refining margin
concepts.def: Value of products a refinery makes from a barrel minus the crude cost and operating costs; the main driver of how hard refiners run.
concepts.formula: margin = product revenue per barrel - crude cost - operating cost

concepts.name: 3-2-1 crack spread
concepts.def: Standard US refining margin proxy: the value of two barrels of gasoline and one barrel of distillate minus three barrels of crude, expressed per barrel.
concepts.formula: (2 x gasoline + 1 x diesel - 3 x crude) / 3, all in dollars per barrel

concepts.name: Product crack
concepts.def: Price of a single refined product minus the price of crude, such as the gasoline crack or the diesel crack; shows which product is driving refinery economics.

concepts.name: Nelson complexity index
concepts.def: Measure of refinery sophistication that weights each secondary processing unit by its cost relative to crude distillation; complex refineries can turn cheap heavy sour crude into light products.

concepts.name: Refinery utilization
concepts.def: Crude processed as a share of operable distillation capacity; high utilization tightens product markets and leaves little slack for outages.
concepts.formula: utilization = crude runs / operable capacity

concepts.name: Refinery turnaround
concepts.def: Planned maintenance shutdown of refinery units, usually concentrated in spring and autumn, which temporarily cuts crude demand and product supply.

concepts.name: Fluid catalytic cracking
concepts.def: Refinery conversion process that uses a catalyst to break heavy gasoil into gasoline, propylene and lighter products; the core of gasoline-oriented refineries.

concepts.name: Hydrocracking
concepts.def: Conversion process that cracks heavy streams under hydrogen pressure, favoring high-quality diesel and jet fuel output.

concepts.name: Coker
concepts.def: Refinery unit that thermally cracks the heaviest residue into lighter products plus petroleum coke, letting refiners profit from running discounted heavy crude.

concepts.name: Refinery product yield
concepts.def: Share of each product, such as gasoline, distillates, jet and fuel oil, obtained from a barrel, set by crude quality and refinery configuration.

concepts.name: Middle distillates
concepts.def: Diesel, gasoil, heating oil and jet fuel; the product group most tied to freight, industry, farming and aviation, and often the tightest part of the barrel.

concepts.name: RBOB gasoline futures
concepts.def: NYMEX gasoline futures contract for a blendstock that becomes finished gasoline after ethanol is added, delivered in New York Harbor; the main US gasoline benchmark.

concepts.name: ULSD futures
concepts.def: NYMEX ultra-low sulfur diesel futures, formerly the heating oil contract, delivered in New York Harbor; the main US distillate benchmark.

concepts.name: ICE low sulphur gasoil
concepts.def: ICE Futures Europe diesel contract delivered in the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp region; the benchmark for European and much of the world's middle distillates.

concepts.name: High sulfur fuel oil
concepts.def: Heavy residual fuel left after distillation, burned by ships fitted with scrubbers and by some power plants; its discount to crude tracks residue supply and sulfur rules.

concepts.name: IMO 2020 sulfur cap
concepts.def: International Maritime Organization rule effective 2020 cutting the sulfur limit in marine fuel outside emission control areas to 0.5 percent from 3.5 percent, shifting demand from high sulfur fuel oil to compliant fuels and distillates.

concepts.name: Reid vapor pressure
concepts.def: Measure of gasoline volatility; regulators require lower RVP in summer to limit evaporation, so summer-grade gasoline costs more and gasoline futures shift grade between seasons.

concepts.name: Driving season
concepts.def: Northern hemisphere summer period of peak gasoline demand, which tends to support gasoline cracks and refinery runs.

concepts.name: Oil demand elasticity
concepts.def: Responsiveness of oil consumption to price; very low in the short run because vehicles, planes and plants cannot switch quickly, so small supply gaps can move prices sharply.

concepts.name: Shale supply response
concepts.def: Ability of US tight oil producers to raise output within months of higher prices because wells are short-cycle, which tends to cap prolonged price spikes.

concepts.name: Rig count
concepts.def: Weekly count of active drilling rigs, most often cited from Baker Hughes; a lagging indicator of price and a leading indicator of production months later.
concepts.aliases: baker hughes rig count,oil rigs,gas rigs

concepts.name: Frac spread count
concepts.def: Number of active hydraulic fracturing crews; tracks well completions and therefore leads shale output more directly than the rig count.

concepts.name: Drilled but uncompleted wells
concepts.def: Wells drilled but not yet fracked and brought online; an inventory that producers can complete to add output without new drilling.

concepts.name: Decline rate
concepts.def: Rate at which a well or field's output falls without new investment; shale wells decline steeply in their early years, so producers must keep drilling just to hold output flat.

concepts.name: Fiscal breakeven oil price
concepts.def: Oil price a petrostate needs to balance its government budget; high fiscal breakevens push producers toward higher prices or higher volumes.

concepts.name: Reserve life index
concepts.def: Years of production remaining if current output continues against current reserves.
concepts.formula: R/P = reserves / annual production

concepts.name: Upstream, midstream, downstream
concepts.def: Oil and gas value chain segments: exploration and production, transport and storage, and refining and marketing, each with different exposure to price and volume.

concepts.name: Netback
concepts.def: Realized value at the wellhead or plant after deducting royalties, transport, processing and production costs from the market price.
concepts.formula: netback = market price - royalties - transport - production costs

concepts.name: Pipeline takeaway capacity
concepts.def: Capacity to move oil or gas out of a producing basin; when output outgrows it, local prices fall to deep discounts versus coastal hubs until new pipes arrive.

concepts.name: Days of cover
concepts.def: Inventories divided by daily demand; normalizes stock levels for demand growth when comparing with history.
concepts.formula: days of cover = stocks / daily consumption

concepts.name: OECD commercial stocks
concepts.def: Industry-held oil inventories in OECD countries, often compared with their five-year average as the headline gauge of oil market balance.

concepts.name: Five-year average comparison
concepts.def: Convention of judging inventories against their seasonal five-year average; surpluses versus this norm tend to coincide with contango and deficits with backwardation.

concepts.name: Supply-demand balance
concepts.def: Projection of supply minus demand over time; a surplus implies inventory builds and contango, while a deficit implies draws and backwardation.

concepts.name: Missing barrels
concepts.def: Gap between the stock change implied by supply and demand estimates and the inventory change actually observed, signaling incomplete or wrong balance data.

concepts.name: IEA Oil Market Report
concepts.def: Monthly International Energy Agency assessment of oil supply, demand and stocks, read alongside EIA and OPEC monthly reports to frame the balance.

concepts.name: OPEC+ quotas and compliance
concepts.def: Production targets agreed by OPEC+ members and how closely actual output matches them; overproduction by members weakens the credibility and effect of cuts.

concepts.name: Production cut
concepts.def: Collective reduction in output targets to tighten balances; its effect depends on compliance, spare capacity and the response of producers outside the group.

concepts.name: Oil price war
concepts.def: Episode in which a major producer raises output or refuses to cut to defend market share and squeeze rivals, crashing prices; 1986, 2014 to 2016 and 2020 are standard examples.

concepts.name: Swing producer
concepts.def: Supplier with spare capacity able to raise or cut output quickly to balance the market; Saudi Arabia has historically played this role in oil.

concepts.name: Call on OPEC
concepts.def: World oil demand minus non-OPEC supply and OPEC natural gas liquids; the crude volume OPEC must supply to keep global inventories flat.
concepts.formula: call = global demand - non-OPEC supply - OPEC NGLs
concepts.aliases: call on opec crude,call on opec+

concepts.name: OVX
concepts.def: Cboe crude oil volatility index derived from options on the United States Oil Fund ETF; the oil market analog of the VIX.

concepts.name: 2020 negative oil price
concepts.def: April 2020 episode when the expiring May WTI futures contract settled below zero because Cushing storage was nearly full and longs had nowhere to take delivery.

concepts.name: Delivery squeeze
concepts.def: Price spike near futures expiry when long holders stand for delivery and deliverable supply is scarce, forcing shorts to buy back at high prices.

concepts.name: Market corner
concepts.def: Gaining control of enough deliverable supply and long futures to dictate settlement prices; the Hunt brothers in silver (1980) and Sumitomo in copper (1996) are classic cases.

concepts.name: Henry Hub
concepts.def: Louisiana pipeline interconnect that is the delivery point for NYMEX natural gas futures and the main US gas price benchmark.

concepts.name: Dutch TTF
concepts.def: Title Transfer Facility, a virtual Dutch gas trading point that serves as Europe's main natural gas benchmark.

concepts.name: Japan Korea Marker
concepts.def: Platts spot price assessment for LNG cargoes delivered into Northeast Asia; the main Asian spot LNG benchmark.

concepts.name: National Balancing Point
concepts.def: Virtual trading point for UK natural gas, quoted in pence per therm and closely linked to TTF.

concepts.name: Natural gas basis
concepts.def: Price difference between a regional gas hub and Henry Hub, set by pipeline constraints, local supply and seasonal demand.

concepts.name: Waha hub
concepts.def: West Texas gas hub where Permian associated gas trades; prices there have at times gone negative when pipeline capacity fell short of supply.

concepts.name: Associated gas
concepts.def: Natural gas produced alongside oil, so its supply follows oil drilling economics rather than gas prices.

concepts.name: EIA natural gas storage report
concepts.def: Weekly report of working gas in US underground storage, released Thursdays; the injection or withdrawal versus expectations is the most market-moving gas data point.

concepts.name: Injection and withdrawal seasons
concepts.def: US gas storage convention: injection season runs roughly April through October as storage fills, withdrawal season November through March as heating demand draws it down.

concepts.name: Heating and cooling degree days
concepts.def: Weather demand measures based on deviation of daily average temperature from 65 F; they drive short-term gas and power demand forecasts.
concepts.formula: HDD = max(0, 65 - average temp F); CDD = max(0, average temp F - 65)
concepts.aliases: hdd,cdd,degree days,heating degree days,cooling degree days

concepts.name: Widowmaker spread
concepts.def: The March-April natural gas futures spread, which can explode when late-winter storage runs short; named for the traders it has ruined.

concepts.name: Amaranth collapse
concepts.def: 2006 failure of hedge fund Amaranth Advisors after concentrated natural gas calendar spread positions lost billions of dollars within weeks.

concepts.name: Liquefaction
concepts.def: Cooling natural gas to about minus 162 Celsius so it shrinks roughly 600-fold for shipping; liquefaction plants are the costliest link in the LNG chain.

concepts.name: Regasification
concepts.def: Warming LNG back into gas at import terminals or floating storage and regasification units for delivery into pipelines.

concepts.name: LNG offtake contract
concepts.def: Long-term agreement underpinning an LNG project, often with take-or-pay terms; US contracts commonly price as a percentage of Henry Hub plus a fixed liquefaction fee.

concepts.name: Oil-indexed LNG pricing
concepts.def: Long-term LNG contracts priced as a slope times a lagged crude average, such as Brent or the Japan Crude Cocktail, plus a constant.
concepts.formula: price = slope x lagged oil price + constant

concepts.name: LNG arbitrage
concepts.def: Routing flexible cargoes to the destination with the highest netback; the JKM-TTF spread minus the shipping cost difference decides whether cargoes head to Asia or Europe.

concepts.name: Coal-to-gas switching
concepts.def: Generators shifting between coal and gas as relative fuel and carbon prices change; a large price-sensitive source of gas demand.

concepts.name: Natural gas liquids
concepts.def: Ethane, propane, butanes and natural gasoline separated from wet gas; prices follow petrochemical demand, crude and export capacity.

concepts.name: Ethane rejection
concepts.def: Leaving ethane in the gas stream to be sold as fuel instead of extracting it when its value as petrochemical feedstock is lower.

concepts.name: Oil-to-gas price ratio
concepts.def: Crude price per barrel divided by gas price per MMBtu; a ratio far above the energy-equivalent level near 6 means gas is cheap relative to oil on an energy basis.
concepts.formula: ratio = oil price per barrel / gas price per MMBtu
concepts.aliases: oil gas ratio,wti henry hub ratio

concepts.name: MMBtu
concepts.def: One million British thermal units, the energy unit for US natural gas pricing; roughly equal to one thousand cubic feet of gas.

concepts.name: Locational marginal price
concepts.def: Wholesale electricity price at a specific grid node, equal to the marginal cost of serving one more megawatt-hour there; it splits into energy, congestion and loss components.
concepts.formula: LMP = energy component + congestion component + loss component

concepts.name: Merit order
concepts.def: Ranking of generators from lowest to highest marginal cost; the costliest unit needed to meet demand sets the clearing price paid to all dispatched units.

concepts.name: ISOs and RTOs
concepts.def: Independent system operators and regional transmission organizations that run US wholesale power markets and dispatch the grid, such as PJM, ERCOT, CAISO and MISO.

concepts.name: Day-ahead and real-time power markets
concepts.def: Two-settlement design: a day-ahead auction sets hourly schedules and prices, and a real-time market settles deviations at spot prices, creating a tradable DA-RT spread.

concepts.name: Virtual bidding
concepts.def: Purely financial bids to buy or sell power day-ahead and reverse the position in real time, which helps converge the two prices.

concepts.name: Capacity market
concepts.def: Market paying generators and demand response to be available in future periods, separate from energy sales, to secure reliability; PJM's capacity auction is a prominent example.

concepts.name: Energy-only market
concepts.def: Power market without capacity payments, where scarcity prices during tight hours must reward investment in new supply; ERCOT in Texas is the main US example.

concepts.name: Scarcity pricing
concepts.def: Rules that lift power prices toward a cap when operating reserves run short, signaling the value of reliability and paying flexible supply.
concepts.aliases: price cap,ordc,operating reserve demand curve,price adder

concepts.name: Heat rate
concepts.def: Fuel energy a power plant burns per unit of electricity, in Btu per kWh; lower heat rates mean more efficient plants.
concepts.formula: heat rate = fuel input Btu / electricity output kWh

concepts.name: Implied market heat rate
concepts.def: Power price divided by gas price; it shows the efficiency of the marginal gas unit priced into the market and is traded as a view on power relative to gas.
concepts.formula: implied heat rate = power price per MWh / gas price per MMBtu

concepts.name: Dark spread
concepts.def: Gross margin of a coal plant: power price minus coal cost adjusted for the plant's efficiency; the clean dark spread also deducts carbon cost.
concepts.formula: dark spread = power price - coal price x coal heat rate

concepts.name: Clean spark spread
concepts.def: Spark spread net of the cost of carbon allowances needed per megawatt-hour; the relevant margin for gas plants in carbon-priced markets.
concepts.formula: clean spark = power - gas price x heat rate - carbon price x emissions per MWh

concepts.name: Capacity factor
concepts.def: Energy a generator actually produces over a period divided by what it would produce running at full nameplate capacity the whole time.
concepts.formula: capacity factor = MWh generated / (MW capacity x hours in period)

concepts.name: Levelized cost of energy
concepts.def: Discounted lifetime cost of building and running a generator divided by discounted lifetime output; useful for comparing technologies but blind to when and where power is produced.
concepts.formula: LCOE = PV(lifetime costs) / PV(lifetime MWh)

concepts.name: Duck curve
concepts.def: Shape of net load in solar-heavy grids: a midday trough and a steep evening ramp, which depresses midday prices and rewards batteries and fast-ramping plants.

concepts.name: Negative power prices
concepts.def: Wholesale prices below zero when inflexible or subsidized generation exceeds demand, so producers pay to keep running rather than shut down.

concepts.name: Renewable price cannibalization
concepts.def: Falling capture prices for wind and solar as more is built, because they produce in the same hours and depress prices in exactly those hours.

concepts.name: Shape risk
concepts.def: Risk that the hourly profile of a hedge or of generation does not match the load or exposure it covers, leaving residual exposure to intraday price patterns.

concepts.name: Financial transmission rights
concepts.def: Instruments paying the congestion price difference between two grid nodes, letting holders hedge or speculate on locational price differences.

concepts.name: Interconnection queue
concepts.def: Backlog of generation and storage projects waiting for grid operator studies and approval to connect; long queues slow the arrival of new supply.

concepts.name: Battery storage arbitrage
concepts.def: Charging batteries when power is cheap and discharging when it is expensive, plus selling ancillary services; returns depend on daily price spreads, efficiency losses and cycle limits.

concepts.name: Ancillary services
concepts.def: Grid services beyond bulk energy, such as frequency regulation, spinning and non-spinning reserves and voltage support, procured by system operators.

concepts.name: Reserve margin
concepts.def: Available generating capacity above expected peak demand, as a share of peak; a thin margin raises the risk of scarcity prices and blackouts.
concepts.formula: reserve margin = (capacity - peak demand) / peak demand

concepts.name: Baseload and peak power
concepts.def: Standard power trading blocks: baseload covers all hours, peak covers weekday daytime hours (often 16 per day), and peak usually trades at a premium.

concepts.name: Carbon allowances
concepts.def: Tradable permits to emit one tonne of CO2 under a cap-and-trade system such as the EU ETS; their price adds to fossil generation cost and shifts the merit order.

concepts.name: Renewable energy certificate
concepts.def: Tradable certificate representing one megawatt-hour of renewable generation, used to meet renewable mandates or support clean energy claims.

concepts.name: Renewable Identification Numbers
concepts.def: Credits generated by biofuel blending and used by refiners and importers to show compliance with the US Renewable Fuel Standard; their cost feeds into refining margins.

concepts.name: Weather derivatives
concepts.def: Contracts paying on weather indices such as heating or cooling degree days or rainfall, used by utilities and energy firms to hedge volume risk.

concepts.name: London Metal Exchange
concepts.def: The main venue for industrial metals futures, with daily prompt dates out to three months and a global warehouse network for physical delivery.

concepts.name: 2022 LME nickel squeeze
concepts.def: March 2022 episode in which nickel prices more than doubled in a day on a short squeeze, after which the London Metal Exchange suspended trading and cancelled trades.

concepts.name: COMEX
concepts.def: CME Group exchange division listing gold, silver and copper futures; its warehouse stocks and the spread to London prices are watched for physical tightness.

concepts.name: LBMA gold price
concepts.def: Twice-daily electronic auction benchmark for gold in London, successor to the historic London gold fix and used to settle many contracts.

concepts.name: Loco London
concepts.def: Gold or silver held in London vaults, the standard basis for over-the-counter bullion trading and settlement.

concepts.name: Allocated versus unallocated metal
concepts.def: Allocated metal is specific bars owned outright and held for the owner; unallocated metal is a claim on a dealer's general stock and carries the dealer's credit risk.

concepts.name: Gold lease rate
concepts.def: Interest rate for borrowing gold, approximated as the dollar interest rate minus the gold forward rate; spikes signal scarce lendable metal.
concepts.formula: lease rate = USD rate - gold forward offered rate

concepts.name: Gold and real yields
concepts.def: Long-observed inverse relationship between gold and real interest rates, because gold pays no income; the link can weaken when central bank or geopolitical buying dominates.

concepts.name: Gold-silver ratio
concepts.def: Ounces of silver needed to buy one ounce of gold; traders use it as a relative value and risk appetite gauge.
concepts.formula: ratio = gold price / silver price

concepts.name: Platinum group metals
concepts.def: Platinum, palladium, rhodium and related metals, used mainly in vehicle catalytic converters, with mine supply concentrated in South Africa and Russia.

concepts.name: Aluminium
concepts.def: Light metal made by energy-intensive smelting of alumina from bauxite; electricity cost is the key driver of the smelter cost curve.

concepts.name: Nickel
concepts.def: Metal used mainly in stainless steel and increasingly in battery cathodes, with supply shifting toward Indonesian processing of laterite ore.

concepts.name: Lithium
concepts.def: Battery metal produced from brines and hard rock spodumene and sold as carbonate or hydroxide; prone to boom-bust cycles as supply responds with long lags.

concepts.name: Cobalt
concepts.def: Battery metal mostly mined as a byproduct of copper and nickel, with supply heavily concentrated in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

concepts.name: Uranium
concepts.def: Nuclear fuel traded as U3O8 mostly through long-term utility contracts with a thin spot market; conversion and enrichment are separately priced steps in the fuel cycle.

concepts.name: Rare earth elements
concepts.def: Group of 17 elements used in magnets, electronics and defense; mining and especially processing are concentrated in China, making supply a policy lever.

concepts.name: Steel spread
concepts.def: Steel price minus raw material cost: iron ore and coking coal for blast furnaces or scrap for electric arc furnaces; the core steelmaker margin.

concepts.name: Metallurgical coal
concepts.def: High-quality coal converted to coke for blast-furnace steelmaking, priced separately from and usually above thermal coal.

concepts.name: Thermal coal
concepts.def: Coal burned for electricity, priced off benchmarks such as Newcastle for Asia and API2 for Europe.

concepts.name: All-in sustaining cost
concepts.def: Gold miner cost metric that adds sustaining capital, exploration, and corporate overhead to cash operating costs per ounce.

concepts.name: Byproduct credits
concepts.def: Revenue from secondary metals subtracted from a mine's primary-metal cost, which can make reported unit costs very low or negative.

concepts.name: Treatment and refining charges
concepts.def: Fees miners pay smelters to process concentrate into metal; falling TC/RCs signal tight concentrate supply relative to smelting capacity.

concepts.name: Ore grade decline
concepts.def: Falling metal content per tonne of ore as the best deposits are depleted, which raises unit costs and capital needs over time.

concepts.name: Mine supply disruption
concepts.def: Unplanned output losses from strikes, accidents, weather, or politics; analysts often bake a disruption allowance into supply forecasts.

concepts.name: Secondary metal supply
concepts.def: Metal recovered from scrap and recycled, which rises with price and supplements mine output, especially in copper, aluminium and steel.

concepts.name: Resource nationalism
concepts.def: Government moves to capture more mineral or energy rent through higher royalties, export bans, forced local processing or nationalization; a key political risk in resources.

concepts.name: Cancelled warrants
concepts.def: LME warehouse stocks earmarked for withdrawal; a rising share of cancelled warrants signals physical demand and possible tightness ahead.

concepts.name: Physical gold ETFs
concepts.def: Exchange-traded funds holding allocated gold bars, giving brokerage access to bullion; their holdings are a gauge of Western investment demand.

concepts.name: Gold miner operating leverage
concepts.def: Miner profits move by more than the gold price because costs are largely fixed, so miners amplify both gains and losses in the metal.

concepts.name: Streaming and royalty companies
concepts.def: Firms that pay upfront for a share of a mine's future metal output or revenue, gaining commodity exposure without operating costs or most capex risk.

concepts.name: Corn
concepts.def: The largest US crop by volume, used for animal feed, ethanol and exports; CBOT corn futures are the global benchmark.

concepts.name: Soybeans
concepts.def: Oilseed crushed into meal for feed and oil for food and biofuel; prices depend on US and Brazilian crops and on Chinese import demand.

concepts.name: Wheat
concepts.def: Food grain traded in several classes, including CBOT soft red winter, Kansas City hard red winter and Minneapolis spring wheat; exports come from many regions so weather risk is diversified.

concepts.name: Ethanol crush margin
concepts.def: Ethanol plant margin: value of ethanol and distillers grains produced minus the cost of corn and natural gas consumed.

concepts.name: Stocks-to-use ratio
concepts.def: Ending stocks divided by annual use; low ratios leave little buffer, so prices react sharply to supply shocks.
concepts.formula: stocks-to-use = ending stocks / total use

concepts.name: Crop progress and condition reports
concepts.def: Weekly USDA reports on planting, development, harvest and crop condition ratings during the season; changes in good-to-excellent ratings move grain futures.

concepts.name: Planting intentions and acreage reports
concepts.def: USDA reports estimating planted area: Prospective Plantings in March and Acreage at the end of June; key early signals of new-crop supply.

concepts.name: Weather market
concepts.def: Growing-season period when grain prices trade mostly on weather forecasts, with critical windows such as corn pollination in July, adding a risk premium that fades with good weather.

concepts.name: Cash grain basis
concepts.def: Local cash price minus nearby futures; it reflects transport, storage and local demand, and it is what farmers and elevators actually trade.

concepts.name: Full carry
concepts.def: Calendar spread equal to storage plus financing cost, the widest contango that can persist before cash-and-carry arbitrage caps it; grain spreads near full carry signal ample supply.
concepts.formula: full carry = storage cost + financing cost over the period

concepts.name: Livestock futures
concepts.def: Live cattle, feeder cattle and lean hog futures, driven by herd cycles, feed costs, disease and meat demand.

concepts.name: Cattle cycle
concepts.def: Multi-year cycle in which ranchers expand or liquidate herds in response to prices and feed costs; because heifers are held back to rebuild, beef supply responds slowly.

concepts.name: Hog crush margin
concepts.def: Hog production margin: lean hog value minus the cost of corn and soybean meal fed to raise the animal.

concepts.name: Sugar-ethanol parity
concepts.def: Brazilian mills shift cane between sugar and ethanol depending on relative returns, linking world sugar prices to Brazilian fuel prices.

concepts.name: Fertilizer
concepts.def: Nitrogen, phosphate and potash crop inputs; nitrogen products such as ammonia and urea are made from natural gas, so gas shocks pass through to farm costs.

concepts.name: Commodity export restriction
concepts.def: Government ban, quota or tax on exports to protect domestic supply or prices, which tightens world markets; common in grains, fertilizer and critical minerals.

concepts.name: El Nino and La Nina
concepts.def: Pacific Ocean temperature cycles that shift rainfall worldwide, affecting crops such as Australian wheat, Southeast Asian palm oil and South American soybeans.

concepts.name: Palm oil
concepts.def: The most produced vegetable oil, grown mainly in Indonesia and Malaysia; it competes with soybean oil and is used for food and biodiesel.

concepts.name: Daily price limit
concepts.def: Maximum price move allowed in a session for some futures contracts; a locked-limit market can halt trading and trap positions until prices reset.

concepts.name: Baltic Dry Index
concepts.def: Baltic Exchange composite of dry bulk freight rates across ship sizes and routes; it moves with both cargo demand and fleet supply.

concepts.name: Voyage and time charters
concepts.def: Ways to hire ships: a voyage charter pays per cargo for one trip, a time charter pays a daily hire rate for a period while the charterer pays fuel and port costs.

concepts.name: Time charter equivalent
concepts.def: Voyage revenue minus voyage costs such as fuel and port fees, divided by voyage days; puts spot voyages on a daily-rate basis comparable with time charters.
concepts.formula: TCE = (voyage revenue - voyage costs) / voyage days

concepts.name: Worldscale
concepts.def: Tanker freight convention quoting rates as a percentage of a published flat rate for each route, updated annually.

concepts.name: Tanker size classes
concepts.def: Crude tanker sizes: VLCCs carry about two million barrels, Suezmaxes about one million and Aframaxes less; each suits different ports and routes.

concepts.name: Forward freight agreement
concepts.def: Cash-settled derivative on future freight rates for a route or index, used by shipowners and charterers to hedge freight exposure.

concepts.name: Floating storage
concepts.def: Storing crude or products on tankers when contango exceeds chartering and financing costs; large floating storage signals severe oversupply.

concepts.name: Ton-mile demand
concepts.def: Cargo tonnage multiplied by distance carried; rerouting and longer voyages raise effective demand for ships even when cargo volumes are flat.
concepts.formula: ton-miles = tonnes carried x miles sailed

concepts.name: Orderbook-to-fleet ratio
concepts.def: Ships on order as a share of the existing fleet; a central gauge of future supply growth in shipping cycles.

concepts.name: Shipping cycle
concepts.def: Boom-bust pattern in which high freight rates spur newbuild orders that arrive years later into softer demand, pushing rates down until scrapping restores balance.

concepts.name: Maritime chokepoints
concepts.def: Narrow sea routes such as Hormuz, Malacca, Suez, Bab el-Mandeb and Panama whose disruption forces rerouting and lifts freight, insurance and delivered prices.

concepts.name: War risk insurance premium
concepts.def: Additional marine insurance charged for voyages through conflict zones, adding to delivered cost and sometimes diverting ships entirely.

concepts.name: Container freight indices
concepts.def: Spot rate benchmarks for container shipping, such as the Shanghai Containerized Freight Index and the Drewry World Container Index.

concepts.name: Shadow fleet
concepts.def: Older tankers with opaque ownership and insurance used to move sanctioned oil outside Western shipping and insurance services.

concepts.name: Sanctioned oil flows
concepts.def: Crude from sanctioned producers that trades at discounts through intermediaries; sanctions often redirect trade flows more than they cut total supply.

concepts.name: Russian oil price cap
concepts.def: G7-led mechanism barring Western shipping, insurance and finance for Russian oil sold above a set price, aiming to cut revenue while keeping barrels flowing.

concepts.name: Demurrage
concepts.def: Fee paid to a shipowner when loading or discharging takes longer than the agreed laytime; port congestion turns it into a material cost.

concepts.name: Storage arbitrage
concepts.def: Buying spot, selling forward and storing the commodity when the contango exceeds storage plus financing cost; this trade caps how wide contango can get.
concepts.formula: profit = futures price - spot price - storage cost - financing cost
concepts.aliases: cash and carry,storage trade,carry trade commodities

concepts.name: Tank tops
concepts.def: Condition where storage approaches full capacity, forcing spot prices down sharply until production or consumption adjusts; it produces super contango.

concepts.name: Storage as a real option
concepts.def: Valuing storage capacity as a strip of spread options between injection and withdrawal dates, with intrinsic value from the current curve and extrinsic value from volatility.

concepts.name: Location spread
concepts.def: Price difference for the same commodity at two delivery points; when transport capacity is free, it is bounded by transport cost.

concepts.name: Inter-commodity spread
concepts.def: Trade between related commodities, such as crack, crush, spark or corn-wheat spreads, that exposes the trader to a processing or substitution margin rather than outright price.

concepts.name: Commodity index
concepts.def: Rules-based basket of commodity futures, such as the production-weighted S&P GSCI or the more diversified Bloomberg Commodity Index, rolled on a set schedule.

concepts.name: Index roll period
concepts.def: Monthly window when commodity index funds roll expiring futures into later months; predictable flows that other traders can position ahead of.

concepts.name: Commodity futures return decomposition
concepts.def: Total return on collateralized futures splits into spot price change, roll yield from curve shape and interest earned on the cash collateral.
concepts.formula: total return = spot return + roll yield + collateral yield

concepts.name: Physical commodity traders
concepts.def: Firms such as Vitol, Trafigura, Glencore and Cargill that buy, store, blend and ship physical commodities, earning on location, time and quality spreads.

concepts.name: Hedging pressure theory
concepts.def: Idea that net hedging demand by producers or consumers creates a risk premium paid to speculators who take the other side, shaping futures returns.

concepts.name: Average price option
concepts.def: Option paying on the average price over a period rather than the price on one date; the standard form for commodity hedges because consumption is continuous.

concepts.name: Commodity swap
concepts.def: OTC contract exchanging a fixed price for a floating average price over a period, used by producers and consumers to hedge without physical delivery.

concepts.name: Price reporting agencies
concepts.def: Firms such as Platts and Argus whose assessments of physical deals set benchmark prices for cargoes and settle many derivatives; methodology details move money.

concepts.name: Real assets
concepts.def: Physical or contract-backed assets with intrinsic use value, such as real estate, infrastructure, farmland, timber and commodities, often held for income and partial inflation protection.

concepts.name: Infrastructure investing
concepts.def: Owning essential long-lived assets such as toll roads, airports, pipelines, utilities, towers and data centers, valued for contracted or regulated cash flows and high barriers to entry.

concepts.name: Core to opportunistic spectrum
concepts.def: Real estate and infrastructure strategy ladder: core (stable income, low leverage), core-plus, value-add (repositioning) and opportunistic (development, distress, high leverage), with rising return targets.

concepts.name: Brownfield and greenfield
concepts.def: Brownfield assets are existing and operating; greenfield assets are new builds that carry construction, permitting and ramp-up risk in exchange for higher expected returns.

concepts.name: Infrastructure concession
concepts.def: Government grant to finance, build or operate an asset such as a toll road for a fixed term, after which it reverts to the grantor, so value runs down toward term end.

concepts.name: Public-private partnership
concepts.def: Long-term contract in which a private party finances, builds and operates public infrastructure, paid through user charges or government availability payments.

concepts.name: Availability payment
concepts.def: Government payment to an operator for keeping an asset available to agreed standards regardless of usage, removing demand risk from the investor.

concepts.name: Project finance
concepts.def: Non-recourse lending to a single-asset special purpose vehicle, repaid only from the project's cash flows and secured by its contracts and assets.

concepts.name: Debt service coverage ratio
concepts.def: Cash available for debt service divided by scheduled principal and interest; lenders set minimums and cash lockup triggers on it in project and real estate loans.
concepts.formula: DSCR = cash flow available for debt service / (principal + interest)

concepts.name: Regulated rate base
concepts.def: Value of a regulated utility's invested capital on which regulators allow a return; earnings grow mainly as the rate base grows.
concepts.formula: allowed earnings = rate base x equity share x allowed ROE

concepts.name: Allowed return on equity
concepts.def: Return on equity a utility regulator lets the company earn on its rate base; the spread between earned and allowed ROE and the cost of equity drives utility valuation.

concepts.name: Master limited partnership
concepts.def: Publicly traded US partnership, common in midstream energy, that passes taxable income through to unitholders and pays large distributions.

concepts.name: Inflation escalator
concepts.def: Contract or tariff clause that raises revenue with a price index such as CPI, giving infrastructure and leases partial inflation protection.

concepts.name: Timberland
concepts.def: Forest real asset earning harvest income plus biological growth; owners can delay harvests when prices are low, letting trees keep growing in volume and value.

concepts.name: Farmland
concepts.def: Real asset earning cash rent or crop income plus land appreciation; values track crop prices, farm incomes and interest rates.

concepts.name: Digital infrastructure
concepts.def: Cell towers, fiber networks and data centers held as infrastructure, earning long-term leases from carriers, cloud providers and other tech tenants.

concepts.name: Tower lease-up economics
concepts.def: Tower costs are mostly fixed, so each additional tenant on an existing tower adds revenue at very high margin; colocation drives returns.

concepts.name: Yieldco
concepts.def: Listed vehicle holding contracted renewable or infrastructure assets and paying out most cash flow as dividends, funded by issuing equity to buy more assets.

concepts.name: Merchant risk
concepts.def: Exposure of an asset's revenue to spot market prices rather than fixed contracts, common in power plants and storage after contracts expire.

concepts.name: Tax equity
concepts.def: US structure in which investors with tax liability fund renewable projects in exchange for tax credits and depreciation benefits; credit transferability now offers an alternative route.

concepts.name: Cap rate spread
concepts.def: Cap rate minus the 10-year Treasury yield; a gauge of real estate's risk premium and relative value versus bonds.
concepts.formula: spread = cap rate - 10-year Treasury yield
concepts.aliases: cap rate spread,real estate risk premium

concepts.name: Mortgage REIT
concepts.def: REIT holding mortgages or mortgage securities funded with leverage and earning the net interest spread; highly sensitive to rates, spreads and funding conditions.

concepts.name: REIT premium or discount to NAV
concepts.def: Gap between a REIT's share price and the estimated private-market value of its properties; persistent discounts can prompt buybacks, asset sales or take-privates.

concepts.name: Implied cap rate
concepts.def: Cap rate implied by a listed REIT's enterprise value and its NOI, compared with private appraisal cap rates to judge whether public or private markets look mispriced.
concepts.formula: implied cap rate = NOI / (equity market value + debt + preferred - non-property assets)

concepts.name: Occupancy and vacancy
concepts.def: Share of leasable space that is leased (occupancy) or empty (vacancy); the main volume driver of property NOI.
concepts.formula: vacancy rate = vacant space / total space

concepts.name: Net absorption
concepts.def: Change in occupied space over a period: space newly leased minus space vacated; positive absorption signals growing demand.

concepts.name: Weighted average lease term
concepts.def: Average remaining lease term weighted by rent; a longer WALT means more contracted income and less near-term re-leasing risk.

concepts.name: Net lease
concepts.def: Lease in which the tenant pays property taxes, insurance and maintenance (triple net), making the landlord's income resemble a long bond tied to tenant credit.

concepts.name: Mark-to-market of rents
concepts.def: Gap between in-place rents and current market rents, indicating income upside or downside as leases roll over.
concepts.aliases: loss to lease,rent reversion,mark to market

concepts.name: Lease rollover risk
concepts.def: Concentration of lease expiries that exposes income to re-leasing at market rents, downtime and leasing costs.

concepts.name: Tenant improvements and leasing commissions
concepts.def: Landlord spending to fit out space and pay brokers when signing leases; large in office and often understated in headline earnings.

concepts.name: Rent concessions
concepts.def: Free months or other incentives that make effective rent lower than headline rent, used to defend face rents in weak markets.
concepts.formula: net effective rent = (total rent over term - concessions) / term

concepts.name: Debt yield
concepts.def: NOI divided by loan amount; a lender metric that does not depend on cap rates or interest rates.
concepts.formula: debt yield = NOI / loan amount

concepts.name: Special servicer
concepts.def: Servicer that takes over a securitized commercial mortgage in default or at risk, deciding whether to modify, extend or foreclose.

concepts.name: Extend and pretend
concepts.def: Lenders extending maturing loans rather than foreclosing, hoping values recover; it delays loss recognition and can trap capital in weak assets.

concepts.name: Office obsolescence
concepts.def: Value loss in older office buildings as tenants favor newer space and use less of it, leaving owners facing heavy capex, conversion or writedowns.

concepts.name: Industrial and logistics property
concepts.def: Warehouses and distribution centers whose demand tracks e-commerce, inventory strategies and supply chains.

concepts.name: Multifamily
concepts.def: Apartment buildings with short leases that let rents reset quickly, giving inflation sensitivity and exposure to new supply waves.

concepts.name: Single-family rental
concepts.def: Institutional ownership of detached homes for rent, a sector that scaled after the 2008 housing crash.

concepts.name: Housing affordability
concepts.def: Ability of typical households to buy a home, measured by price-to-income or mortgage payment as a share of income; poor affordability depresses sales volumes.

concepts.name: Mortgage lock-in effect
concepts.def: Homeowners holding low fixed-rate mortgages are reluctant to sell and take on a higher rate, cutting existing-home supply and turnover.

concepts.name: Case-Shiller home price index
concepts.def: Repeat-sales US home price index that tracks price changes of the same homes over time, published monthly with a lag.

concepts.name: Months' supply of homes
concepts.def: Homes listed for sale divided by the monthly sales pace; low readings point to tight markets and rising prices.
concepts.formula: months supply = inventory for sale / monthly sales

concepts.name: Price-to-rent ratio
concepts.def: Home price divided by annual rent for comparable housing; high ratios suggest owning is expensive relative to renting.
concepts.formula: ratio = home price / annual rent

concepts.name: Real estate cycle
concepts.def: Recurring sequence of recovery, expansion, oversupply and recession driven by long construction lags and credit availability.

concepts.name: Development yield on cost
concepts.def: Stabilized NOI divided by total development cost; it must exceed market cap rates by a margin to justify the risk of building.
concepts.formula: yield on cost = stabilized NOI / total development cost

concepts.name: Appraisal lag
concepts.def: Private property values based on periodic appraisals adjust slowly to market moves, smoothing reported returns and understating volatility and correlation.

concepts.name: NCREIF ODCE index
concepts.def: Index of open-end diversified core equity US real estate funds; the main benchmark for core private real estate.

concepts.name: Non-traded REIT
concepts.def: REIT not listed on an exchange that offers limited periodic redemptions at a sponsor-set NAV; it can cap or prorate withdrawals when requests surge.
concepts.aliases: nontraded reit,perpetual nav reit,semi-liquid real estate

concepts.name: 1031 exchange
concepts.def: US tax rule letting real estate investors defer capital gains by reinvesting sale proceeds into like-kind property within set deadlines.

concepts.name: Positive and negative leverage
concepts.def: Leverage is positive when a property's cap rate exceeds the all-in cost of debt, lifting equity returns, and negative when debt costs more than the property yields.

concepts.name: Ground lease
concepts.def: Long-term lease of land to a building owner who pays ground rent and surrenders improvements at expiry; the landowner's position is senior and bond-like.

concepts.name: RevPAR
concepts.def: Hotel revenue per available room, the main hotel performance metric, combining occupancy and pricing.
concepts.formula: RevPAR = occupancy rate x average daily rate

concepts.name: Financial sponsor
concepts.def: Private equity firm that buys and controls companies using equity from its funds plus acquisition debt, aiming to sell within several years.

concepts.name: Value creation bridge
concepts.def: Attribution of a buyout's equity gain to EBITDA growth, multiple expansion and debt paydown, showing whether returns came from operations or from market and leverage.

concepts.name: Buy-and-build
concepts.def: Strategy of acquiring a platform company and bolting on smaller add-on acquisitions at lower multiples, seeking scale, synergies and multiple arbitrage.

concepts.name: Equity check
concepts.def: Share of a buyout's total price funded with sponsor equity rather than debt; a larger check lowers default risk but also lowers equity returns for a given outcome.

concepts.name: Rollover equity
concepts.def: Equity that selling owners or managers reinvest into the new deal instead of taking cash, aligning them with the buyer's exit.

concepts.name: Carve-out
concepts.def: Purchase of a division from a larger company, requiring standalone functions and usually transitional service agreements with the former parent.

concepts.name: Secondary buyout
concepts.def: Sale of a sponsor-owned company to another private equity firm; common when IPO and strategic exits are scarce.

concepts.name: Leveraged loan
concepts.def: Floating-rate senior secured loan to a sub-investment-grade borrower, typically syndicated and held largely by CLOs and loan funds.

concepts.name: Maintenance versus incurrence covenants
concepts.def: Maintenance covenants are tested regularly, such as quarterly leverage limits; incurrence covenants apply only when the borrower takes an action such as adding debt or paying dividends.

concepts.name: First lien and second lien
concepts.def: Ranking of secured claims on the same collateral; first-lien lenders are repaid first in default, while second-lien lenders accept lower recoveries for higher spreads.

concepts.name: Preferred equity
concepts.def: Capital senior to common equity with a fixed or accruing return, used in buyouts, real estate and GP financing as a bridge between debt and equity.

concepts.name: Original issue discount
concepts.def: Issuing a loan or bond below par, giving lenders upfront yield on top of the coupon spread.
concepts.formula: yield pickup per year approx = OID / expected life of loan

concepts.name: Asset-based finance
concepts.def: Lending secured by pools of receivables, inventory, equipment or consumer loans rather than by enterprise value, a growing part of private credit.

concepts.name: Non-accrual loans
concepts.def: Loans on which a lender has stopped recognizing interest income because full collection is doubtful; a key credit quality metric for BDCs.

concepts.name: Recurring revenue loan
concepts.def: Loan to a software company sized on annual recurring revenue rather than EBITDA, betting on retention and later profitability.

concepts.name: Evergreen fund
concepts.def: Open-ended private markets vehicle with continuous subscriptions and periodic, capped redemptions, rather than a fixed-life fund.

concepts.name: Closed-end fund life
concepts.def: Standard private fund structure with an investment period of several years and a total term near ten years plus extensions, returning capital as assets are sold.

concepts.name: Capital commitment
concepts.def: Amount an LP agrees to provide to a fund over its life, drawn through capital calls; the undrawn part remains a binding liability for the LP.

concepts.name: Overcommitment strategy
concepts.def: Committing more than the target private allocation on the expectation that calls and distributions will keep invested NAV near target; risky if distributions slow.

concepts.name: Denominator effect
concepts.def: When public markets fall faster than lagging private marks, private allocations rise above target, pressuring LPs to slow new commitments or sell on the secondary market.

concepts.name: Commitment pacing
concepts.def: Planning yearly commitments across vintages so a portfolio reaches and holds a target private allocation, usually modeled with cash flow projections.

concepts.name: Limited partnership agreement
concepts.def: Contract governing a private fund: fees, carry, waterfall, investment limits, key person rules, GP removal and reporting.

concepts.name: Key person clause
concepts.def: LPA provision suspending the investment period if named senior professionals leave or stop devoting sufficient time to the fund.

concepts.name: GP removal provisions
concepts.def: LP rights to remove the GP or end the investment period by supermajority vote, either for cause or without cause.

concepts.name: Distribution waterfall
concepts.def: Order in which fund proceeds are split: return of contributed capital, then the preferred return, then a GP catch-up, then the carried interest split.

concepts.name: European versus American waterfall
concepts.def: A European (whole-fund) waterfall pays carry only after LPs recover all contributions and the preferred return; an American (deal-by-deal) waterfall pays carry per realized deal, earlier and with more clawback risk.
concepts.aliases: european waterfall,american waterfall,deal by deal,whole fund

concepts.name: GP catch-up
concepts.def: Waterfall tier after the preferred return in which the GP receives most or all distributions until it has received its full carry share of total profits.

concepts.name: GP commitment
concepts.def: The GP's own capital invested in its fund, commonly around 1 to 3 percent of commitments, intended to align its interests with LPs.

concepts.name: Management fee offsets
concepts.def: Crediting part or all of portfolio company monitoring and transaction fees against the management fee LPs pay.

concepts.name: Fee step-down
concepts.def: Reduction in the management fee rate or switch of its basis from commitments to invested capital after the investment period ends.

concepts.name: IRR pitfalls
concepts.def: IRR is sensitive to timing, can be lifted by early distributions or subscription lines without more profit, implicitly assumes reinvestment at the IRR, and can have multiple solutions.

concepts.name: Kaplan-Schoar PME
concepts.def: Public market equivalent ratio from Kaplan and Schoar (2005) that discounts fund cash flows by public index returns; above 1 means the fund beat the index.
concepts.formula: KS-PME = PV(distributions + NAV) / PV(contributions), discounted at index returns

concepts.name: Direct alpha
concepts.def: Annualized excess return of a private fund over a public benchmark, computed as the IRR of cash flows compounded forward at index returns.

concepts.name: Quartile ranking
concepts.def: Placing a fund within peer vintage returns; many managers can claim top quartile by picking the metric, benchmark, or vintage definition, so claims need checking.

concepts.name: Manager dispersion
concepts.def: Spread of returns between top and bottom managers, much wider in venture and buyouts than in public equity, making manager selection the dominant decision.

concepts.name: Co-investment
concepts.def: LP investing directly alongside a fund in a specific deal, usually with low or no fees and carry, often offered when the GP needs a larger equity check.

concepts.name: GP stakes
concepts.def: Minority equity stakes in private markets firms, entitling holders to a share of management fees, carry and balance sheet returns.

concepts.name: LP-led secondary
concepts.def: Sale of an LP's interests in one or more funds to a secondary buyer, usually priced at a discount or premium to the latest reported NAV.

concepts.name: GP-led secondary
concepts.def: Transaction organized by the GP, such as a continuation vehicle or tender offer, that lets existing LPs sell or roll their exposure to selected assets.

concepts.name: Secondary pricing to NAV
concepts.def: Secondary trades are quoted as a percentage of the latest reported NAV; discounts reflect stale marks, unfunded obligations, asset quality and sellers' liquidity needs.
concepts.formula: price as % of NAV = purchase price / reported NAV

concepts.name: Private company tender offer
concepts.def: Organized purchase of shares from employees and early investors of a private company, offering liquidity before an IPO or sale.

concepts.name: Private company valuation methods
concepts.def: Private holdings are marked using comparable company multiples, recent transactions, DCF models or option pricing methods, typically calibrated to the last financing round.

concepts.name: OPM backsolve
concepts.def: Option pricing method that infers total equity value from the price of the latest preferred round, allocating value across share classes as call options with different strikes.

concepts.name: 409A valuation
concepts.def: Independent valuation of a private US company's common stock used to set option strike prices without adverse tax consequences; usually below preferred round prices.

concepts.name: Liquidation preference
concepts.def: Right of preferred shareholders to receive a set multiple of their investment before common holders in a sale; participating preferred also shares in what remains.

concepts.name: Anti-dilution protection
concepts.def: Adjustment to preferred stock conversion price after a down round; full ratchet resets to the new price, while broad-based weighted average adjusts only partly.

concepts.name: Pro rata rights
concepts.def: Investor right to buy into future rounds to maintain its ownership percentage, valuable in breakout companies.

concepts.name: SAFE
concepts.def: Simple agreement for future equity, introduced by Y Combinator: an early-stage instrument converting into equity at the next priced round, usually subject to a valuation cap or discount.

concepts.name: Convertible note
concepts.def: Early-stage debt that converts into equity at the next financing round, usually at a discount or capped valuation, accruing interest until conversion.

concepts.name: Pre-money and post-money valuation
concepts.def: Pre-money is a company's value before a new investment; post-money adds the new cash, and the investor's ownership equals the investment divided by post-money.
concepts.formula: post-money = pre-money + new investment; ownership = investment / post-money

concepts.name: Option pool shuffle
concepts.def: Requiring an enlarged option pool inside the pre-money valuation, shifting its dilution entirely onto existing holders and lowering the effective pre-money price.

concepts.name: Capitalization table
concepts.def: Ledger of a company's securities and holders, including preferred classes, options, warrants and convertibles; the basis for any payout analysis.

concepts.name: Venture funding stages
concepts.def: Sequence of pre-seed, seed, Series A, B, C and later rounds, each typically tied to milestones, larger checks and new lead investors.

concepts.name: Bridge round
concepts.def: Interim financing, often from existing investors via notes or an extension, to extend runway until a larger round or exit.

concepts.name: Structured round
concepts.def: Venture round that preserves a headline valuation by giving new investors senior preferences, ratchets or guaranteed returns instead of a lower price.

concepts.name: Venture portfolio construction
concepts.def: Choosing the number of companies, initial check sizes and follow-on reserves so a fund can own meaningful stakes in the rare outliers that drive returns.

concepts.name: Follow-on reserves
concepts.def: Capital held back to invest in later rounds of existing portfolio companies, ideally concentrated in the winners.

concepts.name: Return-the-fund test
concepts.def: Venture heuristic that each initial investment should have a plausible path to returning the entire fund on its own, given power-law outcomes.

concepts.name: Venture debt
concepts.def: Loans to venture-backed startups, usually with warrants, sized against equity already raised rather than against cash flow.

concepts.name: Startup accelerator
concepts.def: Program that gives startups a small investment, mentorship and a demo day in exchange for equity; Y Combinator is the best-known example.

concepts.name: Corporate venture capital
concepts.def: Venture investing by operating companies pursuing both strategic and financial goals, often with different incentives from traditional VCs.

concepts.name: Zombie fund
concepts.def: Fund past its intended life holding residual assets with weak exit prospects while still charging fees, often resolved through secondaries.

concepts.name: Holding period
concepts.def: Time a sponsor owns a portfolio company before exit; longer holds lower IRR for the same multiple of money, which is why IRR and MOIC must be read together.

concepts.name: Dual-track exit
concepts.def: Running an IPO process and a sale process in parallel to increase price tension and certainty of exit.

concepts.name: Strategic versus financial buyers
concepts.def: Strategic acquirers can pay for synergies with their existing businesses; financial buyers price on standalone cash flow and leverage capacity.

concepts.name: Sell-side auction
concepts.def: Banker-run sale with staged non-binding and binding bids designed to maximize price and terms for the seller.

concepts.name: Stapled financing
concepts.def: Pre-arranged debt package offered to bidders by the seller's advisor to speed an auction and set a leverage floor.

concepts.name: Representations and warranties insurance
concepts.def: Policy covering losses from breaches of seller representations in an acquisition, reducing escrow and indemnity needs.

concepts.name: Locked box versus completion accounts
concepts.def: Locked box fixes the price from a historical balance sheet with protection against value leakage; completion accounts adjust the price after closing to actual figures.

concepts.name: Search fund
concepts.def: Vehicle in which an entrepreneur raises capital to find, buy and run one small company, with investors funding the search and holding rights to invest in the deal.

concepts.name: Independent sponsor
concepts.def: Dealmaker without a committed fund who sources a deal and then raises equity deal by deal, earning fees and a promote.

concepts.name: SBA 7(a) loan
concepts.def: US government-guaranteed small business loan program widely used to finance acquisitions of small companies, with personal guarantee and equity injection requirements.

concepts.name: Seller note
concepts.def: Part of a purchase price financed by the seller and usually subordinated to senior debt, keeping the seller invested in a smooth handover.

concepts.name: Seller's discretionary earnings
concepts.def: Small-business earnings measure that adds back one owner's compensation and discretionary expenses to pre-tax profit; used to value owner-operated firms.
concepts.formula: SDE = pre-tax profit + owner compensation + interest + D&A + discretionary expenses

concepts.name: Return unsmoothing
concepts.def: Statistical reversal of appraisal smoothing, such as the Geltner method, to estimate the true volatility and correlation of private asset returns.
concepts.formula: true return r_t = (observed r_t - a x observed r_t-1) / (1 - a)

concepts.name: Return autocorrelation
concepts.def: Correlation of an asset's returns with its own past returns; high positive autocorrelation in reported returns is a sign of smoothed or stale pricing.

concepts.name: Buyout replication
concepts.def: View that much of buyout performance can be matched by leveraged portfolios of small, cheap public stocks, which questions the size of private equity alpha.

concepts.name: Permanent capital
concepts.def: Capital without a redemption or fund-term clock, such as holding companies, insurance float or perpetual vehicles, allowing indefinite holds.

concepts.name: Holding company model
concepts.def: Structure owning controlling stakes in several operating businesses indefinitely and reallocating their cash centrally; Berkshire Hathaway and Constellation Software are well-known examples.

concepts.name: Family office
concepts.def: Private firm managing a wealthy family's capital, often investing directly in companies and real assets with long horizons.

concepts.name: Sovereign wealth fund
concepts.def: State-owned investment fund, often funded by commodity revenue or reserves, investing long-term across public and private assets.

concepts.name: Insurance and private credit
concepts.def: Alternative asset managers owning or partnering with insurers and investing policyholder reserves in private credit to earn a spread over liabilities.

concepts.name: Significant risk transfer
