concepts.def: Large opening gap on an earnings or news release; follow-through in the gap direction is related to post-earnings drift and is the basis of several momentum setups.

concepts.name: Key reversal day
concepts.def: Bar that makes a new high (or low) in the trend direction and then closes beyond the prior close in the opposite direction, hinting at exhaustion.

concepts.name: Inside and outside days
concepts.def: An inside day has its range wholly within the prior bar's range, showing contraction; an outside day engulfs the prior range, showing expansion.

concepts.name: NR7
concepts.def: Toby Crabel's setup flagging the narrowest daily range of the last seven days, on the idea that range contraction precedes range expansion.

concepts.name: Opening range breakout
concepts.def: Intraday strategy entering when price breaks the high or low set in the first minutes of the session, associated with Toby Crabel.

concepts.name: Turtle trading
concepts.def: Rule-based trend system taught by Richard Dennis and William Eckhardt in the 1980s: Donchian channel breakouts, ATR-based position sizing and fixed exits, showing trading could be taught.

concepts.name: Stage analysis
concepts.def: Stan Weinstein's framework that every stock cycles through basing, advancing, topping and declining stages, identified mainly with a 30-week moving average; buy stage 2, avoid stage 4.

concepts.name: Volatility contraction pattern
concepts.def: Mark Minervini's base in which successive pullbacks get shallower and volume dries up, showing supply being absorbed before a breakout.

concepts.name: CAN SLIM
concepts.def: William O'Neil's growth stock method combining strong current and annual earnings, new products or highs, supply and demand, leadership, institutional sponsorship and a confirmed market uptrend.

concepts.name: Follow-through day
concepts.def: O'Neil's signal of a new market uptrend: a strong gain in a major index on higher volume, a few days or more after a rally attempt begins from a low.

concepts.name: Distribution day
concepts.def: Session where a major index falls meaningfully on higher volume than the prior day, read as institutional selling; a cluster of them warns of a top.

concepts.name: Real body
concepts.def: The thick part of a candlestick between the open and the close; filled or red when the close is below the open, hollow or green when above.

concepts.name: Shadow (wick)
concepts.def: Thin lines above and below a candlestick body marking the high and low; long shadows show prices that were rejected during the period.

concepts.name: Candlestick pattern
concepts.def: One- to three-candle formation named in Japanese charting tradition that signals indecision, reversal or continuation; meaningful mainly in context, at trends and levels.

concepts.name: Doji
concepts.def: Candle where open and close are nearly equal, signalling indecision; after a strong trend it can warn of exhaustion.

concepts.name: Dragonfly and gravestone doji
concepts.def: Doji variants: a dragonfly opens and closes at the high after a long lower shadow, showing rejection of lows; a gravestone opens and closes at the low after a long upper shadow, showing rejection of highs.

concepts.name: Hammer and hanging man
concepts.def: Small body near the top of the range with a long lower shadow; called a hammer after a decline (bullish) and a hanging man after an advance (bearish warning).

concepts.name: Shooting star and inverted hammer
concepts.def: Small body near the low of the range with a long upper shadow; a shooting star after an advance is bearish, an inverted hammer after a decline is a possible bottom.

concepts.name: Engulfing pattern
concepts.def: Two-candle reversal where the second body fully covers the first and has the opposite colour; bullish after declines, bearish after advances.

concepts.name: Harami
concepts.def: Two-candle pattern where a small body sits inside the prior large body, signalling a loss of momentum; a harami cross uses a doji as the second candle.

concepts.name: Piercing line and dark cloud cover
concepts.def: Two-candle reversals: a piercing line opens below the prior low and closes above the midpoint of a down candle; dark cloud cover is the bearish mirror.

concepts.name: Morning star and evening star
concepts.def: Three-candle reversals: a large candle, a small-bodied star gapped away from it, then a strong candle in the opposite direction closing well into the first body.

concepts.name: Three white soldiers and three black crows
concepts.def: Three consecutive long candles in the same direction, each closing near its extreme; soldiers signal strong buying after a decline, crows strong selling after an advance.

concepts.name: Candlestick pattern reliability
concepts.def: Studies on liquid US stocks generally find little standalone predictive value in candlestick patterns after costs, while some find modest effects in specific markets; context and confirmation matter more than the shape.

concepts.name: Evidence on technical trading rules
concepts.def: Brock, Lakonishok and LeBaron (1992) found moving average and range breakout rules had predictive power on the Dow, but later work using White's Reality Check showed much of such evidence weakens after correcting for data snooping and costs.
concepts.aliases: do technical rules work,bll 1992,brock lakonishok lebaron

concepts.name: Lo, Mamaysky and Wang (2000)
concepts.def: Paper "Foundations of Technical Analysis" that used kernel regression to detect chart patterns automatically and found several patterns carried incremental information about returns in US stocks.
concepts.aliases: foundations of technical analysis,kernel pattern recognition

concepts.name: Self-fulfilling prophecy (technical)
concepts.def: Argument that widely watched levels and signals work partly because enough traders act on them at the same time; the effect is fragile and fades when it becomes crowded.

concepts.name: Round-number clustering
concepts.def: Tendency of limit orders, stops and price targets to cluster at round numbers, which creates support, resistance and overshoots near them.

concepts.name: Stop hunting
concepts.def: Price pushing briefly through an obvious level where stop orders cluster, triggering them and then reversing; the result of liquidity seeking, whether deliberate or not.

concepts.name: 52-week-high momentum
concepts.def: George and Hwang (2004) found that stocks trading near their 52-week high outperform those far from it, consistent with investors anchoring to that level and underreacting to news.

concepts.name: McClellan oscillator
concepts.def: Breadth momentum indicator by Sherman and Marian McClellan equal to a fast minus a slow exponential average of daily net advances; extremes flag overbought or oversold breadth.
concepts.formula: McClellan = EMA19(advances - declines) - EMA39(advances - declines)

concepts.name: McClellan summation index
concepts.def: Running total of the McClellan oscillator, used as a slower gauge of the breadth trend; its direction and level frame the intermediate market cycle.
concepts.formula: summation_t = summation_t-1 + McClellan_t

concepts.name: Arms index (TRIN)
concepts.def: Richard Arms' ratio of the advance-decline ratio to the up-down volume ratio; values above 1 mean volume is concentrated in falling stocks, and very high readings mark short-term selling extremes.
concepts.formula: TRIN = (advancers / decliners) / (up volume / down volume)

concepts.name: Up/down volume ratio
concepts.def: Volume in advancing issues divided by volume in declining issues; lopsided days such as 9-to-1 up or down are read as signs of thrusts or capitulation.
concepts.formula: ratio = up volume / down volume
concepts.aliases: upside downside volume,90% day,9 to 1 day

concepts.name: New highs minus new lows
concepts.def: Daily count of stocks at 52-week highs less those at 52-week lows; expanding new highs confirm an advance, while a rising index with shrinking highs warns of narrowing participation.
concepts.formula: net = new highs - new lows

concepts.name: Hindenburg omen
concepts.def: Breadth warning attributed to Jim Miekka that fires when unusually many stocks make new highs and new lows at once in a rising market, signalling internal disagreement; it gives many false alarms.

concepts.name: Breadth thrust
concepts.def: Rapid shift from very weak to very strong breadth over a short window; Martin Zweig's version uses a 10-day average of the advancing share of issues and has historically appeared near the start of new bull phases.
concepts.formula: Zweig: EMA10(advances / (advances + declines)) rises from below 0.40 to above 0.615 within 10 days

concepts.name: TICK index
concepts.def: Number of NYSE stocks whose last trade was an uptick minus those on a downtick, updated through the day; extreme readings mark intraday buying or selling programs.
concepts.formula: TICK = upticking issues - downticking issues

concepts.name: Bullish percent index
concepts.def: Share of stocks in an index that are on point and figure buy signals; readings above 70 are considered overbought and below 30 oversold.

concepts.name: Equal-weight versus cap-weight spread
concepts.def: Relative performance of an equal-weight index against its cap-weighted version; when cap-weight leads, gains are concentrated in the largest stocks.

concepts.name: Narrow leadership
concepts.def: Market advance driven by a small number of large stocks while most constituents lag; often cited as a late-cycle warning, though it can persist for long periods.

concepts.name: Sector rotation
concepts.def: Movement of leadership between sectors as the cycle evolves, for example from early-cycle financials and discretionary toward late-cycle energy and defensives; also a strategy that follows it.

concepts.name: Relative rotation graph
concepts.def: Julius de Kempenaer's chart plotting a set of assets by relative strength and its momentum, so they rotate through leading, weakening, lagging and improving quadrants.

concepts.name: Ratio chart
concepts.def: Chart of one price divided by another, such as a stock over its index or copper over gold, used to see relative trend independent of overall market direction.

concepts.name: Relative volume
concepts.def: Current volume divided by typical volume at the same point in the day or over recent sessions; high values show unusual interest that makes moves more meaningful.
concepts.formula: RVOL = volume / average volume

concepts.name: Volume climax
concepts.def: Exceptionally high volume at the end of an extended move, signalling that the last eager buyers or sellers have acted; it often marks an exhaustion point.

concepts.name: Selling climax
concepts.def: Wyckoff term for panic selling on very high volume and wide ranges after a long decline, absorbed by strong hands and followed by an automatic rally.

concepts.name: Buying climax
concepts.def: Wyckoff term for a burst of heavy, eager buying at the top of an advance that is met by professional supply, followed by an automatic reaction lower.

concepts.name: Wyckoff method
concepts.def: Richard Wyckoff's approach to reading supply and demand through price, volume and time, based on laws of supply and demand, cause and effect, and effort versus result.

concepts.name: Wyckoff accumulation
concepts.def: Schematic of a trading range in which large operators absorb supply after a decline, typically including a selling climax, a spring and a sign of strength before markup.

concepts.name: Wyckoff distribution
concepts.def: Schematic of a trading range in which large operators sell into demand after an advance, typically with a buying climax and an upthrust before markdown.

concepts.name: Wyckoff spring
concepts.def: Brief break below trading range support that quickly reverses back inside, shaking out weak holders and testing remaining supply before markup.

concepts.name: Upthrust
concepts.def: Brief push above trading range resistance that fails and returns inside the range, trapping buyers; the distribution counterpart of the spring.

concepts.name: Effort versus result
concepts.def: Wyckoff principle comparing volume (effort) with price movement (result); heavy volume with little progress suggests absorption and a possible turn.

concepts.name: Volume spread analysis
concepts.def: Method developed from Wyckoff by Tom Williams that reads each bar's range, close location and relative volume to infer professional buying or selling.

concepts.name: Cumulative volume delta
concepts.def: Running total of volume traded at the ask minus volume traded at the bid; it shows whether aggressive buyers or sellers dominate and can diverge from price.
concepts.formula: delta = buy-initiated volume - sell-initiated volume

concepts.name: Footprint chart
concepts.def: Order flow chart showing, inside each bar, the volume traded at the bid and at the ask at every price, exposing imbalances and absorption.

concepts.name: Tape reading
concepts.def: Watching the stream of trades and quotes (time and sales) to judge who is aggressive, how size is being worked and whether levels are holding.

concepts.name: Absorption
concepts.def: Large resting orders soaking up aggressive buying or selling so that price stops moving despite heavy volume; often a sign of a hidden large participant.

concepts.name: Unusual options activity
concepts.def: Options volume far above open interest or normal levels in a name, often in short-dated out-of-the-money contracts, watched as a possible sign of informed positioning.

concepts.name: Price, volume and open interest reading
concepts.def: Classic futures rule set: rising price with rising open interest confirms a trend, rising price with falling open interest suggests short covering, and so on.

concepts.name: Lending utilization
concepts.def: Share of lendable supply of a security that is currently on loan; high utilization with rising fees signals crowded shorts and hard-to-borrow conditions.
concepts.formula: utilization = shares on loan / lendable shares

concepts.name: Sentiment survey
concepts.def: Poll of investors or advisors about their market outlook; useful mainly at extremes and as a contrarian input, since stated views and positioning can differ.

concepts.name: Contrarian indicator
concepts.def: Measure of crowd sentiment or positioning used against the crowd: extreme optimism is read as bearish and extreme pessimism as bullish.

concepts.name: Dow theory
concepts.def: Framework built from Charles Dow's editorials and formalized by William Hamilton and Robert Rhea: the market has three trends, primary trends have three phases, and the industrial and transport averages must confirm each other.

concepts.name: Primary trend
concepts.def: In Dow theory, the major bull or bear trend lasting a year or more, within which secondary reactions and minor moves occur.

concepts.name: Secondary reaction
concepts.def: In Dow theory, a counter-trend move within the primary trend lasting weeks to months and typically retracing a third to two-thirds of the prior swing.

concepts.name: Three phases of a Dow trend
concepts.def: Dow theory's stages of a primary trend: accumulation by informed investors, public participation as news improves, and distribution or excess as the crowd piles in.

concepts.name: Dow confirmation and non-confirmation
concepts.def: Dow theory rule that a trend signal requires both the industrial and transport averages to make new highs or lows; when one fails, the divergence is a warning.

concepts.name: Elliott wave principle
concepts.def: R.N. Elliott's theory that crowd psychology moves prices in fractal patterns, five waves with the trend followed by three corrective waves, popularized by Frost and Prechter; labelling is subjective.

concepts.name: Impulse wave
concepts.def: Five-wave move in the direction of the larger trend, labelled 1 to 5, in which waves 1, 3 and 5 advance and waves 2 and 4 correct.

concepts.name: Corrective wave
concepts.def: Counter-trend Elliott pattern labelled A, B, C, taking forms such as zigzags (5-3-5), flats (3-3-5) and triangles (3-3-3-3-3).

concepts.name: Elliott wave rules
concepts.def: Three hard rules for impulses: wave 2 never retraces all of wave 1, wave 3 is never the shortest of waves 1, 3 and 5, and wave 4 does not overlap wave 1's price territory.

concepts.name: Extended wave
concepts.def: An impulse wave, most often wave 3, that is much longer than the others and subdivides visibly into its own five waves.

concepts.name: Diagonal triangle
concepts.def: Wedge-shaped Elliott pattern in which waves overlap; an ending diagonal appears in wave 5 or C and often precedes a sharp reversal.

concepts.name: Fibonacci extensions
concepts.def: Price targets set at Fibonacci multiples of a prior swing projected beyond it, commonly 1.272, 1.618 and 2.618, used for profit targets in trends and Elliott wave counts.
concepts.formula: target = swing end + ratio x swing length

concepts.name: Intermarket analysis
concepts.def: John Murphy's approach of reading stocks, bonds, commodities and currencies together, on the view that their relationships shift through the business cycle.

concepts.name: Copper-gold ratio
concepts.def: Copper price divided by gold price, used as a growth versus safety gauge; it has tended to track long-term Treasury yields.
concepts.formula: ratio = copper price / gold price

concepts.name: Credit leading equities
concepts.def: Observation that high-yield spreads often widen before equity prices fall, because bondholders are more sensitive to default risk; a divergence between them is a warning.

concepts.name: Risk appetite ratios
concepts.def: Ratios of cyclical to defensive assets, such as discretionary to staples, small caps to large caps, or high beta to low volatility, used to read risk-on or risk-off behaviour.
concepts.aliases: risk on risk off,xly xlp,iwm spy,splv sphb

concepts.name: Calendar anomaly
concepts.def: Return pattern tied to the calendar rather than to fundamentals, such as month turns, holidays or weekdays; many are small, unstable and vulnerable to data mining.

concepts.name: January barometer
concepts.def: Saying popularized by the Stock Trader's Almanac that the direction of the S&P 500 in January predicts the full year; the evidence is weak once the market's general upward drift is accounted for.

concepts.name: Santa Claus rally
concepts.def: Tendency, noted by Yale Hirsch, for stocks to rise over the last five trading days of the year and the first two of the next.

concepts.name: Month- and quarter-end rebalancing
concepts.def: Predictable flows as balanced funds, pensions and target-date funds trade back to policy weights after stocks and bonds diverge, watched by desks as a short-term price pressure.

concepts.name: Presidential cycle
concepts.def: Pattern, also from Hirsch, in which US stocks have done better in the third year of a presidential term than in the first two; sample sizes are small.

concepts.name: Day-of-week effect
concepts.def: Historic finding that returns differed by weekday, notably weak Mondays documented by French (1980); much of it has faded in recent decades.

concepts.name: Overnight versus intraday returns
concepts.def: Decomposition of returns into close-to-open and open-to-close; for many US stocks and indexes a large share of long-run gains has accrued overnight.
concepts.formula: overnight = open_t / close_t-1 - 1; intraday = close_t / open_t - 1

concepts.name: Tax-loss selling
concepts.def: Selling of losing positions before the tax year ends to realize capital losses, which depresses prices of recent losers and can lead to a rebound afterwards.

concepts.name: Window dressing
concepts.def: Fund managers buying recent winners and selling losers before reporting dates so holdings look better; it creates small predictable trading pressures near quarter ends.

concepts.name: Options expiration effects
concepts.def: Price behaviour around monthly and quarterly option expiry, including pinning near large open interest strikes and changes in dealer hedging flows afterwards.

concepts.name: EDGAR
concepts.def: The SEC's Electronic Data Gathering, Analysis and Retrieval system where public company, fund and insider filings are submitted and published free of charge.

concepts.name: EDGAR full-text search
concepts.def: SEC tool that searches the text of filings, including exhibits, over recent years; useful for finding mentions of customers, suppliers, risks or terms across all filers.

concepts.name: XBRL and inline XBRL
concepts.def: Tagging standard that labels each financial statement number in a filing with a defined element, making SEC financial data machine-readable; inline XBRL embeds the tags in the human-readable document.

concepts.name: Form 10-Q
concepts.def: Quarterly report for the first three fiscal quarters with unaudited, reviewed financial statements, MD&A and updates to risks; filed 40 or 45 days after quarter end depending on filer size.

concepts.name: Red-flag 8-K items
concepts.def: 8-K items that often signal trouble: 4.01 change of auditor, 4.02 non-reliance on prior financial statements, 5.02 sudden officer departures, and 3.01 delisting notices.

concepts.name: NT 10-K and NT 10-Q
concepts.def: Form 12b-25 notice that a company cannot file its periodic report on time; late filings frequently precede restatements, control failures or negative news.

concepts.name: Executive pay analysis
concepts.def: Reading the proxy to see which metrics drive management bonuses and equity awards, since pay design shapes behaviour, for example EPS targets encouraging buybacks or adjusted metrics.

concepts.name: Risk factors (Item 1A)
concepts.def: Section of SEC filings listing material risks to the business; mostly boilerplate, so the useful signal is in additions, deletions and wording changes between filings.

concepts.name: Critical accounting estimates
concepts.def: Disclosure of the judgments with the largest effect on reported results, such as reserves, impairments and revenue estimates, and how sensitive results are to them.

concepts.name: Financial statement footnotes
concepts.def: Notes to the financial statements that detail accounting policies, debt terms, leases, contingencies, segments and related parties; often where the real risks and adjustments are found.

concepts.name: Auditor's report
concepts.def: The independent auditor's opinion on whether financial statements fairly present the company's position under the applicable framework; qualified or adverse opinions are rare and serious.

concepts.name: SEC comment letters
concepts.def: Correspondence in which SEC staff question a company's disclosures and the company responds; published on EDGAR after reviews close, they reveal where regulators see weak accounting.

concepts.name: Schedule 13G
concepts.def: Short-form beneficial ownership report for holders above 5 percent who are passive or qualified institutions; switching from 13G to 13D signals a change toward activism.

concepts.name: Form S-1
concepts.def: Registration statement for an IPO or other registered offering by companies that cannot use short forms, containing the prospectus, financials, risk factors and use of proceeds.

concepts.name: Form S-3 and shelf registration
concepts.def: Short-form registration available to seasoned issuers that lets them register securities in advance and sell them from the shelf over time, enabling fast follow-ons and at-the-market programs.

concepts.name: Form 20-F and 6-K
concepts.def: Annual report (20-F) and current reports (6-K) filed by foreign private issuers; less frequent and less detailed interim reporting than US domestic filers.

concepts.name: Form 144
concepts.def: Notice filed by affiliates intending to sell restricted or control securities under Rule 144; a leading indicator of insider selling before the trade itself is reported.

concepts.name: Form D
concepts.def: Notice filed after an exempt private offering under Regulation D, giving the amount raised and investor types; used to track private fundraising by companies and funds.

concepts.name: Form N-PORT
concepts.def: Monthly portfolio holdings report filed by registered funds, with quarter-end data made public after a lag; more detailed than 13F, covering bonds and derivatives.

concepts.name: Textual analysis of disclosures
concepts.def: Using dictionaries or language models to score tone, uncertainty and readability in filings and calls; Loughran and McDonald (2011) showed general dictionaries misclassify many finance words.

concepts.name: Earnings release
concepts.def: Press release reporting quarterly results, usually with GAAP and non-GAAP figures and guidance, furnished to the SEC on Form 8-K under Item 2.02, often shortly before the call.

concepts.name: Earnings guidance
concepts.def: Management's forecast of future revenue, earnings or other metrics; changes in guidance often move stocks more than the reported quarter.

concepts.name: Whisper number
concepts.def: Unofficial expectation for earnings circulating among traders that differs from published consensus; beating consensus but missing the whisper can still disappoint.

concepts.name: Beat and raise
concepts.def: Quarter in which a company beats consensus and raises guidance, usually the best reaction case; a beat without a raise can disappoint when expectations already price in more.

concepts.name: Sandbagging guidance
concepts.def: Management setting guidance low enough to beat it reliably; investors learn the pattern and adjust expectations, so the beat itself carries less information.

concepts.name: Expectations walk-down
concepts.def: Pattern in which analyst estimates start optimistic and drift down toward a level the company can beat by reporting day, documented by Richardson, Teoh and Wysocki.

concepts.name: Kitchen-sink quarter
concepts.def: Quarter in which management, often new, takes every possible charge and write-down at once to reset the base and make later results look better.

concepts.name: Earnings pre-announcement
concepts.def: Company disclosing results or a guidance change ahead of the scheduled release, more often for negative news to avoid a surprise.

concepts.name: Earnings quiet period
concepts.def: Weeks before results when companies limit communication with investors and analysts to avoid selective disclosure of the quarter's results.

concepts.name: Earnings calendar
concepts.def: Schedule of expected earnings release dates; confirmed dates come from company announcements, and a late or changed date can itself carry information.

concepts.name: Implied earnings move
concepts.def: Price move the options market prices for an earnings release, approximated by the at-the-money straddle for the nearest expiry divided by the stock price.
concepts.formula: implied move = ATM straddle price / stock price

concepts.name: Estimate dispersion
concepts.def: Spread of analyst forecasts for the same metric; high dispersion signals uncertainty, and Diether, Malloy and Scherbina (2002) found high-dispersion stocks subsequently underperform.
concepts.formula: dispersion = std dev of estimates / abs(mean estimate)

concepts.name: Read-across
concepts.def: Inferring news about one company from results or comments of a peer, supplier or customer; markets often move peers on an early reporter's numbers.

concepts.name: Management credibility tracking
concepts.def: Recording management's past guidance, targets and claims against outcomes to calibrate how much weight to give new statements.

concepts.name: Economic calendar
concepts.def: Schedule of upcoming data releases, central bank meetings and auctions with release times and consensus forecasts; essential for knowing when event risk is concentrated.

concepts.name: Statistical release process
concepts.def: How official data are produced and published: fixed schedules announced in advance, strict pre-release access rules, and release at set times so all users get data at once.

concepts.name: Real-time data vintages
concepts.def: Archive of what each statistic showed on each past date before revisions, such as ALFRED, needed so backtests use only information known at the time.

concepts.name: Economists' consensus forecast
concepts.def: Median of surveyed economist forecasts for a data release; markets react to the surprise against this number rather than to the level.
concepts.formula: surprise = actual - consensus median

concepts.name: Fed blackout period
concepts.def: Period around each FOMC meeting during which Fed officials refrain from public comment on policy, so markets get no new signals before the decision.

concepts.name: Initiation of coverage
concepts.def: First published report by an analyst on a company, usually a long piece with model, thesis, rating and target; initiations after IPO quiet periods often skew positive.

concepts.name: Analyst rating
concepts.def: Recommendation such as buy, hold or sell, or overweight and underweight relative to a coverage group; buy ratings far outnumber sells, so downgrades carry more information.

concepts.name: Price target
concepts.def: Analyst's projected price, usually over twelve months, derived from multiples or DCF; targets tend to follow price rather than lead it and are on average optimistic.

concepts.name: Rating change effect
concepts.def: Stock price reaction to analyst upgrades and downgrades; Womack (1996) found significant drift after changes, larger after downgrades.

concepts.name: Analyst optimism bias
concepts.def: Systematic upward bias in analyst forecasts and ratings, linked to investment banking ties and the need for management access; it is larger for long-horizon forecasts.

concepts.name: Analyst herding
concepts.def: Tendency of analysts to keep forecasts near consensus to limit career risk; it compresses dispersion and delays the incorporation of new information.

concepts.name: Global Research Analyst Settlement
concepts.def: 2003 settlement between regulators and major banks over research conflicts, requiring separation of research from investment banking and funding of independent research.

concepts.name: FINRA Rule 2241
concepts.def: FINRA rule on equity research conflicts, restricting investment banking influence over analysts, requiring disclosures and setting quiet periods around offerings.

concepts.name: MiFID II research unbundling
concepts.def: European rules that required asset managers to pay for research separately from trading commissions, which cut research budgets and analyst coverage of smaller companies; later partly relaxed.

concepts.name: Soft dollars
concepts.def: Paying for research and services with trading commissions rather than direct fees, permitted in the US within Section 28(e) limits; criticized for hiding costs from clients.

concepts.name: Corporate access
concepts.def: Broker-arranged meetings between investors and company management at conferences, roadshows and site visits; a large part of what institutions pay brokers for.

concepts.name: Non-deal roadshow
concepts.def: Management visiting investors without an offering attached, to explain strategy; Reg FD forbids sharing material nonpublic information in these meetings.

concepts.name: Activist investor
concepts.def: Investor who buys a stake and pushes management for changes such as asset sales, buybacks or board seats, often signalled by a 13D filing.

concepts.name: Supply chain checks
concepts.def: Tracking component orders, supplier commentary and production schedules to infer a company's volumes, such as supplier capacity bookings ahead of a product launch.

concepts.name: Primary research
concepts.def: Original information gathered directly by the investor, through surveys, interviews, site visits or data collection, rather than read from published sources.

concepts.name: Expert call compliance
concepts.def: Controls on expert network use: screening out current employees with confidential duties, pre-call disclaimers, chaperones and logs, to avoid receiving MNPI.

concepts.name: Web-scraped data
concepts.def: Data collected from websites, such as prices, inventory counts, reviews or job listings; terms of service, legal limits and site changes create compliance and continuity risk.

concepts.name: Credit card panel data
concepts.def: Aggregated, anonymized transaction data from card or bank account panels used to estimate company sales before reporting; panel composition biases must be corrected.

concepts.name: Satellite and geolocation data
concepts.def: Imagery of parking lots, oil tanks, ships or crops, and phone location data on store visits, used to estimate activity at assets and retailers.

concepts.name: Foot traffic data
concepts.def: Counts of visits to physical locations estimated from phone location panels, used for retailers, restaurants and real estate; panel changes can create false trends.

concepts.name: Strategic news timing
concepts.def: Companies releasing bad news when attention is low, such as Friday evenings or busy days; DellaVigna and Pollet (2009) found weaker immediate reactions to Friday announcements.

concepts.name: Limited attention
concepts.def: Investors can process only so much information, so news released when attention is scarce is incorporated slowly, contributing to drifts and underreaction.

concepts.name: Regulation FD
concepts.def: SEC rule adopted in 2000 requiring issuers that disclose material nonpublic information to analysts or investors to disclose it publicly at the same time, or promptly if unintentional.

concepts.name: Selective disclosure
concepts.def: Giving material information to some investors or analysts before the public; prohibited for issuers by Reg FD and a historic source of sell-side edge.

concepts.name: Mosaic theory
concepts.def: Doctrine that an analyst may combine public and non-material nonpublic information into a conclusion that would itself be material, without violating insider trading law.

concepts.name: Insider trading law (US)
concepts.def: Mostly judge-made doctrine under Rule 10b-5: liability requires trading on MNPI in breach of a duty, under the classical theory for insiders or the misappropriation theory for outsiders.

concepts.name: Rule 10b-5
concepts.def: SEC anti-fraud rule under the Exchange Act prohibiting material misstatements, omissions and deceptive practices in connection with buying or selling securities.

concepts.name: Misappropriation theory
concepts.def: Insider trading theory, upheld in United States v. O'Hagan (1997), that an outsider who trades on confidential information taken in breach of a duty to its source commits fraud.

concepts.name: Tipper and tippee liability
concepts.def: Rule from Dirks v. SEC (1983) that a person who receives a tip is liable if the insider breached a duty for personal benefit and the tippee knew or should have known.

concepts.name: Shadow trading
concepts.def: Trading a different but economically linked company's securities using MNPI about one's own employer; SEC v. Panuwat applied the misappropriation theory to it.

concepts.name: Insider blackout window
concepts.def: Company policy barring insiders from trading in the weeks before earnings until shortly after release, to reduce the risk of trading on MNPI.

concepts.name: Section 16(b) short-swing rule
concepts.def: Exchange Act provision requiring officers, directors and 10 percent holders to give the company any profit from buying and selling its stock within six months, regardless of intent.

concepts.name: Information barrier
concepts.def: Policies and physical or system separation that keep MNPI held by one part of a firm, such as banking, away from trading and research.

concepts.name: Restricted and watch lists
concepts.def: Compliance lists of securities in which a firm limits trading or research because it may hold MNPI; the watch list is confidential, the restricted list is broadly communicated.

concepts.name: Wall-crossing
concepts.def: Bringing an investor over the wall by sharing confidential information, such as a pending offering, with consent; the investor is then restricted until the information is cleansed.

concepts.name: Expectations gap
concepts.def: Difference between what the price implies about future fundamentals and what the investor expects; the source of return when the gap closes.

concepts.name: Priced in
concepts.def: Claim that known information is already reflected in the price; testing it requires estimating what expectations the price implies, not assuming them.

concepts.name: Decision journal
concepts.def: Record written at the time of each decision of the reasoning, expectations, confidence and emotional state, so later reviews can separate skill from luck.

concepts.name: Investment memo
concepts.def: Written case for a position covering thesis, valuation, risks, catalysts and sizing, reviewed by others before capital is committed.

concepts.name: Bear case and steelmanning
concepts.def: Writing the strongest version of the opposing argument and the downside scenario before committing, to counter confirmation bias.

concepts.name: Red team review
concepts.def: Assigning someone to attack a thesis or model as an adversary would, to find weaknesses the author cannot see.

concepts.name: Source triangulation
concepts.def: Confirming a fact with independent sources that do not share the same origin; three reports from one original source are one source.

concepts.name: Information half-life
concepts.def: How fast the value of a piece of information decays as it spreads into prices, from milliseconds for headlines to months for slow-moving fundamentals.

concepts.name: Idea generation
concepts.def: Process for finding candidate investments, such as screens, new highs and lows, spin-offs, insider buying, conferences and peer reads; sources shape which biases enter the pipeline.

concepts.name: Stock screen
concepts.def: Filter applied to a universe on quantitative criteria such as valuation, quality or momentum to narrow research candidates; point-in-time data are needed to backtest screens honestly.

concepts.name: Sample selection bias in research data
concepts.def: When the panel, survey or alt-data sample differs systematically from the population of interest, such as card users skewing young, so naive extrapolation misestimates the total.

concepts.name: Pump and dump
concepts.def: Manipulation in which promoters hype a thinly traded security with misleading claims, then sell into the buying they create.

concepts.name: Cornering a market
concepts.def: Gaining control of enough supply of a security or commodity, often alongside large long derivatives positions, to dictate prices to shorts who must deliver or cover.

concepts.name: Securities and Exchange Commission
concepts.def: US federal agency that regulates securities markets, issuers, broker-dealers, exchanges, investment advisers and funds, with a mission of investor protection, fair and orderly markets and capital formation.

concepts.name: FINRA
concepts.def: Self-regulatory organization overseen by the SEC that writes and enforces rules for US broker-dealers, licenses registered representatives and runs market surveillance.

concepts.name: Commodity Futures Trading Commission
concepts.def: US agency regulating futures, options on futures and most swaps, including exchanges, clearing houses and intermediaries, under the Commodity Exchange Act.

concepts.name: Self-regulatory organization
concepts.def: Industry body given authority to set and enforce rules for its members under government oversight, such as exchanges, FINRA and the NFA.

concepts.name: Securities Act of 1933
concepts.def: US law requiring registration and full disclosure for public offerings of securities, with liability for misstatements in registration statements, unless an exemption applies.

concepts.name: Securities Exchange Act of 1934
concepts.def: US law that created the SEC and governs secondary trading, exchanges, broker-dealers, periodic reporting, proxy solicitation and anti-fraud rules.

concepts.name: Investment Company Act of 1940
concepts.def: US law regulating mutual funds, ETFs and other registered investment companies, covering disclosure, leverage limits, custody, governance and conflicts.

concepts.name: Investment Advisers Act of 1940
concepts.def: US law requiring registration of investment advisers and imposing a fiduciary duty of care and loyalty toward clients.

concepts.name: Sarbanes-Oxley Act
concepts.def: 2002 US law passed after Enron and WorldCom that requires CEO and CFO certification of financial reports, internal control assessments and created the PCAOB to oversee auditors.

concepts.name: Internal control over financial reporting
concepts.def: Processes that give reasonable assurance financial statements are reliable; a material weakness disclosure signals higher risk of misstatement.

concepts.name: Dodd-Frank Act
concepts.def: 2010 US financial reform law that moved most swaps to clearing and reporting, created the CFPB and FSOC, imposed the Volcker Rule and expanded systemic risk oversight.

concepts.name: Volcker Rule
concepts.def: Dodd-Frank provision limiting proprietary trading by banks and their investments in hedge funds and private equity funds, with exemptions for market making and hedging.

concepts.name: JOBS Act
concepts.def: 2012 US law easing capital raising, including confidential IPO filings and lighter disclosure for emerging growth companies, general solicitation in some private offerings, and crowdfunding.

concepts.name: Order protection rule (Rule 611)
concepts.def: Reg NMS rule requiring trading centers to prevent trade-throughs of protected, automatically accessible quotes at better prices on other venues.

concepts.name: Access fee cap (Rule 610)
concepts.def: Reg NMS limit on the fee a venue may charge to execute against its displayed quotes, which shapes the economics of maker-taker pricing.

concepts.name: Sub-penny rule (Rule 612)
concepts.def: Reg NMS rule setting minimum quoting increments for stocks, historically one cent for prices of a dollar or more, which also determines queue and spread dynamics.

concepts.name: Locate requirement
concepts.def: Under Reg SHO, a broker must have reasonable grounds to believe shares can be borrowed for delivery before accepting a short sale.

concepts.name: Threshold securities list
concepts.def: Reg SHO list of securities with large, persistent fails to deliver, published daily, triggering mandatory close-out requirements.

concepts.name: Alternative uptick rule (Rule 201)
concepts.def: SEC circuit breaker that, after a stock falls 10 percent in a day, allows short sales only above the national best bid for the rest of that day and the next.

concepts.name: Regulation ATS
concepts.def: SEC framework under which alternative trading systems, including dark pools, operate as broker-dealers rather than exchanges, with Form ATS-N disclosures for NMS stock ATSs.

concepts.name: Regulation SCI
concepts.def: SEC rule requiring exchanges, clearing agencies and large ATSs to keep systems capacity, integrity and resilience, test them and report outages.

concepts.name: Market access rule (Rule 15c3-5)
concepts.def: SEC rule requiring brokers that provide market access to have pre-trade risk controls, such as credit and fat-finger limits, so no client trades unfiltered.

concepts.name: Net capital rule (15c3-1)
concepts.def: SEC rule requiring broker-dealers to hold minimum liquid net capital, after haircuts on securities positions, so they can wind down without harming customers.

concepts.name: Regulation T
concepts.def: Federal Reserve rule governing credit brokers may extend for securities purchases, setting initial margin for stocks at 50 percent of purchase value.

concepts.name: Stock exchange
concepts.def: Regulated venue where buyers and sellers trade listed securities under published rules, providing price discovery, listings, auctions and market data.

concepts.name: Maker-taker pricing
concepts.def: Exchange fee model that pays rebates to orders adding liquidity and charges fees to orders removing it; inverted venues do the reverse.

concepts.name: Consolidated audit trail
concepts.def: SEC-mandated database tracking the full lifecycle of orders across US equity and options markets for surveillance; its cost and privacy terms have been contested.

concepts.name: Listing standards
concepts.def: Exchange requirements to list and stay listed, such as minimum price, market value, shareholders and governance; breaches lead to deficiency notices and possible delisting.

concepts.name: Delisting
concepts.def: Removal of a security from an exchange, voluntarily or for failing standards; it usually cuts liquidity and many holders must sell, and delisting returns must be in backtests.

concepts.name: American depositary receipt
concepts.def: US-traded certificate representing shares of a foreign company held by a depositary bank; prices track local shares via conversion arbitrage, with FX and fees added.

concepts.name: Rule 144
concepts.def: SEC safe harbour for public resale of restricted and control securities, with holding periods, volume limits for affiliates and Form 144 notice.

concepts.name: Rule 144A
concepts.def: SEC rule allowing resale of privately placed securities to qualified institutional buyers, creating a large institutional market for high-yield and other bonds without registration.

concepts.name: Regulation D
concepts.def: SEC exemptions for private offerings, chiefly Rule 506, allowing unlimited capital raises from accredited investors without registration; 506(c) permits general solicitation if buyers are verified.

concepts.name: IPO lockup
concepts.def: Agreement barring insiders and pre-IPO holders from selling for a period after an IPO, commonly 180 days; expirations can weigh on prices as supply arrives.

concepts.name: IPO quiet period
concepts.def: Restrictions on issuer communications during registration and on research by underwriting banks for a period after an IPO.

concepts.name: Multilateral netting
concepts.def: Offsetting each member's trades against all others through the clearing house so only net obligations settle, sharply reducing the securities and cash that must move.

concepts.name: Clearing member
concepts.def: Firm admitted to a clearing house that clears its own and clients' trades, posts margin and contributes to the default fund.

concepts.name: Clearing house concentration risk
concepts.def: Concern that central clearing concentrates systemic risk in a few CCPs, whose failure or procyclical margin calls could spread stress.
concepts.aliases: too big to fail ccp,ccp risk

concepts.name: Procyclical margin
concepts.def: Margin and haircut models that raise requirements when volatility rises, forcing collateral calls and selling at the worst time and amplifying stress.

concepts.name: DTCC
concepts.def: Depository Trust and Clearing Corporation, the US post-trade utility that owns NSCC, DTC and FICC, clearing and settling most US securities trades.

concepts.name: NSCC
concepts.def: National Securities Clearing Corporation, DTCC's CCP for US equities and corporate bonds, which nets trades through continuous net settlement and requires member margin.

concepts.name: DTC
concepts.def: Depository Trust Company, the US central securities depository that holds securities in book-entry form and settles transfers between participants.

concepts.name: FICC
concepts.def: Fixed Income Clearing Corporation, DTCC's clearing house for US Treasuries, agency securities and repo, central to Treasury clearing reform.

concepts.name: Delivery versus payment
concepts.def: Settlement method that transfers securities only if the matching cash payment is made at the same time, removing principal risk.

concepts.name: Custodian bank
concepts.def: Bank that holds and safekeeps assets for funds and institutions, settles their trades, collects income and handles corporate actions.

concepts.name: Treasury clearing mandate
concepts.def: SEC rule requiring most cash Treasury and Treasury repo trades by direct participants to be centrally cleared, phased in over several years.

concepts.name: Index provider
concepts.def: Firm that designs, calculates and licenses benchmarks, such as S&P Dow Jones Indices, MSCI and FTSE Russell; its rules decide which stocks passive money must buy.

concepts.name: Index methodology
concepts.def: Published rules for an index: eligibility, weighting, float adjustment, caps, rebalancing schedule and treatment of corporate actions.

concepts.name: Free float adjustment
concepts.def: Weighting index constituents by shares available to public investors, excluding strategic, government and insider holdings.
concepts.formula: float mcap = price x shares outstanding x float factor

concepts.name: Equal-weight index
concepts.def: Index giving every constituent the same weight at rebalance, tilting toward smaller stocks and requiring regular trading back to equal weights.

concepts.name: Price-weighted index
concepts.def: Index weighting stocks by share price, as the Dow Jones Industrial Average does, so a high-priced stock moves it more regardless of company size.
concepts.formula: DJIA = sum of prices / Dow divisor

concepts.name: S&P 500 eligibility rules
concepts.def: S&P criteria for addition, including US domicile, size, liquidity, float and positive GAAP earnings in the latest quarter and the sum of the last four, with a committee making final choices.

concepts.name: Russell reconstitution
concepts.def: Periodic rebuilding of the Russell US indexes by market cap ranking on a rank day, historically annual in June, generating some of the heaviest closing auction volume of the year.

concepts.name: MSCI index reviews
concepts.def: MSCI's quarterly and semi-annual reviews that add, delete and reweight constituents, plus annual market classification reviews that can move a country between categories.

concepts.name: Market classification
concepts.def: Index providers' grouping of countries into developed, emerging and frontier based on economic development, size and market accessibility; reclassification shifts large passive flows.

concepts.name: Index inclusion effect
concepts.def: Price rise of stocks added to major indexes from announcement to inclusion, documented by Shleifer (1986) and Harris and Gurel (1986); evidence suggests it has shrunk as it became anticipated.

concepts.name: Pre-positioning index changes
concepts.def: Traders buying expected additions and selling deletions ahead of index funds, earning the price pressure that funds pay; it raises passive investors' hidden costs.

concepts.name: Index capping rules
concepts.def: Limits on single-stock or group weights in an index, often to meet fund diversification rules; caps force selling of the largest names at rebalances.

concepts.name: GICS
concepts.def: Global Industry Classification Standard developed by MSCI and S&P, which assigns companies to sectors, industry groups, industries and sub-industries; reclassifications shift sector fund holdings.

concepts.name: Program trading
concepts.def: Trading a basket of many stocks at once, for index arbitrage, portfolio transitions or rebalancing; historically defined by NYSE as baskets of fifteen or more stocks.

concepts.name: Model risk management
concepts.def: Framework of policies, inventory, tiering, validation, monitoring and governance that controls losses from model errors or misuse across an organization.

concepts.name: Model inventory
concepts.def: Complete register of models in use, with owners, purpose, inputs, dependencies, risk tier and validation status; missing models are unmanaged risk.

concepts.name: Model tiering
concepts.def: Ranking models by materiality, complexity and uncertainty to set the depth and frequency of validation and monitoring.

concepts.name: Conceptual soundness
concepts.def: Validation step assessing whether a model's theory, design, assumptions and data are appropriate for its purpose, judged against literature and industry practice.

concepts.name: Outcomes analysis
concepts.def: Comparing model outputs with actual outcomes, including backtesting, to judge accuracy and detect deterioration.

concepts.name: Ongoing model monitoring
concepts.def: Periodic checks that a model still performs as validated, tracking input drift, output stability, overrides and errors against thresholds that trigger review.

concepts.name: Benchmark and challenger models
concepts.def: Alternative models built to compare against a production model; large disagreements flag specification or implementation problems.

concepts.name: Model limitations
concepts.def: Documented conditions where a model is unreliable, such as untested regimes, extrapolated inputs or simplified mechanics; users must know them to avoid misuse.

concepts.name: Model misuse
concepts.def: Applying a model outside the purpose, population or range it was built and validated for, a major source of model risk even when the model itself is sound.

concepts.name: Model documentation
concepts.def: Written description of a model's purpose, theory, data, assumptions, limitations, testing and change history, detailed enough for an independent party to understand and reproduce it.

concepts.name: Model change control
concepts.def: Process requiring versioning, testing and approval of model changes before production, so silent edits do not alter results.

concepts.name: Model overlay
concepts.def: Judgemental adjustment applied to model output to cover known weaknesses or unusual conditions; it should be documented, justified and tracked for performance.

concepts.name: Model interdependency
concepts.def: Outputs of one model feeding another, so an error propagates and compounds; aggregate model risk can exceed the sum of individual model risks.

concepts.name: Aggregate model risk
concepts.def: Risk from many models sharing data, assumptions or vendors, so they fail together; SR 11-7 asks firms to consider it across the portfolio of models.

concepts.name: Data quality risk
concepts.def: Errors, gaps, staleness or bias in model inputs that corrupt outputs regardless of model quality; garbage in, garbage out.

concepts.name: Spreadsheet risk
concepts.def: Errors from manual, untested spreadsheet models, such as wrong ranges or copy-paste mistakes; audits have repeatedly found errors in a large share of operational spreadsheets.

concepts.name: Implementation risk
concepts.def: Gap between the model as designed and the model as coded or deployed, from bugs, unit errors, wrong data mappings or deployment mistakes.

concepts.name: Independent code review
concepts.def: Second person checking model code for errors, hidden look-ahead and divergence from documentation; finds implementation bugs that output testing can miss.

concepts.name: Parameter uncertainty
concepts.def: Error in model outputs from estimating parameters with finite, noisy data; ignoring it makes forecasts and optimized portfolios look more precise than they are.

concepts.name: Parameter stability
concepts.def: Whether estimated coefficients stay similar across subperiods and samples; unstable parameters suggest overfitting or structural change.

concepts.name: Specification error
concepts.def: Error from choosing the wrong functional form, omitting relevant variables or including irrelevant ones, so estimates are biased whatever the sample size.

concepts.name: Model uncertainty
concepts.def: Uncertainty about which model is correct, beyond parameter error within a model; often larger than parameter uncertainty and ignored when one model is chosen.

concepts.name: Knightian uncertainty
concepts.def: Frank Knight's distinction between risk, where probabilities are known, and uncertainty, where they cannot be meaningfully assigned; models handle the first and fail silently on the second.

concepts.name: Model averaging
concepts.def: Combining predictions from several models weighted by evidence or performance, as in Bayesian model averaging, to hedge model uncertainty.

concepts.name: Stressing a model
concepts.def: Feeding a model extreme, boundary and inconsistent inputs to see where outputs become unstable, unrealistic or break, rather than only stressing the portfolio it values.

concepts.name: Boundary testing
concepts.def: Checking model behaviour at the edges of its input range, such as zero or negative rates, zero volatility or empty data, where hidden assumptions fail.

concepts.name: P&L attribution test
concepts.def: FRTB requirement comparing risk-model P&L with front-office P&L for each trading desk; desks failing it lose internal model approval.

concepts.name: Mark-to-model
concepts.def: Valuing positions with a model when no reliable market price exists; the inputs and assumptions are unobservable, so valuations can drift from realizable prices.

concepts.name: Fair value hierarchy (Level 1, 2, 3)
concepts.def: Accounting classification of fair value inputs: Level 1 quoted prices, Level 2 observable inputs, Level 3 unobservable model inputs; Level 3 valuations carry the most model risk.

concepts.name: Model valuation adjustment
concepts.def: Reserve deducted from model-based valuations to reflect model uncertainty or known limitations, so reported values are prudent.

concepts.name: Population stability index
concepts.def: Measure of how much a variable's distribution has shifted between a reference sample and current data, used to monitor input drift in credit and other models.
concepts.formula: PSI = sum((actual% - expected%) x ln(actual% / expected%))

concepts.name: Shadow deployment
concepts.def: Running a new model in production on live inputs without acting on its outputs, to compare it with expectations before it controls capital.

concepts.name: Drawdown-based strategy review
concepts.def: Rules that cut risk or trigger review when a strategy's drawdown exceeds what its backtest says is plausible, separating bad luck from a broken model.

concepts.name: Backtest protocol
concepts.def: Rules fixed before testing: hypothesis, universe, data, costs, sample splits, metrics and the number of variants allowed, to limit researcher degrees of freedom.

concepts.name: Pre-registration
concepts.def: Recording a hypothesis and test plan before seeing the results, so findings cannot be reframed after the fact.

concepts.name: Trial log
concepts.def: Record of every backtest variant tried, including failures, needed to count trials for deflated Sharpe ratios and multiple testing corrections.

concepts.name: Holdout discipline
concepts.def: Keeping a final test sample untouched until the model is fixed and using it once; every peek turns it into training data.

concepts.name: HARKing
concepts.def: Hypothesizing after the results are known: presenting a post hoc finding as if it had been predicted, which hides how many alternatives were explored.

concepts.name: Delisting return bias
concepts.def: Overstated backtest returns from dropping stocks when they delist without recording the often large final loss; Shumway (1997) showed missing delisting returns bias results.

concepts.name: Corporate action adjustment
concepts.def: Adjusting historical prices and volumes for splits, dividends, spin-offs and mergers; wrong adjustments create false signals and returns in backtests.

concepts.name: Transaction cost assumptions
concepts.def: Backtests that assume zero or fixed costs overstate returns, especially for high-turnover and small-cap strategies; costs should scale with size, volatility and liquidity.

concepts.name: Lucas critique
concepts.def: Robert Lucas's (1976) argument that relationships estimated under one policy regime break when policy changes, because agents change behaviour; models must be structural to survive policy shifts.

concepts.name: Goodhart's law
concepts.def: When a measure becomes a target it ceases to be a good measure, because people optimize the measure instead of the goal; applies to KPIs, risk limits and model metrics.

concepts.name: Model performativity
concepts.def: When a widely used model changes the market it describes, as portfolio insurance did in 1987 or common risk models do when many funds sell together.

concepts.name: All models are wrong
concepts.def: George Box's maxim that all models are wrong but some are useful; the question is whether a model is wrong in ways that matter for its use.
concepts.aliases: box maxim,essentially all models are wrong

concepts.name: Gaussian assumption failure
concepts.def: Models assuming normally distributed returns understate the frequency of large moves; many crisis losses followed from treating fat-tailed outcomes as near impossible.

concepts.name: Liquidity assumption failure
concepts.def: Models assuming positions can be sold at marked prices within a fixed horizon break when liquidity vanishes and forced sellers move prices.

concepts.name: Gaussian copula and CDOs
concepts.def: David Li's (2000) Gaussian copula let banks and rating agencies price CDO tranches with a single correlation input; it understated joint default risk in housing and contributed to the 2008 losses.

concepts.name: Rating agency model failures
concepts.def: Before 2008, structured finance rating models assumed modest correlation of mortgage defaults and relied on short histories of rising house prices, so many AAA tranches were later downgraded.

concepts.name: London Whale (2012)
concepts.def: JPMorgan trading losses in a large synthetic credit portfolio; investigations found a new VaR model with spreadsheet errors that understated risk, alongside weak oversight.

concepts.name: Reinhart-Rogoff spreadsheet error
concepts.def: Herndon, Ash and Pollin (2013) found coding errors and exclusions in an influential spreadsheet linking high public debt to lower growth, a cautionary case about unreviewed analysis.
concepts.aliases: reinhart rogoff,growth in a time of debt

concepts.name: Metallgesellschaft (1993)
concepts.def: Oil marketing unit hedged long-dated fixed-price supply contracts with rolled short-dated futures; contango and margin calls created funding losses, showing hedge models must include liquidity.

concepts.name: Negative rate model breaks
concepts.def: Interest rate models and systems that assumed rates could not fall below zero, such as lognormal models, failed when rates went negative, forcing shifts to normal or shifted models.

concepts.name: Volatility smile and Black-Scholes
concepts.def: Black-Scholes assumes constant volatility and lognormal prices; the observed smile and skew, steepest after 1987, show the market rejects that assumption and prices crash risk.

concepts.name: DSGE model limitations
concepts.def: Macro models widely used by central banks before 2008 largely lacked a financial sector and so offered little warning of the crisis; later versions added financial frictions.

concepts.name: Matrix multiplication
concepts.def: Combining two grids of numbers so each output entry is a weighted sum of a row of the first against a column of the second. A neural network's layer, a graph walk and a portfolio's return across scenarios are all matrix products, which is why GPUs, built to do many of them at once, run AI.
concepts.formula: C_ij = sum_k A_ik B_kj

concepts.name: Parallel prefix scan
concepts.def: Computing every running total (or running product) of a sequence in about log2 of its length rounds by combining partial results that double in span each round, possible whenever the operation is associative. Matrix products are, so a step-by-step recursion such as a filter can be run as a scan of matrix multiplications.
concepts.formula: P_t = M_1 M_2 ... M_t for every t, in log2(T) rounds

concepts.name: Personalized PageRank
concepts.def: A random walk on a graph that restarts at chosen seed nodes with a fixed probability each step; how often it visits each node ranks the nodes by their connection to the seeds. Each step is one sparse matrix-vector product, and many seed sets can be walked at once as one matrix product.
concepts.formula: r = (1 - a) s + a P r

concepts.name: Proof of useful work
concepts.def: A blockchain consensus design in which the computation miners must do to add blocks is itself useful, such as the matrix multiplications of AI inference, instead of hashing done only to secure the chain. Its claims rest on cheap verification of the work and on whether the useful output finds paying buyers.

concepts.name: Riemannian geometry
concepts.def: The geometry of curved spaces, where distance is measured along the space itself rather than in a straight line through it. Covariance matrices live on such a space: an average of two of them computed entry by entry can describe a risk structure neither had.

concepts.name: Affine-invariant distance
concepts.def: A distance between two covariance matrices, the norm of the logarithm of A^-1/2 B A^-1/2, that does not change when every asset is rescaled or the assets are mixed. It compares the shape of risk rather than its units, so a quiet era and a loud era with the same structure sit close together only if their structure matches.

concepts.name: Log-Euclidean distance
concepts.def: A distance between covariance matrices taken after mapping each through the matrix logarithm, which flattens the curved space so ordinary averages and distances apply. Cheaper than the affine-invariant distance and close to it when the matrices are near each other.
concepts.formula: d(A,B) = || log A - log B ||_F

concepts.name: Frechet mean
concepts.def: The point that minimizes the average squared distance to a set of points in a curved space: the right notion of an average where adding and dividing do not apply. The typical risk structure of an era is the Frechet mean of its covariance matrices.

concepts.name: Multidimensional scaling
concepts.def: A way to draw points on a page so their distances match a table of distances as closely as possible. Classical scaling takes the top eigenvectors of the double-centred squared distances; the share of the structure each axis carries says how faithful the drawing is.

concepts.name: Persistent homology
concepts.def: Topological data analysis: grow a ball around every point and record when connected pieces merge (H0) and when loops appear and fill in (H1). Features that persist across many scales are structure; ones that flicker are noise. Applied to the correlation distances between markets, it measures how tangled their co-movement is.

concepts.name: Vietoris-Rips complex
concepts.def: The shape built from points by joining every pair closer than a scale r and filling every triangle whose three sides are all joined. Raising r from 0 traces a filtration whose changes persistent homology records.

concepts.name: Minimum spanning tree
concepts.def: The cheapest set of links that connects every point. In a correlation network it keeps each market's closest relation and shows the backbone of co-movement; its edge lengths are exactly when the pieces of the Rips filtration merge.

concepts.name: Optimal transport
concepts.def: The cheapest way to move one distribution of mass into another. Its cost, the Wasserstein distance, compares whole distributions, tails included, where mean and variance compare only two numbers.

concepts.name: Wasserstein distance
concepts.def: The optimal-transport cost between two distributions. In one dimension it is the average gap between their sorted samples; in several, the sliced version averages one-dimensional distances over random directions.
concepts.formula: W1 = mean | sort(x) - sort(y) |

concepts.name: Sliced Wasserstein distance
concepts.def: The Wasserstein distance between multivariate samples estimated by projecting both onto many random directions, sorting, and averaging the one-dimensional distances: transport between distributions in several dimensions at the price of a sort.

concepts.name: Bures distance
concepts.def: The 2-Wasserstein distance between two normal distributions, which has a closed form in their means and covariances. It is how far apart two regimes are as whole distributions.

concepts.name: Path signature
concepts.def: The sequence of iterated integrals that summarizes a path: its increments, then the areas it sweeps, then higher terms. Signatures turn a time series into features that capture order of events, not only their sizes.

concepts.name: Levy area
concepts.def: The signed area between a two-dimensional path and the straight chord joining its ends, the second level of the path signature. For cumulative stock and bond returns it is positive when stock moves tend to come before bond moves.
concepts.formula: A = 1/2 integral (x dy - y dx)

concepts.name: Detrended fluctuation analysis
concepts.def: A way to estimate long memory: integrate the series, remove a line in boxes of each size, and see how the leftover wiggle grows with box size. The slope is the Hurst exponent, about 0.5 for a random walk's steps.
concepts.formula: F(n) ~ n^H

concepts.name: Analog forecasting
concepts.def: Predicting by finding the past moments that looked most like today and reading what followed them. It is the market historian's oldest tool; tested honestly, with a placebo of randomly chosen moments, its edge usually comes from averaging several pasts rather than from the resemblance.

concepts.name: Nearest neighbours
concepts.def: A rule that predicts from the k past cases closest to the present by some distance. Its quality depends almost entirely on whether the distance measures what matters.

concepts.name: Benjamini-Hochberg procedure
concepts.def: A correction for testing many claims at once that controls the false-discovery rate: the expected share of claims called significant that are flukes. Sort the p-values and keep those under their rank times the target over the number of tests.
concepts.formula: p_(k) <= k q / m

concepts.name: Mixture of normals
concepts.def: A distribution built by drawing from one of several normal distributions with given weights. Mixing normals of different widths fattens the tails and sharpens the peak, which is how real monthly returns look.
concepts.formula: f(x) = sum w_k N(x; mu_k, s_k)
